reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Difficult to find parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Somewhat recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,400–1,600, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Loud, but you can still talk, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Parking_is_unavailable, E:PARKING_OPTION_NO_PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=1+ hour, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION]}, time_line=a month ago, review=Had heard of the place so thought would try. I didn’t know about the 6:30 pm guest list time and no prior / call bookings which was unique and I was sure I can walk in. LOL.
It’s a small diner with limited seating. The hero is definitely an open pasta cooking kitchen but the shaky bar stools, overstaffed and uncleaned glasses made the place smaller than it was.
The two girls outside- Aradhya and S were sweet and genuine.
I waited for an hour to get the table but the rush was justified, the seating not so much.
The stools are wooden , unstable and extremely uncomfortable.
Coming to the food:
Lasagna Verde- a must order. It was a very different take on the Lasagna which I loved, the sauces were amazing and simply loved it.
The Truffle Chitara was a usual truffle which can rarely go wrong.
On the contrary I didn’t quite enjoy The Pomodoro- very soupy, spicy and lacked lustre. The pasta was overpowered with the tomato passata.

I am very particular about my Tiramisu especially in an Italian restaurant and while it was good, I won’t say the best I have ever tried.

We paid- 2850₹ for two which was quite good in my opinion., name_person=Sanjoli Malani}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Free_street_parking, E:PARKING_OPTION_FREE_STREET_PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Somewhat difficult to find parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=10-30 min}, time_line=4 weeks ago, review=Visiting Pomodoro in Bandra, Mumbai was such an unexpected and memorable experience, especially coming from New Jersey, where I’m used to a very different style of Italian-inspired food. Despite the name, Pomodoro isn’t your typical pizza-and-pasta spot—what they do offer is a creative, flavorful blend of Italian inspiration with a distinctly Indian twist that makes the restaurant stand out.

The first thing I noticed was the warm, cozy vibe of the place. It has a modern feel without being overwhelming, and the service was welcoming from the moment I walked in. The staff took time to explain the menu, which helped a lot because many of the dishes were familiar in concept but had unique Indian spice profiles woven in. It’s the kind of fusion that doesn’t feel forced; instead, it feels like the chef truly understands both cuisines and knows how to bring them together beautifully.

I tried a couple of their signature dishes, and each one had layers of flavor you don’t typically find in Western Italian food. The sauces had richer aromatics, and the spices added depth without overpowering the dish. It felt like Italian comfort food reimagined through a Mumbai lens. The appetizers had great texture and seasoning, and the mains were hearty, balanced, and satisfying. Even the drinks menu had a thoughtful mix of refreshing options that paired well with the bolder flavors.

What really impressed me was how Pomodoro manages to stay true to its inspiration while still embracing local ingredients and flavor traditions. It’s not trying to imitate American or classic Italian food—it’s creating something new, rooted in Mumbai’s own culinary identity. As someone who travels often and tries restaurants wherever I go, this felt like one of those rare finds that you can’t compare directly to anything else.

Overall, Pomodoro is absolutely worth a visit if you’re in Bandra and want a dining experience that feels familiar yet completely original. Whether you’re from NJ like me, or a local seeking something different, this place has a charm—and a flavor profile—that stays with you long after you leave., name_person=Shakeel}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Loud, but you can still talk, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=10-30 min}, time_line=a month ago, review=Finally checked this one off from the plethora of cafés and restaurants in my list for Bombay. Started with the Elder & Verde, slightly on the sweeter side for my liking but still refreshing and worth trying to accompany all the food. The tricolour antipasti was a killer, bursting (tomatoes,  quite literally) with flavour and umami. The truffle chittara was a classic, buttery dish which I would order again. Also, as a pesto lover I had to try their spaghetti. This one was pretty salty for me and could have been toned down a bit. But flavour wise still good. The classic tiramisu and pistachio gelato were both definitely worth ordering again. While the tiramisu was a contrast of strong yet sweet, the gelato was a good accompaniment to that with its rich and creamy texture. All in all, I would definitely give Pomodoro a try again to savour other dishes on the menu., name_person=Ranveer Chhibber}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Indoor_dining_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_INDOOR_DINING_AREA], GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=Up to 10 min, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Clearly_labeled_vegetarian_dishes, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_CLEARLY_LABELED_ITEMS]}, time_line=a month ago, review=The Food Was amazing.. Amongst the best in its class in Mumbai.  The Truffle fries had the most perfect and delicate taste.  The Lasagna was crafted in house and served with freshly made in house sauces and just the right dash of seasoning.  A must visit for Pasta lovers. This is now an all time favorite on my list, name_person=Manoj Wanvari}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,000–1,200, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=1+ hour}, time_line=a month ago, review=The food was great. Umuul was exceptional w her recommendations and quick service, name_person=Tanavi Datta}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Brunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,600–1,800, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Moderate noise, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Dietary_restrictions, E:OTHER_DIETARY_RESTRICTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING, Kid-friendliness, E:KID_FRIENDLINESS, Wheelchair_accessibility, E:ACCESSIBILITY], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Somewhat difficult to find parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Clearly_labeled_vegetarian_dishes, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_CLEARLY_LABELED_ITEMS]}, time_line=2 months ago, review=This is my honest review. I visited pomodoro on weekday exactly at 12pm and there was no line so thats a plus point i ordered two pasta's the classic pomodoro and Fettuccini in pesto sauce both of them were very delicious absolutely worth the money. Yea ik its a bit overpriced but i would def visit again. But their coffee is very okayish i had house cold coffee but it had more of vanilla flavour rather than coffee. I spent 1700 for three things and i dined alone, yes portion sizes are very small can barely feed one. Overall 3.5/5, name_person=Riya satra}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Indoor_dining_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_INDOOR_DINING_AREA], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=Up to 10 min}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=Stumbled upon this place, and found out it was hype. Decided to walk in, found out we had a 10 minute wait. The server was kind enough to find us a table even though they were close to closing time, so big ups to her, thank you.

Coming to the food, definitely not the best, but it's great if you need something greasy and are looking for a hangover cure.

We ordered the orzetto parmigiani, which was a little to buttery for me (actually very heavy on the butter, practically drowning), but again, if you're looking for greasy, this is it.

The chicken parm, was nice, but not mind blowing.

And then the tiramisu, I'm not big on desserts, but again, this didn't make me rethink my life choices.

So, all in all, pretty average. No complains. I've heard people waiting ridiculously long for tables here, but if it were me I'd pass., name_person=Travis Saldanha}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Somewhat recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,400–1,600, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Moderate noise, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Difficult to find parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=30-60 min, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION]}, time_line=2 months ago, review=We visited Pomodoro recently and ordered the Red White Green, Truffle Fungi Tortellini, The Pomodoro, and house cold coffee. This is the overall decision made by each member (5members). We went to the restaurant for lunch as it was newly opened. Talking about ambience, it has no such great nor a bad in observation. It has both AC & Non-Ac section. Here the problem starts, there were multiple files flying around our plates. The restaurant was empty, yet the service was soooo slow and least interested staff. We have to call them everytime just to serve water. That was very annoying. Talking about food, we ordered paneer malai tikka which was good, shahi paneer which was just creamy. I don’t know who suggested the chef to make white creamy shahi paneer. Very strange. Veg handi which was more of just veggies and less gravy. Roti, Naan & daal khichadi. Again the staff forget to serve pappad with khichadi. Coming to taste, zero salt in shahi paneer & veg handi. Very less spices in both dishes. Naan & rotis were good. Finally daal khichadi tasted good and decent. We were not at all happy with the service to be very honest. One common question was what if the restaurant gets completely packed how will they provide service? Disappointing service. Also there is no parking space for car owners. Bikers just be aware. The main part comes here, the quantity. It serves just for 2. Daal khichadi was enough for 3-4 person. TBH, except daal khichadi nothing felt really good in terms of taste wise and quantity wise. I hope restaurant owners should make an improvement as they have just started as there is scope of improvement., name_person=Amit Jadhav}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=5 months ago, review=Food taste and quality was very good. The gravy around it was good enough. It was not too spicy. For the main course we ordered Tri paneer which was basically a combination off 3 dishes that was pretty good as well. Also ordered some rotis to have with the main course. Later we ordered paneer tikka sizzler which was to my surprise that they added a mini Naan. The quantity of the rice was less. Mojito

["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=2 months ago, review=On a warm afternoon the taste of the hour was a craving for fish and we thought of dropping in at Isvara. It's not crowded and with plenty of seating available we chose to be seated in the cool interiors. There are cocktails prepared with malvani ingredients like Kokum, bottled beer, meads and other alcohol. The menu has an array of various malavani preparations of fish. The fish is fresh and the curry delicious however the service was a bit slow. It's priced pretty steep as well., name_person=Pink Ribbon}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=10-30 min}, time_line=5 months ago, review=A Hidden Gem for Konkani Food Lovers!

The atmosphere at The Konkani Haven – Isvara Restaurant is truly something special — calm, serene, and perfect for a relaxed meal. The ambiance sets the tone with soothing music, tasteful decor, and a peaceful vibe that immediately makes you feel at home.

The food is the real star here — authentic Konkani flavors that are hard to find elsewhere. Every dish we tried was fresh, flavorful, and clearly made with care. The seafood options, in particular, were outstanding!

Service was warm and attentive without being intrusive. You can tell the staff genuinely care about your dining experience.

Highly recommend for anyone looking to enjoy great food in a tranquil setting. Will definitely be coming back!, name_person=Dr Arvind Yadav}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,200–1,400, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[2_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=4 weeks ago, review=Lovely ambience and spacious setting, but the food was average. The egg curry was tasty yet served in a very small portion, and the chapati was too hard and seemed machine-made, which made it quite dry., name_person=Sailee Kalyankar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3}, time_line=a year ago, review=I visited this place on a national holiday so obviously the place was not that busy given it was a holiday and a dry day.

The food was good but not wow. I definitely would recommend to try the Konkani style shrimps. We also tried a lot of other fish items which were also good. If you like spicy food you definitely need to try the Prawns thecha which was super spicy.

The service is very slow given that it was not crowded at all. We had to wait quite a long time for even things like Fresh Lime sodas...

So we had done pre bookings through Zomato through their Carnival offer for this outing. We were surprised when the restaurant informed us that the Zomato offer excludes all lamb related products and they will make a seperate bill for that. This was a bit new for me but yes it is what it is., name_person=Stephen Fernandes}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3}, time_line=a year ago, review=The most recommended to try here is the prawns ambotik , mutton kalimiri and the wade. Their most instagrammble dish , the thecha prawns is too hot (🔥🔥🔥🔥) to handle!
We also had the stuffed pomfret which was a misnomer because it was actually patrani maach... nevertheless it was fresh so no complaints there...
What was disappointing was their bombil fry and their mandeli fry.... unfortunately what they served us was charred bombil...not at all expected from a seafood speciality restaurant.
Their solkadi is good...but I think u should go for their innovative cocktails...we had the Aampanna gimlet which was refreshing!
We had been to the restaurant in the afternoon and there was only one person who took care of everything...maybe noone goes there in the afternoon...so I would advise go there only for dinner when u would b able to enjoy the ambience as well cause without the lighting...the place is not worth spending ur time in.
I wouldn't say value for money....expensive. our bill went to 2500 per person
Can go once though..cause the seafood is fresh and the masalas they prepare in are different and tasteful.
For dessert we had the doodhi halwa which was very very good, name_person=Dr Amrapali Keny - Pawar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=11 months ago, review=It's a great and quite place. The food is delicious. Some goan music. Perfect place for family dinner. Ambience is good. The prices are bit on upper side but the food is really delicious so can't argue much. You can also go with friends. Tasted Veg and Non-veg food, both are great, so doesn't matter if you're friends are vegetarian. Service is bit slow, but when you taste the food, it's worth the wait. Maybe they prepare it freshly according to the order and requirements. Overall a great place for Goan and kokani food lovers., name_person=Kalpesh Chawande}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,200–1,400, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=11 months ago, review=Prawn rawa fry 😍
Absolute winner 🏆 all around. The malvan curry, the pomfret tawa fry, the kokum soup, everything is fresh, without fuss and delivers on taste. Highly recommended!!, name_person=Saloni Chandra}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Gavane, Surmai_Rava_Fry, Prawns_Thecha, Kolambi_Bhaat], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Somewhat difficult to find parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Would not recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,800–2,000, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Free_street_parking, E:PARKING_OPTION_FREE_STREET_PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Clearly_labeled_vegetarian_dishes, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_CLEARLY_LABELED_ITEMS]}, time_line=a year ago, review=An absolute must-visit for seafood lovers! The prawns thecha was perfectly spiced. The bharlela pomfret, stuffed and grilled to perfection.

Service was excellent, and the atmosphere had a cozy coastal charm. A top-notch dining experience—don’t miss it!

They also have a good choice of cocktails to go with the bold flavors of the dishes, perfectly complementing the prawns thecha and bharlelea pomfret for a balanced and refreshing experience., name_person=jeyson barboza}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Service is bit slow, but when you taste the food, it's worth the wait.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Chicken sagoti was absolutely delicious, and the staff was incredibly attentive.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Bringing ordered food to table & not serving it.}"]

reviews: ["{\"name_person\":\"aakruti dave\",\"time_line\":\"Edited a month ago\",\"review\":\"If you're looking for a cool place to unwind after office hours, this bar & restaurant right beside the Lower Oshiwara metro station is a fantastic choice. reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner}, time_line=4 months ago, review=We recently dined at The Fern, Powai, and were impressed by their vibrant food festival. The buffet featured a delightful mix of traditional and modern Indian dishes.

The vegetarian starters were fantastic, especially the smoky Pahadi Paneer Tikka and Golden Fried Babycorn. For the main course, we enjoyed the rich Shahi Gulab Paneer and flavorful Rajan Masala, along with the must-try Kachori Chaat.

Desserts like Shahi Tukda and Kala Jamun, paired with refreshing mocktails, were also highlights. The service was impeccable, with Manager Yogesh and his team ensuring we felt well cared for.

Overall, The Fern’s food festival offers a delightful culinary experience. Highly recommended for Indian food lovers!, name_person=Tulipragi}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=5 months ago, review=Tiara is a wonderful spot to unwind with family. The atmosphere is calm and welcoming, perfect for a relaxed meal together. Whether you go for the à la carte menu or the well-curated buffet spread, you’re in for a treat — both offer a good balance of variety and flavour.

What really stood out, though, was the service — warm, attentive, and genuinely thoughtful. It’s the kind of place where you feel well taken care of without being rushed., name_person=Meenal Adhia}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Plenty of parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION]}, time_line=6 months ago, review=Our fabulous dinner at Tiara - Meluha The Fern, Powai, Mumbai is a fabulous experience.

Tiara is celebrating Hills of India Food Festival - a lavish buffet spread of cuisine of Hilly regions of India.

Valet parking facility available
Number of covers - 80
The buffet time 12:30 pm to 3:30 pm and 7.30 pm - 11 pm

Tiara is a buffet restaurant, popular for good food and excellent service.

The fresh fruit juices are refreshing.

Loved the hill cuisine specialties -
Nilgiri chicken,
Munnar egg biryani,
Tenderloin Shaptak (Water buffalo),
Grilled fish in orange sauce,
Mooli ki jholi,
Mooli kanda,
Kewa Datshi and many more delicious dishes.

Soups, veg and non-veg starters are fabulous, along with various types of veg and non-veg salad.

Desserts are delicious, must try the regional specialities.

A satisfying dining experience at Tiara. A not so hidden gem in Powai. A must visit for all buffet lovers, name_person=Aspy Engineer}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,600–1,800, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Paneer_Tikka], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a year ago, review=Tucked away in the bustling streets of Powai, Tiara - The Meluha Fern is a hidden gem that promises to tantalize your taste buds with its all-day dining experience. Our recent visit was a testament to the restaurant's commitment to serving ultimate culinary delights.

We began our meal with the Manchow soup, available in both vegetarian and non-vegetarian options. The flavorful broth, teeming with vegetables and tender chicken, set the tone for a delightful culinary journey. The Hawker's Chicken Wings, crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside, were a treat for the taste buds. The Bhoonadar Paneer Tikka, marinated to perfection, melted in our mouths, leaving us craving for more.

The Steamed Rice with Nalli Nihari was a masterclass in comfort food. The tender lamb shanks, slow-cooked in a rich and aromatic gravy, paired perfectly with the fluffy steamed rice.

The pièce de résistance was the dessert course. The Key Lime Pie, with its tangy and sweet filling, was a refreshing delight. However, the Pistachio Raspberry Delight stole the show, with its unique combination of flavors and textures. The crunch of the pistachios complemented the sweetness of the raspberries, creating a truly unforgettable experience.

Tiara - The Meluha Fern is a must-visit destination for foodies and those seeking a memorable dining experience. With its diverse menu, impeccable service, and cozy ambiance, this restaurant is sure to leave you craving for more. Be sure to try their signature dishes and desserts, and don't forget to make a reservation to avoid missing out on this culinary delight., name_person=Fizza Ratlamwala}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=10-30 min}, time_line=3 weeks ago, review=They call it a five Stars but the place has flies all over. Extremely disappointed I had gone there for my parents anniversary the service was unbelievable slow and the staff was clueless. The food on its own is okay they have some good options but the service quality totally kills the expirince.

Would not recommend this place to anyone there is serious issue with staff shortage or training. The food options are limited and because of the service delays you won't even get to taste half of the starters. ["{guided_block={}, time_line=2 months ago, review=Kanishka Veg Restaurant is a prominent pure vegetarian eatery situated in Mumbai, strategically located near iconic landmarks like the Mahalakshmi Temple and Haji Ali Dargah, making it a convenient dining spot for visitors exploring these spiritual sites. Nestled at 5-B, Haji Ali Circle, Tardeo Road, Mahalaxmi, the restaurant offers an inviting ambiance conducive for family dinners and casual meals alike.¹

Kanishka Veg Restaurant serves an array of delectable vegetarian dishes catering to diverse palates. *Authentic South Indian dishes* like _Sada Dosa_ and _Rava Masala Dosa_ are highlights, delivering *typical South Indian taste* that's true to regional flavors, complemented by flavorful chutneys that enhance the culinary experience. Patrons praise the *tasty dosa*, underscoring the restaurant's knack for capturing traditional essence.² ³

The restaurant boasts a *good atmosphere*, with interiors that are well-furnished and equipped with pleasant lighting, fostering a comfortable dining environment. Reviews highlight *good service*, with staff often described as attentive, friendly, and polite – essential for patrons seeking hassle-free dining, even during bustling festival periods like Diwali and Raksha Bandhan.⁴

Among popular items, diners specifically love *paneer tikka*, *kulcha*, *cheese pulav*, and *fried rice*, showcasing the kitchen's versatility across North Indian and Chinese-inspired vegetarian preparations. *Pav Bhaji* is another crowd-pleaser, available with options like Jain Pav Bhaji, reflecting accommodation for diverse dietary preferences.

On the beverage front, while the *chocolate shake is average*, visitors appreciate refreshing options like lassi – with one reviewer finding the lassi "definitely worth trying – refreshing and delicious!".

Kanishka Veg Restaurant offers a balanced mix of affordability and quality, with price ranges typically ₹200-₹400 per person, making it accessible for varied budgets. Cuisines span *South Indian*, *North Indian*, *Chinese*, *Fast Food*, and vegetarian staples, appealing to those craving familiar comfort food with vegetarian integrity.

Located opposite Haji Ali Juice Centre, proximity to spiritual hubs like Mahalakshmi Temple (0.3 km from Baskin-Robbins, another nearby eatery) and Haji Ali Dargah positions Kanishka Veg Restaurant as a practical choice for visitors blending devotion with gastronomy. Other nearby dining options include Cafe Noorani, McDonald’s Tardeo, and Haji Ali Juice Centre for those exploring alternatives.⁵

reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 months ago, review=A school friend sent me a reel about Poe and Pao in Chembur. I decided to go chasing Poe and Pao. Since I was already in Bandra, I thought I’d try their Matunga outlet instead.

Now, if you’re a true-blue Mumbaikar, you know traffic jams aren’t an inconvenience, they’re a lifestyle. So there I was, stuck in the middle of one, wishing for a restroom more than anything else.

When I finally reached, they said, “Go next door.” I stumbled into Dakshin Culture Curry and found the cleanest restroom in Mumbai. Small, but spotless. You can’t do pranayama there, but you’ll definitely come out feeling zen.

Feeling human again, I stepped out… and somehow found myself in Diva Maharashtracha. For a moment, I thought I’d taken a wrong turn in life. That’s when someone explained that Dakshin Culture Curry, Goa Portuguesa, and Diva Maharashtracha are a trilogy, same team, shared menu, different cuisines. And Poe and Pao? The latest addition to the family.

One look at the menu, and I knew there was no way I was walking back to Poe and Pao.

I started with a Sushegad Shot (feni, lime, and kaffir leaves) -  Goa in a glass. Then came the Khekade Kalimiri Soup, a crab-and-black-pepper combo that doubles as a natural sinus reliever. After that, Ravas Moile, Tender Coconut Cashew Nut Sukke (their signature dish), Chicken Modak, and Appam n Amboli.

The Chicken Modak was the surprise star—moist chicken kheema wrapped in a soft, pillowy coating. Though, between us, it did look slightly jaundiced.

They ended the meal with complimentary Caramel Custard—light, soft, and just the right sweetness.

The staff were courteous and attentive, the ambience warm and welcoming.

What we ordered:
In Starters 🍢
🔸Fish Fry Porichaphu 🐟❤️
This was a very tempting dish. Pomphret which was nicely marinated was served in red masala and fried. It had a nice tangy sweet taste. The covering was crisp with hint of spices and the sauce served along was tangy sweet. A must try!

🔹Spice Rubbed Rawas ❤️💯
Rawas fish marinated with spices and yogurt and nicely grilled. The flavors were soaked in the fish. The dish was so well prepared that all I wanted to eat was this yummy Rawas. My new favorite.

In Cocktails 🍹
🔸Cosmopolitan 🍸❤️💯

🔹Mango Margarita 🍹❤️
This was tangy sweet due to the mango flavor but again a yummy boozy drink. Well served with sugar coated at the rim. It was an eye candy.

In Mains 🍛
🔸Prawns Manglorean Sukkha 🍤❤️💯
This was a delight. If you want something light to go with your breads then this is it. This was so flavorful and tasty. Hint of all the spices nicely marinated in prawns. The prawns were in good number and juicy.

🔹Chicken Chettinad 🍲❤️❤️💯
This was the best Chicken Chettinad. Spicy and tasty, with so many flavors. I could eat it everyday. Just like homemade gravies but much more flavors and spices. Too yum. A must must try here.

🔸Malabar Paratha
It was served hot and crisp. Went really well with Chettinad gravy and the chicken pieces.

🔹Appam ❤️
They've a special counter to make appams. And my mum loved it to the core that through out the meal she had more of appams. Beautifully made and served steaming hot.

🔸Neer Dosa
Soft and light. Non sticky and thin slices. The beauty of neer dosa. Just perfect.

In Desserts 🍦
🔹Shahi Tukda ❤️
Fried bread stuffed with rabdi. The rabdi was so so good. Specially made by the chef. It was full of rich milky flavors.

🔸Watalappam 🍮❤️💯
Similar to our beloved custard but a famous South Indian dessert made from Coco and jaggery. Only if you taste it then only you can understand what I'm saying. It was so soft and tasty. Loved it!

Chang’s at Lower Parel is one of those places you walk into with a certain set of expectations — especially for dinner. Big space, familiar menu, and that promise of bold Asian flavours. Our visit was mostly enjoyable, but a few things definitely held it back from being a great meal.

Let’s start with the biggest issue of the night — temperature. A surprising number of dishes arrived almost cold. Not “could be hotter” warm, but genuinely needing to be sent back. We had to request reheating more than once, which took away from the flow of the meal. For a restaurant of this scale and reputation, that was disappointing and honestly shouldn’t happen.

Drinks came first. The Samurai Fizz (2.5/5) was… fine. Refreshing, yes, but pretty forgettable. It didn’t really stand out in flavour. On the other hand, the Passionfruit Iced Tea (4.5/5) was excellent — well-balanced, refreshing, and easily the best drink we ordered.

Soups were a letdown. Both the Hot & Sour Soup (2/5) and Chang’s Noodle Soup (2/5) lacked depth and warmth — in flavour and temperature. They felt rushed and flat, which is a shame because these are usually comforting starters.

Things picked up once the appetisers started rolling in. The Shrimp Tempura Roll (4/5) was nicely done — crispy shrimp, clean flavours, and well-balanced textures. The Pan Fried Handmade Shrimp Dumplings (2/5), however, were underwhelming. Soft, yes, but bland and missing that punch you expect from dumplings.

Vegetarian dishes did surprisingly well. The Kung Pao Potatoes (4/5) were addictive — crispy, spicy, and full of flavour. Easily one of the better plates on the table.

Among the chicken dishes, both the Orange Chicken (4/5) and Dynamite Chicken (4/5) delivered what you expect — crispy, saucy, and comforting. No complaints there. But the real star of the night was the Ring of Fire Shrimp (5/5). Perfectly crispy, bold flavours, and just the right amount of heat. This dish alone made the wait and reheating worth it.

The Mongolian Tenderloin (3/5) was a mixed experience. The meat was beautifully tender, cooked just right, but the flavour was surprisingly bland. It needed more sauce or seasoning to really shine.

For sides, the Hong Kong Egg Fried Rice (4/5) was simple and satisfying, and the Chicken in Black Bean (4/5) was solid — comforting, flavourful, and reliable.

Desserts wrapped things up nicely. The Great Wall of Chocolate (4/5) was rich and indulgent without being too heavy, while the Banana Spring Roll (4/5) was crisp, warm, and a crowd-pleaser.

Where P.F. Chang’s really scored was service. The staff was extremely friendly, attentive, and handled the reheating requests politely and efficiently. They genuinely tried to make the experience better, which made a big difference. The atmosphere was pleasant — lively but not chaotic — making it a comfortable place for a dinner outing.

Overall, P.F. Chang’s Lower Parel had some strong dishes and excellent service, but the repeated issue of food being served cold brought the overall experience down. If they can fix that one major flaw, it would easily be a much better dining spot. reviews:
["{guided_block={}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=We recently visited Yazu, Andheri, and it completely impressed us with its amazing Pan-Asian experience. The ambience is subtle yet classy, with dim lights and soothing vibes — a perfect spot for a relaxed dinner with friends or loved ones.

For drinks, we tried the Mock Penzi and Strawberry & Orange Mojito. Both were beautifully presented with a slightly sweet note — refreshing and perfect to kickstart the meal.

Coming to the starters, the Yazu Signature Chicken was an absolute treat — a perfect balance of sweet and spicy, topped with cashews and onions for that added crunch. Next, we tried the Pan-fried Chicken Shanghai Dimsums, which were flavourful and well-cooked. The Manchow Soup was comforting, rich in taste, and just perfect for the winter season.

The highlight of the evening was definitely the Crispy Prawns Cheng Fung — a must-try dish here! For mains, we opted for the Burnt Garlic Fried Rice, which had subtle yet delicious flavours and paired well with the rest of the spread.

We wrapped up our meal with the Pick Me Up Tiramisu Cake, which was decadent and delightful — a perfect ending to a perfect meal.

Special mention to Mr. Suraj for suggesting some amazing dishes and enhancing our overall dining experience.
Yazu is a must-visit place for all Asian food lovers! Highly recommended. 🌟, name_person=priyanka shikhare}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=Yazu brings a refreshing Pan-Asian twist to the Unlimited Buffet Brunch scene in Andheri. The ambience is warm, stylish and perfect for a relaxed yet indulgent Sunday outing. 🥂🍜

The brunch menu offers a well-curated variety of Asian favourites—enough to tempt every palate without feeling overwhelming. You get comforting soups like Manchow & Tibetan Thenthuk, flavour-packed salads, a delicious range of dimsums such as Truffle Edamame, Cream Cheese & Sriracha Chicken Dumplings, along with assorted sushi rolls and wok starters including Spicy Cottage Cheese, Signature Chicken & Black Pepper Fish.

The main course keeps it soulful with classics like Thai Green Curry, Black Bean Chicken, Fish in Chilli Basil, Veg Fried Rice, Hakka Noodles & more. The best part? You can savour it all as part of the unlimited brunch — making it value-for-money if you love exploring multiple flavours in one meal.

A great pick for a premium yet comforting Sunday brunch with friends or family — good food, soothing ambience and a menu that truly celebrates Pan-Asian cuisine. 🌿✨, name_person=Purva Sangade}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=Tucked away right behind Infinity Mall in Lokhandwala, Andheri West, Yazu The Pan Asian Supper Club is truly a paradise for Asian cuisine enthusiasts. The location is excellent, and the restaurant itself boasts a large, well-stocked bar and a calming yet well-lit ambiance. Offering both comfortable indoor and outdoor seating, Yazu sets a sophisticated stage for a memorable meal.

We kicked off our evening with a selection of inventive cocktails. The Orange Cinnamon was an immediate winner; the classic pairing of cinnamon with whiskey never fails to impress. For something different, the Sakura Chan was a strong yet beautifully balanced cocktail, blending sake, gin, lemon, and kaffir for a delightful sweet kick.

The small plates menu offered some absolute treasures. The Yazu Signature Spicy Lamb was a testament to the chef's skill—slow-cooked to tender perfection, the meat was incredibly flavorful and a fantastic choice. The Prawn Tempura Roll was equally fabulous, proving that Yazu excels at classic Japanese favorites.

We also sampled the delightful Pan Fried Chicken Shanghai Dimsums, which were as good as imagined, perfectly complemented by the spicy Shanghai sauce. The Crispy Chicken Cheung Fun, a traditional Cantonese rice noodle roll, was a pleasant surprise, with the crispy chicken adding an excellent textural element.

For the mains, the Chicken Donburi with Veggies was a wonderfully comforting and flavorful bowl. The combination of chicken, teriyaki sauce, and fresh veggies served over Japanese sticky rice was a harmonious blend that we absolutely loved.

To conclude our feast, the Blueberry Cheesecake delivered a stellar performance. It was a fantastic execution of a classic dessert—mesmerizingly good.

Overall, Yazu clearly invests heavily in ensuring a high-quality experience for every patron. From the strong cocktails to the perfectly executed Pan Asian dishes, we had a truly great time and highly recommend Yazu for a sophisticated dining experience.

The variety on offer was impressive — from soul-warming soups and vibrant salads to delicate dimsum and flavour-packed mains, there was something to please every palate. The menu felt thoughtfully curated, offering both vegetarian and non-vegetarian options without compromising on creativity or taste.

Among the standouts were the Truffle Edamame Dumplings and Cream Cheese Dumplings — both silky, flavorful, and beautifully presented. The Sriracha Chicken Dumplings were spicy and juicy, while the Prawn XO Dumplings delivered that perfect seafood punch. From the sushi section, the Spicy Salmon Roll and Crispy Avocado & Cucumber Roll were fresh and delicious — a must-try for sushi lovers.

Neither does this place have the common courtesy to take care of senior citizens (especially the ones with jain preference)

Nor does it have the ability to take care of a big family which has children and their dietary preference..

4 out of 5 orders were taken wrongly and the quality and taste of the food was something like I mentioned before “a strict reminder” that family dinners should be actually done at home.

We ordered a fungi pasta (for kids) which we specifically pointed out; a wrong order of normal pasta (totally tasteless) was served to us.

We ordered a jain dish of potato (which was to be served with pocket papad; it was a weird potato dish with a hint of garlic!) and no pocket papad

We ordered for a kofta curry (we specifically asked the waiter if this will be enough for 6 adults and 2 kids) he didn’t utter a word; during serving we see literally 2 koftas with gravy (again tasteless) when we asked the waiter why wouldn’t he suggest something better he brashly said “do hi kofta aata hain”

We specifically asked him to switch the AC on multiple times as we felt suffocated; neither did he bother with listening to us first few times; nor did he do anything about it..

All of this just RUINED our family dinner spirit and mood!

I will not at all recommend this place if you’re planning to have a nice family dinner.. their staff makes you feel “unwanted” and their AC section is more like a sauna bath.

Stay far far away from this place, I’m praying we don’t get food poisoning because our mind feels thoroughly poisoned with this restaurants ambience and service.. they ruined a family get together..

Had an amazing dining experience at Mizu Bandra, one of those places that perfectly blends cozy vibes with top-notch Japanese cuisine. The ambiance is modern, minimal, and effortlessly elegant — perfect for both a casual outing or a special dinner. ✨

Here’s what I tried:

🍣 Salmon and Prawn Rolls – absolutely fresh and flavorful! The rolls were perfectly rolled, with the right balance of rice, seafood, and seasoning. The texture was spot on, and every bite just melted in the mouth. Easily one of the highlights of the meal!

🥟 Gyozas – crispy on the outside, juicy on the inside. These dumplings were packed with flavor and served hot, making them the perfect appetizer.

🍜 Ramen – rich, flavorful, and comforting. The broth was hearty and aromatic, the noodles cooked just right, and the toppings perfectly balanced — truly authentic and satisfying.

🍛 Golden Curry – such a comforting dish! Creamy, flavorful, and mildly spiced with that signature Japanese curry richness. It’s the kind of dish that just warms you up instantly.

🍗 Chicken Rice Bowl – tender, well-marinated chicken served over fluffy rice — simple, hearty, and full of flavor. Perfect for anyone who loves balanced, wholesome bowls.

Everything at Mizu was beautifully presented and tasted even better than it looked. The service was friendly and attentive, adding to the overall experience. If you’re in Bandra and craving authentic Japanese flavors with a modern twist, Mizu is definitely the place to go., name_person=JASON SEQUEIRA}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,200–1,400, GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservations recommended, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=6 months ago, review=Mizu has quickly become one of my favorite spots in Bombay. The vibe is super calming and minimal, with a beautiful setup that makes you want to just sit back and enjoy a long, relaxed meal.

We ordered the salmon roll, prawn sushi, asparagus sushi, and both chicken and veg gyoza—and honestly, everything was incredible. The salmon roll was so fresh and perfectly balanced, and the prawn sushi had just the right amount of flavor without being overpowering. Even the asparagus sushi (which I wasn’t expecting much from) turned out to be a standout—super clean and fresh-tasting.

The gyozas were spot on too—crispy on the bottom, juicy inside, and served with a dipping sauce that really tied it all together. You can tell they really care about the quality of ingredients and presentation.

Drinks were great (highly recommend trying one of their signature cocktails), and the service was warm and helpful without hovering. It’s definitely on the pricier side, but for the quality of food, the ambiance, and the overall experience, I’d say it’s totally worth it.

I want to be honest., name_person=Omkar Arjun Jagdale}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Other, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=a month ago, review=Farmers Café

Farmers Café is one of those places that feels like a familiar friend. Other cafés may come and go in the neighborhood, but this one remains a steady presence, always drawing us back. The green facade draped in plants feels lazy in the best way, as if the walls themselves are exhaling calm into the street. Stepping in, the inside may feel cramped, especially near the display, but even in its tightness the space carries a chaotic charm that seems to belong here. There is something reassuring about knowing that most of the menu leans cleaner and healthier than what you find in most restaurants, making indulgence here feel almost virtuous.

We carried with us our long-time favorite, the raspberry chocolate cake with crumble. The layers of raspberry, semi-wet and vivid, pressed against the smoothness of chocolate in a union that sings. On top, a crust of nuts, granola, and oats added the right measure of crunch, tartness, and sweetness, a trio that makes this cake one of the most reliable joys. The hazelnut chocolate cheesecake was a new delight. It was luxurious without being cloying, its top layer speckled with nuts and chocolate chips, and beneath it the chocolate was firm yet smooth, melting into perfection. The nuts deepened the bite, and together it felt like a dessert designed to linger.

The skinny chocolate cake told a different story. Its chocolate layers were thick, flowing, and smooth, but the other portion had a sandy texture that weighed the experience down. The chocolate syrup helped carry it through, compensating for what was lost. The millet truffles looked like tiny treasures, their hard shells dotted with nuts, breaking open to reveal a sandy interior. That texture was expected, given their healthier design, but it made them more admirable than indulgent.

Farmers Café is cramped and chaotic, yes, but it is also green and warm and filled with desserts that let you believe you are choosing wisely. It is not inexpensive, but the familiarity, the healthier touch, and the flavors that stay with you long after you leave make it worth the return, again and again.

The sizzlers are prepared with fresh ingredients, and the presentation is top-notch. The dishes arrive with that signature sizzling sound and a mouth-watering aroma, ensuring that you're in for an unforgettable dining experience.

Apart from sizzlers, Veg Sizzles also offers a diverse multi-cuisine menu, catering to different tastes and preferences. From pastas to Indian curries, their extensive menu ensures there's something for everyone, no matter what you're craving.

The place exudes luxury and elegance with its vibrant ambiance, cozy yet spacious seating, and perfect vibe for both dining and parties.

From cocktails like the Greon Fairy Sour and Mint Berry Mash beautifully crafted by mixologist Tanishq, to the perfectly cooked Grilled Tiger Prawns, flavorful Tofu Tamarindo, crispy Chicken Tuile Gyoza, creamy Tuscan Spaghetti, and smoky Polo Asado every dish was a masterpiece in flavor and presentation.

We ended the evening with their signature dessert The Pear an indulgent creation with glazed pear mousse, salted honey caramel, and brown butter gelato on pecan crumble the perfect finale to an exceptional meal.

The staff was attentive, courteous, and ensured quick service, making the whole experience seamless. Overall, Mercii is not just a restaurant but a complete premium dining destination highly recommended for anyone looking to enjoy world-class food and ambiance in Mumbai., name_person=ABHISHEK}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 months ago, review=Mercii is a high-end European & modern‑global fine dining restaurant in Santacruz (West), backed by Arpita Khan Sharma. The name “Mercii” (French for “thank you”) reflects a philosophy of gratitude, hospitality, and treating guests with warmth rather than cold luxury. The brand positioning is clearly premium & aspirational - it's meant to be more than just food — a full immersive dining experience. One of the standout features is the artificial skylight ceiling - during the day, it simulates soft sunlight and at night, it shifts into a starry sky/ambient skyscape. The interiors are luxurious and ornate - plush seating, rich textures, elegant lighting, jharokha (lattice) motifs, and private alcoves or “VIP room” that can host small groups upto 30 guests. The design attempts to balance regal elegance and vibrant nightlife energy, not just static “luxury.” Overall, the ambience is crafted to wow — it’s meant for special occasions, dates, or high-end dinners.
The kitchen is led by Group Culinary Director Dennis Koll, whose background and experience bring a refined European / global sensibility to the menu. The menu is ambitious — it offers European core (Italian, French etc.) with influences and creative fusions. Many dishes include theatrical or tableside finishing touches to elevate the experience. Some Standouts are
• Crimson & Green (salad)
• Furi Spice Rolls (sushi)
• Edamame Ricotta Gyoza (small plate)
• Rosette Ravioli  (large plate)
• The Pear (dessert)
The bar is a focal point. The cocktail program is expansive, creative, and often experimental, combining dessert flavors, smoky / bold elements, fruit, and classic roots. Some standouts are
• Cocktails - Heet Mango Margarita, Greon Fairy Sour, Smoky Terrain , Mercii Murmur, Mercii Rocher, Flower Power and Holy Biscoff.
• Mocktails - Mint Berry Mash and Sweet Kiss.
The drinks are not just side acts — they are integrated into the experience. Staff are attentive, polite and help with recommendations making the experience special. Mercii is not for everyone — it’s tailored for people who value showpiece ambience, Culinary experience with creative food and artisian drinks, top notch service and luxury. If you're planning a special celebration, date, or want to impress guests, Mercii delivers a strong statement., name_person=Bhavin Parekh}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 months ago, review=Visited Mercii in Santacruz and had such a lovely experience! reviews:
["{guided_block={}, time_line=a week ago, review=Sancha Ice Creams – Andheri West

Whenever we’re in Andheri and the post-dinner sweet cravings hit the entire extended family, there’s always one collective voice that rises above everything else: “Sancha ki ice cream!” This tradition hasn’t changed in years — and honestly, I hope it never does.

Sancha has managed to do something very few brands can: keep that unmistakable taste absolutely consistent over time. So Sancha, a big thank you for staying true to your flavours and staying firmly in business all these years. You’ve been part of our family outings for as long as I can remember.

Whether it’s the chikoo flavour, the strawberry, or just good old classic vanilla, every scoop feels familiar, comforting, and perfect in its simplicity. It’s not just dessert — it’s a memory we keep revisiting.

Sancha isn’t just ice cream for us. It’s a ritual., name_person=Rishi Bharaj}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=4 months ago, review=Nice creamy ice-cream at reasonable rates. Comfortable seating and atmosphere., name_person=vinay dwivedi}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Indoor_dining_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_INDOOR_DINING_AREA], GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=a year ago, review=I ask myself - why havent i visited sancha icecream yet?

The ambience is cool and service great.

What we ate

Mulberry in waffle cone - this flavour is unique. Its the first time i tried it and i loved it.

Fig and honey in a waffle cone - loved it

We also tasted the seasonal guava, orange, sitalphal and my most favourite chocochips - which were all amazing

At sancha icecream, the experience was memorable., name_person=imran badami}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=2 years ago, review=Sancha, a long-standing establishment, is renowned for its exceptional ice cream. Went to this place recently and tried the the Coffee Mocha flavor, which is a must-try for those who adore coffee. It had a delightful grainy texture, and the taste was simply outstanding. While it may be a tad pricey, the experience is undoubtedly worthwhile. Additionally, Sancha provides a seating area for customers, although securing a parking space in the evening can pose a slight challenge. 🙂, name_person=Kruparth Rajput}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=3 years ago, review=One of the oldest icecream parlours in Andheri west near rock beach. I started having the vanila after years am still stuck on it. Cannot be compared with any other icecreams its yum the other seasonal flavours r musy try like mango, strawbery, sitaphal etc nd running flavours, kajudraksh, gulkand, tender coconut, butter scotch, chochip are round the year flavours. The place is quite and peaceful the staff is really good and makes u taste the icecreams happily!! Must try. They also deliver, name_person=A-di}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=4 years ago, review=Sancha Ice Creams is home. I go here Since I was a little girl. Uncle or aunty at the counter are home. Their ice creams are heavy cream. If you want to have the best butterscotch ice cream in the world, Sancha is your place. All the other flavours too are simply natural and amazing. I can feel the ice cream in my head as I write this. Their new ambience is very soothing. A light wood furniture with pastel embossed matte shine tiles in the background to their ice cream box the white brick wall, grey floor tiles. Go! Now!, name_person=Dr Devina Medda}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=4 months ago, review=A 7 Bungalows institution. I've seen this place evolve over the decades and one thing has always remained the same: the quality of the ice cream is always top-notch. reviews: ["{\"name_person\":\"Mads Travel (Madhuri)\",\"time_line\":\"2 weeks ago\",\"review\":\"We visited in the afternoon to chill in the evening and watch the sunset. The restaurant is located right by the shore \u2013 on clear days and during low tide, you can literally drive up close to the entry gate, with the sea just a few steps away.\\n\\nReaching the place, however, can be tricky during high tide. You\u2019ll need to leave your vehicle on the main road and walk through a small trail shaded by big trees. The staff is very helpful \u2013 they\u2019re available to guide and even escort guests if needed \u2013 but if it rains continuously, walking back becomes extremely difficult since the trail gets muddy and slippery. On high tide days, getting in and out can be quite a challenge. For us, it was especially difficult because we happened to visit on a high tide day, and returning was tough while it was raining. ▪️Papad churi

reviews: ["{\"name_person\":\"Anand Iyer\",\"time_line\":\"2 weeks ago\",\"review\":\"Namah Pod CST offers a good place for quick rest and relaxation with fully air-conditioned pods and ample leg space. The pods are compact and clean, providing essential facilities such as charging points and reading lights, making it suitable for travelers seeking comfort during short stays.\",\"guided_block\":{}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Sanket Dyankar\",\"time_line\":\"a month ago\",\"review\":\"Although the pods were actually available, we were informed that none were. I also happened to catch a glimpse of the availability screen, which clearly showed that many pods were vacant. However, I was told that only the family pod was available. reviews: ["{\"name_person\":\"anil sharma\",\"time_line\":\"4 months ago\",\"review\":\"Oye Kake is a vegetarian Punjabi restaurant located on Patel Street in Fort, Mumbai. It is close to famous places like CST and the Gateway of India. The restaurant has a bright and colorful look with Punjabi-style decoration. The walls have fun paintings, and the furniture gives a dhaba (roadside eatery) feel.\\n\\nThe food here is tasty and made with good ingredients. The Amritsari Kulcha Thali is one of the best items. It comes with stuffed kulcha, spicy chole (chickpeas), salad, and curd. The kulcha is soft from inside and crispy outside. The chole is full of flavor. The Dal Makhani is creamy and rich, perfect with butter naan. The Paneer Bhurji and Rajma Chawal also taste like home-cooked food.\\n\\nThe sweet lassi and mango lassi are served in large glasses and are thick and fresh. They go well with the food and are very filling.\\n\\nPrices are a bit high, but the quality and taste make it worth it, especially for special occasions or weekend lunch. Portion size is good, but not very big.\\n\\nThe staff is friendly and gives fast service. The place is clean, including the washroom. During busy hours, you might have to wait a little, but not too long.\\n\\nOye Kake is a good choice if you are looking for pure vegetarian Punjabi food in South Mumbai. It\u2019s a nice spot for families, office workers, and tourists. The location is easy to find and safe to walk around.\\n\\nOverall, it gives a happy Punjabi food experience in the middle of Mumbai\u2019s busy Fort area.\",\"guided_block\":{\"GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE\":\"Lunch\",\"GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE\":\"\u20b9400\u2013600\",\"GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT\":3,\"GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL\":\"Moderate noise\",\"GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE\":[\"3-4_people\",\"E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR\"],\"GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS\":\"Highly recommend\",\"GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO\":[\"Menu_is_all_vegetarian\",\"E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_COMPLETELY_VEGETARIAN\"],\"GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY\":\"Difficult to find parking\",\"GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS\":[\"Valet\",\"E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET\",\"Paid_parking_garage\",\"E:PARKING_OPTION_PAID_PARKING_GARAGE\"],\"GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS\":[\"Vegetarian_options\",\"E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS\",\"Parking\",\"E:PARKING\",\"Kid-friendliness\",\"E:KID_FRIENDLINESS\",\"Wheelchair_accessibility\",\"E:ACCESSIBILITY\"]}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Aman Chawla\",\"time_line\":\"5 months ago\",\"review\":\"Oye Kake is a 100% vegetarian Punjabi restaurant in Mumbai, known for its rich and flavorful North Indian dishes. reviews: ["{\"name_person\":\"Anna\",\"time_line\":\"a month ago\",\"review\":\"Stumbled upon The Lovefools in Bandra with my partner \u2014 and honestly, what a find! It\u2019s literally a hidden, handpicked gem tucked away in the cutest little corner. \u2728\\n\\nWe went all out with the food \u2014 Malabar Sukka, Dal Baati Tart, Asparagus Kulcha, Yaki Pork Chashu, and Belper Knolle Chicken \u2014 and not one missed the mark. Sip • Grab • Taste

Visited Bombay Salad Co. on a Saturday with family, and this place genuinely delivers on the healthy-but-still-tasty promise. The menu is built for health-conscious eaters, but even someone who isn’t into salads will find plenty to enjoy here.

📍 Location & Access
It’s located just off Linking Road, but the approach lane is quite narrow. Valet parking is not available, so if you’re driving, it’s smarter to park a little ahead and walk. Avoid taking the car right to the door not worth the stress.

🍴 What We Ordered:

Three Salad Bowls – we chose the small bowls, but the portions were still surprisingly generous. Fresh greens, good balance of protein and crunch, and well-made dressings nothing watery or bland here.

Cappuccino – smooth, well-made, not bitter. A nice warm pairing with fresh salads.

✨ Ambience & Experience
The vibe is calm, cozy, and “feel good” without trying too hard. Staff is polite, service is steady, and the ingredients felt fresh  which is the real win for a salad-focused place.

⭐ Overall Verdict:
If you're looking for healthy food that doesn't taste like a compromise, Bombay Salad Co. hits the mark.
Great for a relaxed meal, post-gym brunch, or a weekend family catch-up.

Saturday afternoon, 2 pm. The café was buzzing, almost too full to imagine getting a seat. But we got lucky. The place felt alive, conversations floating, sunlight spilling through the windows, staff gliding from table to table with purpose.

I have been trying to eat cleaner lately (not a saint, just a little less junk). Menus like this feel like a test. After a quick chat with the server and some app browsing, I picked the Avocado & Feta bowl (₹360). He asked if I wanted medium or large. I went with medium. When it arrived, I had to laugh this “medium” is a whole meal in itself. Fresh, creamy, and big enough to make me pause halfway. And somewhere between bites, I learned that those peppery leaves I’ve been eating for years are called rocket.

We paired it with a Peach Pie Smoothie (₹350) thick, nutty, and surprisingly filling and an LA Bowl with Quinoa + Falafel (₹460). By the time we reached the last bites, two of us were negotiating who would finish what. The portions here are generous.

1. The vibe: bright, busy, but not chaotic

2. Honest portions that make the pricing feel fair

3. Staff who guide you with a smile

4. Food that actually feels like fuel, not guilt

What could be better:

5. A small discount or loyalty offer would make this an easy weekly habit

6. It can get very crowded post 2 pm on weekends

Our total came to ₹1,287 including taxes and service charge (worth it for the quality).

Tip if you go:
Order a medium bowl if you are pairing it with a smoothie it’s more than enough for one. And go before 2 pm if you want a guaranteed table.

I really feel there should be some decrease in the room rate as it's too high even on weekdays. The overall stay was really good but I was really unhappy with the no entry of Auto Rickshaw inside the property. My mom is a senior citizen with 2 hip replacements. I was being told Rick is not allowed inside so I had to make her walk inside completely. Kindly relook and rethink about it before somebody is being stopped in future. I had booked 2 Deluxe twins through MMT after checking details on the Seven Eleven website. I did book through MMT as I am a Platinum member and only on MMT food package was available to book. After entering the room I didn't see a bathtub in the bath room which was very strange which was clearly mentioned in facilities on their own website. Please find the screenshot of the website of your kind reference. Later I did check for a room upgrade for atleast 1 room as I mentioned I am a Platinum member but the staff clearly denied it which was again upsetting for me. Iron bed was missing in both rooms. Please give atleast room slippers

For Lunch i did order Dal Khichdi, Biryani and Poori Bhaji all was super yummy and instructions were very well followed by the staff, even the quantity was also good as per the prices but the issue i had was when the food came i was being ask to pay first which was very really weird. I did check with the guy can't I pay at the time of check out while settling the bills. He is like NO. I was really unhappy with this kind of rule which i haven't heard in Taj properties also

My stay included the Lunch or Dinner plan so I decided to go for Dinner with my family. The restaurant was very good with an amazing and welcoming staff specially Biswajit was very kind and helpful till the end and dinner food was just yummmm. Thank you Chef Vikram was such good taste and dishes we ordered

Keeping in mind the outstanding dinner, the morning breakfast wasn't that great in taste and wasn't a lavish spread. Idli weren't soft at all and Sabudana Khichdi was oily. The only items I liked were crispy Dosa and Thin parathas. Breakfast would have included Upma, Medu vada, Seviyan upma and Poha for sure

The overall stay in Seven Eleven was good but the authorities really need to look into above pointers for sure to make it more better

They serve dishes from various regions of India, including Rajasthan, Kerala, and Maharashtra, offering a rich and diverse culinary experience.

The quality of food here is exceptional—comparable to top-tier establishments like Taj Santacruz, if not better. Upon being seated, you’re welcomed with a refreshing Kokum drink and crisp Kerala chips, accompanied by three chutneys. The mango pickle is my personal favorite. Based on the waiter’s suggestion, I tried the Kerala and Rajasthani cuisines, and they were absolutely delightful.

In keeping with traditional Indian culture, the restaurant encourages eating with your hands—though cutlery is provided upon request. Even the moringa soup was rich, flavorful, and comforting.

The staff is courteous and well-informed about the menu. They’re happy to guide you through the offerings, and I highly recommend trusting their suggestions—they know what they’re doing.

For those arriving by car, valet parking is available, making your visit even more convenient.

All in all, this place delivers an authentic and satisfying Indian dining experience. Whether you’re a fan of traditional Indian flavors or exploring them for the first time, it’s definitely worth a visit. reviews: ["{\"name_person\":\"Nitika Gupta\",\"time_line\":\"3 years ago\",\"review\":\"Zatar is one of the finest Lebanese delivery kitchen I have come across lately .\\nTheir delivery is always on time by default .\\nThe packaging is 10/10 being spillproof & leakproof .\\nAlso the portion size is generous being value for money in all respect .\\nThe ingredients used are fresh which only enhances the overall taste of the dishes .\\nMy favourite dishes are the creamy hummus , muhammarah ( literally the best in all of mumbai ) , the Greek salad which is wholesome , nutritious & very filling & lastly the harissa paneer makaneesh .\\nI regularly order from here for my house parties . Highly recommended .\",\"guided_block\":{}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Savio Dcunha\",\"time_line\":\"6 years ago\",\"review\":\"Zaatar is a generic name for a family of related Middle Eastern herbs. What Zaatar is to Lebanon, is what Peanut Butter is to America. I was thrilled to find out from Zomato, a Lebanese & Middle Eastern Cuisine existed at Mahalaxmi. I had tried this during lunch after my client visit. The vegetarian food is satisfying, and the menu offers a good variety for those looking to unwind by the sea.

We tried the mac and cheese pasta, akuri (spiced scrambled eggs), paneer bhurji, and a draft beer. The dishes were well-prepared and flavourful—simple comfort food done right. However, the experience was somewhat diminished by the reluctant staff and noticeably delayed service. Been reviewing since a long time and never have I ever gave such a terrific feedback to a restaurant that's good for nothing !

THE BISLERI WE ORDERED WAS THE ONLY ORDER WE LIKED AT THIS PLACE

Starting with the ambience, you will surely love this place if you go for looks and show off ! It has a dedicated space for kids to play but that is only when you want to go and try their food thats good for nothing !

So as usual, we ordered Masala Papad - Rating is 0.5 out of 5 because the Papad was just dripped out from oil and it had no masala as a topping, only sev, some tomato and onions along with 1.5-2 leaves of coriander ! They should change the name to Oily Masala Papad instead !

Secondly, we ordered Paneer Lababdar - In the picture, you will be able to see 17-18 chopped pieces of almonds, never have I ever seen this in a Paneer Lababdar recipe. Remember about these almonds, I'll tell you about it later.

Sorry youtube chefs if I missed out this part of recipe but the color, the gravy, the content itself was 0.1 out of 5 because the paneer was oil fried for the starters we order like Paneer Chilly but as this might be the Chefs first time to make Paneer Lababdar, he had to do the experiment on us ! I never used Fork and Spoon to cut a Paneer into 2 pieces, this time I did !

Remember I told you about the almonds ? They dissapeared when the vegetable was served to us, we were 3, one of the guy had a luck to eat 4-5 pieces, the rest is mistery !

Coming to the taste, don't know what was inside, one cannot guess what it was, the gravy was nothing but something that I cannot even express in words ! If you could say, it had a taste of tomato gravy ? No, it didnt. If you say it had something related to onions and coriander mixture ? No. Don't know what it was but I never ate Paneer Lababdar this bad ! Sorry I do not want to disrespect Food but the Restaurant, the Owner or anyone who handles the kitchen, must rethink about the chefs !

We order 1 butter roti each and that was all ! They do not serve Cold Drinks as they have Mocktails which I am sure would be another disappointment ! Thanks BISLERI to save us at some point !

We paid the bill and we left, not returning again to this place !

❌ Not Suggesting this place ❌

After this trauma, we went to MK Chinese Resturant near Nalasopara East D-Mart - Check the review on my profile !

I politely informed the hotel guy about the issue, to which he responded that this is how Cheese Mysore Masala Dosa is served at your restaurant.

Still unsure, I approached the lady at the counter and very humbly and explained the situation, even showing her a photo of what was served. Her response, however, was surprisingly dismissive and rude. Instead of understanding the concern or offering a courteous explanation, she said very rudely that "we are very up to date, and customers need to update themselves." I found this response not only unprofessional but quite arrogant.

As a customer, I believe respectful communication and a basic level of customer service are essential, especially when feedback is shared politely. I paid the bill and left, but the entire experience left me genuinely disappointed.

Located in the bustling neighborhood of Thakur Complex, Kandivali East, Aai Shree Khodiyar Kathiyawadi Dhaba is a popular food joint known for serving traditional Kathiyawadi cuisine with bold, fiery flavors. The dhaba-style setup gives off a rustic charm, attracting foodies looking for an authentic taste of Gujarat right in the heart of Mumbai.

The menu features a variety of Kathiyawadi staples like Ringan no Olo (Baingan Bharta), Lasaniya Batata, Sev Tameta, Bajra Rotla, and the ever-loved Khichdi Kadhi combo. True to its regional roots, the food here is rich in oil and heavy on spices, making it ideal for those who crave robust, no-compromise flavors. However, for the faint-hearted or those with sensitive stomachs, the spice and oil levels might feel overwhelming.

While the food certainly packs a punch, it’s the homely service and reasonable prices that keep customers coming back. The rotlas are served piping hot, smeared with ghee, and accompanied by tangy pickles and raw onion – completing the authentic Kathiyawadi experience.

The dhaba tends to get busy during evenings and weekends, so a bit of waiting might be expected. It's a casual, no-frills place where the food takes center stage. However, if you prefer milder, less greasy food, this place might not be your go-to. I have visited twice and had a decent experience on both occasions. The place gets busy in the evenings, so it is better to visit in the afternoon or early evening. When I went with my family at 9:30 pm, we had to wait for 20 minutes to get a table.

The restaurant has both indoor air-conditioned seating and outdoor seating. We chose outdoor seating as air-conditioned seating area was fully occupied. But the tables on the left side did not seem suitable for four people, they were comfortable for only two people.

During my visits, I tried Pav Bhaji, Watermelon Juice, Filter Coffee, Triple Schezwan Fried Rice, Masala Dosa, Veg Mille-Jullie, Roti, Jeera Rice, and Sizzling Brownie. The Filter Coffee was good. The Pav Bhaji was made less spicy for a younger diner and was prepared just right. The Triple Schezwan Fried Rice was very good with a lot of vegetables. Masala Dosa was tasty and filling for one person. Veg Mille-Jullie had a spicy and tangy taste that made it different. The Sizzling Brownie was nice, although the brownie was slightly undercooked. The food quality is good, the portions are reasonable, but the prices are slightly high. The service is slow and we had to ask more than once for basic things like spoons or water.

It’s set in a charming bungalow near Carter Road, with valet parking available. While there are a few tables on the ground floor, we were guided upstairs where ample seating is available.

The interiors are beautifully done — plenty of plants, warm lighting, and a calm vibe that instantly lifts the ambiance. Even the regular water served was pineapple-infused, which felt refreshing.

The menu offers a wide range of healthy fusion dishes, with calorie counts mentioned for most items — a thoughtful touch. Service is attentive, with a good number of staff around. Each table has a small bell to call for service, though personally, I preferred calling staff the usual way as the bell felt a bit unnecessary.

Tried the Dal Pakwan Nachos, which had a perfect mix of flavors reminiscent of classic chaat. The Sea Salt Caramel Latte, infused with date syrup, was beautifully balanced and made with premium beans.

Prices are slightly on the higher side, but the overall ambiance, food quality, coffee, and service make it well worth it.
