Headed here for breakfast recently and this place is truly and authentically Maharashtrian. Right from the ambience to the nostalgic Marathi music they play to the hammered steel crockery, everything is quintessential Maharashtrian. And of course, the food tops this list as you can imagine. The food overall was a mixed bag – detailed dish wise review coming up.
The service was super quick and fresh. The waitress (Sanchita) serving us was prompt, pleasant and attentive. Place is clean, parking is available on the street but I would imagine it might get pretty difficult during peak hours.
What we ordered and rating each dish:
1.	Kokum Sharbat – 4.5 out of 5 – The taste was actually phenomenal but deducting half a star as it was not cold and ice wasn’t readily available that time of the day
2.	Nimbu Paani – 5 on 5 – superb balance of flavors and chilled to perfection
3.	Besan Laddoo – 5 on 5 – this is not a standard on their menu but we were lucky since it was right after Diwali, so this was available as part of their special Diwali faral menu. The laddoo’s are as “gharghuti” as it gets. Mind blowing-ly tasty, couldn’t get enough. We loved it so much, we packed half a dozen for home as well
4.	Kolhapuri Misal – 4 on 5 – Very tasty and spicy as it needs to be. However, did seem a tad bit flat – have had better missal. Don’t get me wrong- this wasn’t bad at all but have had better is all
5.	Starter Platter – 4 on 5 – This is a brilliant idea for a menu btw – mini sizes and 2 pieces each of their snacks – aloo vadi, batata vada, kothimbir vada,  veg cutlet, kanda bhaji, batata bhaji and patti samosa. The bhajis, batata vada, cutlet and aloo vadi were mind-blowing! The kothimbir vada and patti samosa though were strictly ok. In fact did not quite fully understand the flavor they were trying to go for with the patti samosa.
6.	Poori Bhaji – 3 on 5 – A strict ok from me. The poori was amazing but the bhaji fell flat. Again not bad, but not as flavorful as the other things
7.	Sabudana vada – 4 on 5 – Flavor was awesome, just felt like it could have been crispier, name_person=Kanchan Shetty}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Menu_is_all_vegetarian, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_COMPLETELY_VEGETARIAN]}, time_line=4 months ago, review=Top quality Maharashtrian food joint which can stand shoulder to shoulder with any other Marathi eatery in say Dadar, Girgaum, Thane or anywhere else! A family favourite for years, Khavayye manages to serve simple but punchy fare, and a lot of variety without compromising on the core branding. Over the years I would have tried some twenty dishes, but can't find fault as such with anything. Perhaps their misal thali could get better: there's lots of poha, usal and misal (or chivda) that they serve, but the amount of rasa was too little as compared to these other garnishes, so I ended up eating them by themselves - though I'm not complaining. The staff, although courteous, could slightly be more enterprising if you ask me. However, all in all, Khavayye rocks., name_person=Dinesh Iyer}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=This is very authentic place, we came in for simple tea & vada pav and were truly surprised by quality of both, specially vada pav freshly made and didn't feel like it had soda or any other those unnecessary stuff, just pure, simple authentic vada pav. remember for such nice thing it takes time, so have patients. their offering is very nice, menu has some very interesting things not seen anywhere. definitely must go with friends or family., name_person=SageRaj Bariya}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹400–600, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Veg_Thali, Kothimbir_Vadi, Pithla, Ukadiche_Modak_Tup, Batata_Wada, Sabudana_Vada, Vada_Pav, Patti_Samosa, Shev_Tomato_Bhaji, अळूवडी, Aamba_Modak_with_Aamras, Aluwadi], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3}, time_line=a year ago, review=If you're in Thane and looking to dive into a comprehensive Maharashtrian culinary experience, Hotel Khavayye is the place to be. As the city's centre premier spot for authentic Maharashtrian cuisine, it offers an impressive array of dishes from breakfast through dinner, making it a must-visit for food enthusiasts.
The restaurant, with its 13 tables and seating capacity for 70 on the ground floor, provides a cozy setting to enjoy the rich flavors of Maharashtra. The menu is extensive, featuring everything from the simple yet comforting Waran Bhat to the exotic Amsrus Puri. For breakfast, don't miss the unique Dhadpe Pohe, Poha Papad, and Papad Fenis, which showcase the traditional morning fare. The Fhodni Cha Bhat and Masala Bhat are standout dishes that capture the essence of Maharashtrian spices and cooking techniques. While the menu includes other items like Pav Bhaji Sandwiches, the real star here is the pure Maharashtrian cuisine.
The restaurant also offers a variety of thalis, such as the Amsrus Thali, Gavran Thali, and Poht Bhar Thali, each with a distinct selection of dishes. Breakfast options are equally tempting, with Thalipeeth, Upma, and Missal leading the charge.
One downside is that the service staff, unfortunately, do not speak Marathi, which can be surprising given the restaurant's strong regional focus. However, this minor inconvenience is easily overshadowed by the food quality and the authentic dining experience.Parking is available but be aware that it is adjacent to a service road and is at the owner's risk. After 8 PM, parking tends to be less of an issue.
Overall, Hotel Khavayye stands out as a delightful haven for those eager to explore the depth and diversity of Maharashtrian cuisine. Whether you're a local or a visitor, this restaurant offers a genuine taste of Maharashtra that is hard to match., name_person=Harshal Ambre}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Somewhat recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹200–400, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Kothimbir_Vadi, Puneri_Misal_2_Pav], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Difficult to find parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Menu_is_all_vegetarian, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_COMPLETELY_VEGETARIAN, Clearly_labeled_vegetarian_dishes, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_CLEARLY_LABELED_ITEMS]}, time_line=a year ago, review=A decent place to try the maharashtrian cuisine. Although we initially had a bit of difficulty locating it, we eventually found it just beside INOX📽, tucked away in a cozy corner. The hunt was totally worth it!

Here’s how our experience unfolded:

Starters:🥗🥣

We ordered two paneer dishes, which seemed to be flavoured with black pepper. The taste was bold and comforting, and the presentation was on point.

Main Course:🍱

For mains, we went with biryani and noodles.

The biryani was aromatic, but both varieties tasted slightly similar, which was a minor letdown.

What we loved:

Fast and efficient service — no long waiting!

Spacious seating, ideal for small groups or cozy dates.

The decor and ambience made for Insta-worthy moments.📸

A good spot for food lovers seeking something different around Dadar., name_person=Mrudul Chandan}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Somewhat recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹400–600, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR, 5-8_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_FIVE_TO_EIGHT, 9+_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_NINE_OR_MORE], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION]}, time_line=5 months ago, review=Angrezi Dhaba is a bit of a hidden gem – quite literally. It's clear a lot of thought has gone into creating an inviting and stylish ambiance, blending a modern aesthetic with classic dhaba charm.
And then, the music hits.
While the food at Angrezi Dhaba is genuinely excellent – flavorful, well-presented, and a testament to a skilled kitchen – the entire experience is relentlessly undermined by the deafening volume of the music. I’ve been here on multiple occasions, and here’s some of the food I’ve tried:

Chicken Parmesan – perfectly cooked, cheesy, and full of flavour.

Spaghetti Aglio Olio – simple, classic, and done just right.

Cheesy Garlic Pizzetta – essentially your classic garlic bread in a new format; not something I’d personally order again.

Quattro Formaggi Pizza – honestly, one of the best four-cheese pizzas I’ve had in Mumbai.

Pollo Pesto Pizza – a pleasant surprise! The pesto adds a nice freshness, and the chicken was tender and well-seasoned.

Pollo Picante Pizza – a must-try, with grilled chicken, capers, and olives in a spicy tomato sauce.

I would definitely recommend this spot to anyone craving truly authentic pizza — thin crust, a great cheese blend, and that unmistakable Italian aroma. Almost every pizza here is an easy 10/10.

reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=a month ago, review=There’s something truly special about The Table.

It’s one of those rare restaurants that manages to feel both familiar and surprising every single time. The space has an easy charm — elegant but not trying too hard — and the energy always feels just right, whether it’s lunch sunlight filtering through the windows or a lively dinner service.

The food is consistently beautiful in its simplicity. Every dish feels like it’s been thought through — fresh, balanced, and built around great produce rather than fuss. You can taste the confidence in the cooking. The menu reads globally, but the soul of it feels distinctly their own.

And the service — calm, intuitive, quietly excellent. It’s clear that a lot of care goes into every part of the experience.

After all these years, The Table still feels like one of the most assured, grown-up dining rooms in Mumbai — the kind of place you leave already planning your next visit., name_person=Nuzzy J}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservations recommended, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Moderate noise, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Wheelchair_accessibility, E:ACCESSIBILITY], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=Really enjoyed our meal at The Table, Mumbai. We started with fresh oysters, followed by the salmon and beef tartare, both well balanced and made with great quality ingredients. The French onion soup and corn bread were comforting and full of flavor.

The lobster was cooked perfectly and tasted excellent, and the beef fillet that followed was tender, well seasoned, and done just right. The atmosphere is relaxed yet refined, with attentive service throughout. A great place for a leisurely, well-executed meal—would happily return., name_person=Vishal Shah}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Varies by time/day, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Moderate noise, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[1_person, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_ONE], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=a week ago, review=Having conducted prior research on this establishment, I was eager to experience their signature offering.

And what an evening it was! Perfect ambience, beautiful presentations, and above all, impeccable, friendly and very personal service!
A special shout out to Dhiraj who was the team member that attended to us. I am planning to take my wife there next time I'm back in Bombay and Dhiraj is a huge part of the reason for that ❤️!
Highly, highly recommend The Table., name_person=Mayank Vora}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 months ago, review=Incredible meal at The Table, can easily see why they're no 1.

But the taste was one of the best ones I have had. The not-too-sweet and strong taste of chocolate made it delightful in every bite.

Churros with white chocolate

reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=If you're looking for an unlimited affordable buffet in the Western Suburbs, Peshawari Grill in Goregaon East is a top Restaurant. Located on the 2nd floor of The Hub Mall, Western Express Highway, this Restaurant delivers a solid spread of veg & non-veg unlimited food in a comfortable, spacious setting.

From the moment we arrived, the ambience hit the right note — generous seating, warm lighting, and a relaxed vibe that works for both family dinners and friendly meet-ups. The staff are attentive and the buffet layout is well organised. They allow you to enjoy your dinner without disturbing much but be available when you call out any of them.

On to the food — you’ll find a wide variety of dishes: live counters with pani puri, soups, a full spread of starters (veg & non-veg kebabs, tandoori items), main courses ranging from North Indian to Chinese & Mughlai, breads, rice, and a nice dessert section.

Key favourites: the paneer tikka, chicken rarhya, lasooni fish, and for desserts the dudhi halw and kheer are worth a try.

With the special offer of ₹499 on Mondays & Tuesdays, you’re looking at an exceptional deal for the area.

The location is convenient for the Western Suburbs (Goregaon East), making it a solid choice for buffet restaurant in that region.

If I were to offer some tips:

Go early (lunch/dinner) to avoid peak crowd and ensure you get the full buffet spread without items running out.

Try out your best veg and non veg dishes - one at a time so that you don't get confused.
Start with the live counters (pani puri, kebabs) and work your way to mains & desserts — being strategic helps when you want to make the most of a buffet.

Bring your foodie group or family — the place has big seating which is great for group bookings.

In short: if you’re in Mumbai’s Western Suburbs and on the lookout for an unlimited food buffet restaurant that is within your budget, this is very much worth a visit. reviews:

I visited with a few friends and we were all left seriously impressed. From the moment we walked in, the grand Indian décor set the tone for a rich, indulgent dining experience. The ambiance is regal, yet welcoming, perfect for a relaxed catch-up or even a celebration.

The food? Beyond delicious. Every dish was packed with flavor and beautifully presented. Must-try items include the Paneer Tikka Multani, Murgh Darbari Kebab, Aachari Lamb Chop, Bhatti Da Murgh, Tandoori Jhinga, and the ultra-fragrant Ghosh-ki-Dum Biryani. For desserts, the Rasmalai Tres Leches and Jalebi with Rabadi were a hit—rich, creative, and perfectly balanced. Their mocktails were refreshing and paired well with the spices.

The service was lightning fast, and the staff were courteous, attentive, and extremely well-mannered, which made the whole experience even better. A huge shoutout to Chef Ishijot Singh, whose culinary mastery truly shines through each dish., name_person=Jannat Sorathia}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,000–1,200, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[5-8_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_FIVE_TO_EIGHT, Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=6 months ago, review=Mulk is wow, It would be totally unjustified if I wrote anything about the food. The quality of food and the taste are on a different level. The Jeera Phudine ka sherbet, the Tandoori items, the veg starters, the kebabs, the biryanis, the main course just awesome. Go and try anything on the menu. Just go. The hospitality is wonderful with good people around to serve you with lovely food. The only thing that is not imp but just as important was the AC it wasn't cooling, I guess that will be taken care of., name_person=Dinesh r Vijlah}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SPECIAL_EVENTS=[No_special_event, E:DINING_SPECIAL_EVENTS_NO_SPECIAL_EVENT], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=4 months ago, review=Mulk in Andheri West, Mumbai, is a truly special place for a meal. From the moment we were welcomed with a delicious sev puri, the experience was wonderful.

For beverages, we enjoyed the lassi and a spicy guava drink, both of which were excellent. We started with the paneer kurkure and stuffed aaloo, which were perfectly prepared and full of flavor. The food is why i would definitely visit again!!, name_person=devanshi shah}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=5 months ago, review=I visited Era Restaurant one afternoon for lunch, and the experience was truly delightful. The ambiance was calm and peaceful, with soothing music playing in the background — perfect for a relaxed meal. The service was impeccable, and every dish I ordered was absolutely delicious. I genuinely enjoyed the entire experience and would highly recommend this place. Looking forward to visiting again soon!, name_person=Shodhan Vora}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,600–1,800, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Moderate noise, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Wheelchair_accessibility, E:ACCESSIBILITY], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[5-8_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_FIVE_TO_EIGHT], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION]}, time_line=6 months ago, review=We went to this place on a friends recommendation.

The place was packed by 8:30. The service was a bit slow but the staff that waited our table were quite good with recommendations etc.

Food
The dim sums were yummy both chicken coriander and crystal vegetable
We also tried the avocado sushi which was nice and the lotus root starter is okay I would suggest it. The pandan leaf chicken was tasty. We also had the Parmesan fries that was delicious.

The drinks we had was okay.

For mains we just had the khao Suey it was yummy and the portion size of decent and finally we had the mango sticky rice which was slightly disappointing because we tried it in other places and the ratio of mango was little.

My review is subject to change if I visit the place again., name_person=Rosemary Pattem}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING, Wheelchair_accessibility, E:ACCESSIBILITY], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Somewhat difficult to find parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Moderate noise, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION]}, time_line=5 months ago, review=Having been here 5 times in the past 3 months has given me a different experience each time. The ambience is cozy and nice. The music is decent up until 8.30 pm after which they pick up pace and start giving club vibes instead of a lovely restaurant and lounge. So not suitable for conversations in the evenings.

The service is nice until the servers keep interrupting between the conversations for feedback on every single dish, and also to share their own views in between the tables conversation. That's honestly not okay.

The food is lovely mostly, except for the desserts. Every time we tried a new dessert, it was a new disappointment. The house mocktails and cocktails are quite nice. And, giving an honest feedback may also be met with an explanation of how one needs to appreciate the food offered instead. Yes that happened with us over desserts and a broccoli tikka. Just avoid it.

The turnip cake in thai chilli is amazing although they never seem to have it anymore. The dynamite prawns are delicious according to a friend, the truffle mushroom and cream cheese sushi, shrimp tempura sushi, pan seared veg gyoza, kung pao cottage cheese bao are absolutely amazing! Also, do not miss the Korean cream cheese bun!

The Korean chilli potato, vegetable crystal dimsum and creamy broccoli tikka don't have any flavour according to us. The tikkas are a bit disappointing as well as it's not actually from a tandoor or given enough time to catch onto any flavour. You can also spot the handmade ho fan noodles that has novelty of being handmade but it was a bit bland for our taste.

In mains, the chilli garlic fried rice, classic hakka noodles and Malaysian noodles are amazing! Even the Teriyaki bowl and pan fried noodle bowl is really delicious., name_person=samiksha singhal}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,800–2,000, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Loud, but you can still talk, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Clearly_labeled_vegetarian_dishes, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_CLEARLY_LABELED_ITEMS]}, time_line=a month ago, review=Had an absolutely wonderful experience at Era! From the moment we walked in, the place had such a warm and inviting vibe. The decor is stunning, every corner is beautifully done and gives off an elegant yet cozy feel. The ambiance was perfect for a special occasion, with great lighting, music, and overall atmosphere.

The food was incredible - every dish was fresh, full of flavour, and plated beautifully. You can really tell there’s attention to detail in both presentation and taste. The service was top-notch too; the staff were polite, attentive, and made sure everything went smoothly throughout the evening.

We went for a birthday night dinner, and it turned out to be the perfect choice. Amazing food, beautiful setting, and such a lovely overall experience. Would highly recommend Era for anyone looking to celebrate something special or just enjoy a truly memorable meal!, name_person=Shivani Sharma}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=My experience was great here with great ambience & delicious food like

California Sushi, Crispy Lotus Root

Baked Vanilla Cheesecake, Cheese & Chives

Dimsum, Tofu in Sichuan Peppercorn, Indonesian style

cottage cheese all items were tasty along with drink specially that Drinks in mocktail s Mango & Thai BasilCooler, Kankitsuri, name_person=Jyothika Shirola}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,800–2,000, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=9 months ago, review=Era is located off Link Road Andheri West and it is near Fun Republic.

The restaurant is spacious with one the best ambiance made. They have created an old Italian jazzy bar theme which looks extremely beautiful. Loved every space from the moment you enter as they have really made every corner perfectly. The huge bar looks perfect. The lights with chandelier and every walls have different elements used. The DJ console is nicely placed with a huge piano. Also the seatings are nicely arranged with options for all size of groups. So overall the vibe and the restaurant is just beautiful and perfect.

They specialise in multi cuisine hence options from Asian and Indian cuisines are available. Loved the menu as it covers a variety of dishes. Prices are at par with similar type of high end restaurants and the quantity served is good.

Went here on a Wednesday dinner and trust me the music played was outstanding and it didn’t felt like it was a Weekday. The kitchen service was on time and the table service by staff Vishal & Shubham was smooth.

What We Had -
APPETISERS~
Sanpai Chicken -
Chicken with mushrooms and veggies tossed in chilli sauce tasted good. Loved the juicy chicken as the sauce in it tasted really good. Even the sauce was chilly garlic based it didn’t had strong flavours.

Chicken & Prawn Shu Mai Dimsum -
Perfect outer covering and generously filled with prawns and chicken tasted amazing. The freshness and juiciness was great and eating this with chilli oil was simply divine.

Shrimp Tempura Roll -
Fresh prawns, avocado, tempura crunch and spicy sauce on the topped tasted outstanding. Everything about the sushi was perfect and we loved eating every piece of this.

Truffle Parsley Chicken -
Juicy chicken tikka with parsley pesto marination tasted nice as the chicken was flavourful and the grilling was perfect however I missed the taste or aroma of truffle in this.

MAINS~
Truffle Mushroom Fried Rice -
Simple and tasty. This had sticky rice with mushrooms and edamame along with truffle oil drizzle. Overall this was perfect as the truffle oil was excellent and the rice plus mushrooms had nice earthy flavours.

Chicken Masala with Truffle Garlic Naan -
Surprisingly good as the gravy tasted really nice. Not too tangy but it was lightly spicy. Eating this with naan was perfect.

DESSERTS~
Saffron Tres Leches.
Era Millionaire Brownie.
Between both the desserts the Saffron Tres Leches was the best. The brownie was decent as I found it a little dry.

MOCKTAILS~
Passionfruit Ice Tea.
Kankitsurui.
Yuzu Galangal Mojito.
The drinks were made nicely and no complaints here.

So our meal at Era Andheri West was one of the memorable experiences as the food was perfect, the service was excellent and topping all this the vibe of the place is fantastic. Hence you should not miss this., name_person=Shaikh Khalid Sarfaraz}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=4 months ago, review=I recently ordered food from Era Restaurant, and it exceeded all expectations! The packaging was neat and secure, ensuring the food arrived hot and fresh. Every dish was presented beautifully, even in takeaway form, showing the restaurant’s commitment to quality.
The Chicken Satay was a star on its own — tender, juicy pieces of chicken, perfectly grilled with a smoky aroma, and served with a delicious, creamy peanut sauce that elevated every bite.
The Chicken Fried Rice was equally impressive — fluffy grains of rice stir-fried to perfection with generous portions of chicken, fresh vegetables, and just the right amount of seasoning. It
What impressed me most was that the quality and taste felt exactly like dining in at a fine restaurant — no compromise despite it being a delivery order. The portion sizes were generous, and every dish had that special touch that makes Era stand out.
Era Restaurant truly knows how to deliver excellence, both in taste and service. This will definitely be my go-to place for future orders!, name_person=Poonam Kadam}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=The service was impeccable, and every dish I ordered was absolutely delicious.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=The menu offers a great variety of dishes, blending flavour’s.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Food was not good Small size portions .}"]

Thankfully, we had a reservation, so we were seated right away.
We tried quite a few dishes: Chicken Lettuce Wrap, Seafood Dumplings with Chilli Oil, Salt & Pepper Vegetables, Lotus Leaf Rice, Tenderloin in Chilli Oil & Spring Onion, and ended with the Royal China Mud Cake. Almost everything was delicious, but the Salt & Pepper Vegetables and the Tenderloin with Lotus Leaf Rice were the real standouts for us.
The staff were friendly and attentive, and overall the service was good. A couple of dishes did take a little longer to arrive, but given how busy it was, that was understandable.

The place has a very classy and elegant vibe. The staff was extremely polite and welcoming, which made the visit even better.
We started with Orange Blossom, a refreshing mocktail full of fruity flavours of orange, cranberry, and apple. The Yuzu Viking was another favourite with pineapple juice and elderflower syrup, very light and fresh.
For starters, the Belgian Pork Dumplings were soft, flavourful, and perfectly steamed. The Smoked Shredded Chicken was crispy, garlicky, and had a nice crunch from the vegetables.
The highlight for me was the Truffle Tenderloin, seared to perfection and served on a sizzling plate with that rich truffle aroma. The Hong Kong Street Style Noodles were simple yet very tasty, with beansprouts and spring onion adding the right crunch.
We ended with the Chocolate Dome, which was a delightful surprise with mud cake and ice cream inside. Overall, Royal China is definitely a place I would recommend for anyone who enjoys great food, a classy setting, and excellent service., name_person=Tanishka Chavan}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,400–1,600, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[5-8_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_FIVE_TO_EIGHT], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=3 months ago, review=Gets a little crowded and noisy. ["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Very loud, hard to hear, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_SPECIAL_EVENTS=[No_special_event, E:DINING_SPECIAL_EVENTS_NO_SPECIAL_EVENT], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=My visit here turned out to be disappointing. The atmosphere was fine, but the way the staff handled basic service left me uncomfortable. I had ordered a beer, and before I could finish the last sip, someone from the staff simply picked up the bottle and walked away. When I asked about it, they acted as if nothing had happened. What made it worse was how they dealt with bottles on the table. They took half filled ones and claimed they were empty. Anyone can see that if a bottle needs to be cleared, it should be done with respect for the guest instead of pretending it was already finished. It felt careless in a way that made the moment frustrating and almost humorous because of how casually it happened. This might be a training issue, since rushed staff often make mistakes without realizing how it affects the guest. It could also be a deeper problem with how the team has been managed. The service culture in the cocktail bar section in front of the kitchen felt completely off. The place has potential only if they replace the current team with a new one in that section so guests can actually enjoy what the space has to offer. If someone still plans to visit, a quieter time might help, though I hope the management takes feedback seriously and makes the changes that are clearly needed., name_person=Sparsh Keshwani}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Indoor_dining_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_INDOOR_DINING_AREA], GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[5-8_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_FIVE_TO_EIGHT], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 months ago, review=Bonobo never disappoints when it comes to atmosphere and energy. Drinks are well crafted, and the service team is attentive without being intrusive. Even on busy nights, they manage to keep things running smoothly.

name: AL's Kitchen and Grill, Orlem, Malad
reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=2 months ago, review=I recently visited ALS Kitchen, Orlem Malad West, and I must say it turned out to be one of the best pocket-friendly restaurants I’ve tried in this area. The food, flavors, and overall experience were truly satisfying, especially for the price point.

We ordered three dishes – Rawas Koliwada, Surmai Tawa Fry, and Chicken Tikka Biryani – and each one was a delight in its own way. The Rawas Koliwada was fresh, crispy on the outside, yet soft and juicy inside, with that authentic koli-style marination that gives a perfect kick of spice. The Surmai Tawa Fry was another highlight – perfectly seared, well-spiced, and cooked just right to retain the fish’s natural flavors. For seafood lovers, both of these are absolute must-tries.

Coming to the Chicken Tikka Biryani, it was flavorful, aromatic, and comforting. The chicken pieces were tender, well-marinated, and cooked to perfection. The biryani had just the right balance of spices, making it tasty without being too heavy or oily – something that’s hard to find these days.

The service was quick, the staff was polite, and the ambiance felt simple yet welcoming. For the quality and taste offered, the pricing is very reasonable, making it a great option for both casual outings and regular visits.

Overall, I would rate ALS Kitchen a 4/5. If you’re in Malad West and looking for delicious seafood or a wholesome biryani at pocket-friendly prices, this place should definitely be on your list!, name_person=Saahil Ledwani}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=4 months ago, review=Have you ever tried this Delicious Biryani 👌🏻
This place serve veg, Non veg, Ssafood, Chinese & specially Biryani then must visit 👍🏽
Comfortable sitting arrangement with private party, small event, birthday party 30-40 pax capacity, name_person=Aashu Shinde}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Chicken_Tawa_Pulao, Apple_Chicken, Als_Special_Chicken_Biryani, Prawns_Fry, Chicken_Thali, Bombil_Fry, Ravas_Fish_Fry], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=a year ago, review=Al’s Kitchen is a hidden gem that combines top-notch food with a welcoming atmosphere, making it a must-visit for any food lover. From the moment you walk in, the staff greets you with genuine warmth and attentiveness, making sure that every customer feels right at home. The ambiance is cozy yet modern, and the layout creates an inviting space, perfect for a casual dinner or a special gathering with friends and family.

The food, however, is what truly steals the show. Al’s Kitchen offers a diverse menu that caters to various tastes, whether you’re in the mood for classic comfort dishes or adventurous new flavors. Every dish is crafted with a clear attention to detail, from the perfect seasoning to the beautiful presentation. Their signature dishes are a must-try — I especially recommend the slow-cooked beef brisket, which is tender and packed with a depth of flavor that you won’t forget anytime soon. For vegetarians, they also offer creative options that don’t compromise on taste.

Another standout aspect of Al’s Kitchen is the level of care they put into every aspect of the dining experience. The staff are well-versed in the menu and are happy to provide recommendations based on your preferences, while also ensuring that dietary needs are accommodated. The portions are generous, but if you have room for dessert, don’t miss out — their chocolate lava cake is rich and absolutely delicious!

Overall, Al’s Kitchen is a restaurant where quality, taste, and customer service come together seamlessly. It’s a place where you can truly relax and savor a meal, knowing that you’re in good hands. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a satisfying and memorable dining experience., name_person=jeet sandhu}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹400–600}, time_line=Edited 3 years ago, review=Yummy food, even veg and nonveg.. the mutton seekh kabab was delicious, with proper spice and was cooked well. reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹400–600, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=Up to 10 min}, time_line=3 months ago, review=Stumbled upon this Famous café recently and it’s already one of my new favorite spots in the city!

☕ Hot Chocolate: Absolutely divine — rich, velvety, and perfectly balanced. Not too sweet, just how I like it. If you're a hot chocolate lover, this one's a must-try.

🍰 Tiramisu pay Latte: A creative twist that actually works. The espresso and tiramisu flavors complement each other beautifully — creamy, strong, and comforting.

🍜 Asian Bowl: Fresh, flavorful, and filling. The sauce was on point and the veggies had a lovely crunch. Loved the flavours, could be more spicy.

🌯 Bombay Roll: A nostalgic kick! Spicy, tangy, and wrapped in a soft roll — this one's packed with bold Mumbai street-style flavor.

🍮 San Sebastian Cheesecake: Easily the highlight of the entire menu. Creamy, with chocolate syrup on top, and melts in your mouth. The sandwich was filling, fresh, and delicious (though a bit messy with the egg yolk), while the Tiramisu latte was the star of the meal — highly recommended. The Mocha felt a little bland in comparison. Portion sizes are just right — enough to satisfy without being too heavy. Pricing leans slightly on the higher side, but the quality of ingredients justifies it. Service was quick, and food arrived without a long wait. Overall, a solid spot if you’re looking for good food and coffee.

It's petite café at the mouth of Versova Metro — easy to find and hard to miss. The vibe outside is very "open"— sitting by the road, watching cars, people, and the city move while sipping on coffee. The indoors are smaller, but the outdoor setup has a vibe, lively feel. Tables are well spaced, clean, and service is efficient., name_person=Stylemonger}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Brunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,000–1,200, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=4 months ago, review=I found a breakfast spot right below versova metro station. The place itself has a cozy, vibrant Mexican vibe, great for a casual evening out.

🍴 What We Tried

Mexican Tortilla Soup – tasty, warm, comforting, but honestly just enough for one person.

Enchilada – the best dish of the evening; crispy tortilla with well-balanced fillings, a must-try.

Taqitas (Paneer) – interesting to try, but with paneer it felt more like eating paneer bhurji in a tortilla roll.

Burrito Bowl & Aeros Mexicano – both mains were flavorful, but the quantity was quite small for the price.

✨ Food & Service
The food overall was tasty, and the service attentive and polite. However, for 2+ people, you need to order multiple portions to feel satisfied, which makes it heavy on the pocket.

💡 Tip: Great for trying small plates or sharing starters, but if you’re coming in a bigger group or with a big appetite, be prepared to order more than usual.

⭐ Overall Verdict
Poco Loco serves authentic-tasting Mexican dishes with good service and a lively vibe. There's a buzzer provided at each desk to call the staff when in need. Menu is to be scanned from the QR and hence the order placing experience was smooth. Sihi, however, was the most anticipated item that has disappointed. The portion size was too small and the taste didn't quite impress us. reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=I visited Spice Laundry and honestly loved every bit of it.
The ambience is adorable, classy, and very welcoming.
The Checkmate Sushi in black and white looked beautiful and was filled with avocado, cucumber, and cream cheese, making it light and creamy.
The Jennifer Aniston Quinoa Bowl had red quinoa, sweet potato chips, boiled beetroot, avocado, chickpeas, broccoli, kale, hummus, sunflower seeds, and a cashew–jaggery dressing, which was wholesome and tasty.
The Berry Merry mocktail with fresh strawberry, mixed berry purée, pineapple foam, and fizz was refreshing.
Dragon’s Kiss was a lovely fusion of lychee and dragon fruit, sweet and exotic.
The Pav Bhaji Fondue was a spicy mashed veggie mix with cheese, served hot with croutons.
The Cheese Wheel Pasta was rich and creamy, tossed fresh in a parmesan cheese wheel.
We ended with the Hazelnut Strawberry Pull Me Up Cake, which was indulgent and delicious.
Everything felt gourmet and well presented.
One of the best vegetarian food spots in Chembur for sure. 💛🍽️, name_person=Tanishka Chavan}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 weeks ago, review=This restaurant has really won me over with their menu! I love the cozy vibe of this place, and all the service staff were so amazing and nice. I came here with my friend, and we tried lots of things, and each one of them was great!

They also make pizza in a traditional wood-fired oven, so we tried the Pannazo Sandwich and Farmers Choice Pizza, and both were just fabulous! The Pannazzo Sandwich was literally a flavor bomb! I highly recommend it.

They've also started their new Christmas menu, and I tried the Pink Wasabi Strawberry Sushi - it's something unique, something I'd never had before, and I love it!

My friend ordered a mocktail named White Christmas: it was a tender coconut-based cocktail, and he enjoyed the drink a lot, so I'll recommend this as well.

We also tried their Plant Protein Schezwan Sizzler, and OMG, this was so fulfilling - a perfect main course.

Last but not least, we ordered a Christmas special dessert named Christmas Matcha: this dessert came with table drama, and it's basically a cheesecake covered with matcha cream and decorated to resemble a Christmas tree. Taste-wise, this was 10/10! I highly recommend this!, name_person=jd}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=Mumbai ke is pure veg and Jain Restaurant ne introduce kar Diya hai unka New Menu . We picked this restaurant for my brother's birthday based on its aesthetic appeal and a promising menu listed on Zomato. The place even had my name in it so naturally, there was some curiosity and excitement. I wish I could say it lived up to any of it.

We were a group of seven and ordered a variety mocktails, starters, Indian and Asian mains, and desserts. But things started going south pretty quickly.

Service: Disorganized and careless. Our server completely forgot to place one of our mains, and by the time we realized, the kitchen had closed. All we received in return was a dry sorry no attempt to make up for it, no basic courtesy.

Food: Inconsistent and disappointing. Everything was either bland or too salty. The spice balance was completely off, but salt was always on the higher side almost as if they were compensating for a lack of flavor.

Desserts: A complete mess. Half the items were sold out. Some were apparently not available after the kitchen closed even though we had ordered them before. Communication was poor, and no one seemed to be on the same page.

In summary: Chaos, excessive salt, and a whole lot of embarrassment especially after choosing this place for a special occasion. It’s not just about poor service; it’s about how little they seemed to care about it.

reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,200–1,400, GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservation required, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Very quiet, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=a month ago, review=I visited Waarsa after seeing a few reels about their Biryani Festival, but honestly, it didn’t quite live up to the hype. I tried the Islampuri Chaap Biryani — the mutton was well-cooked and flavourful, inspired by Bengal-style biryani. Interestingly, they used sweet potato instead of the usual potato, and the classic boiled egg was missing. The mutton portion was generous, but the rice quantity was just enough for one person. To be fair, the staff was kind enough to offer an extra bowl of rice for my friend.

I also tried the Tangdi Kebab, which was soft, juicy, and nicely done — not extraordinary, but definitely enjoyable. The Mutton Galouti Kebab was the real winner — absolutely delicious. The Dal Makhani was standard, like what you’d get at most restaurants.

Maybe I went in with high expectations after seeing all the hype online, but overall, I’d say it’s a decent experience made better by their warm, courteous staff and good service., name_person=Aditi Datta}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,000–1,200, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Vegetarian_menu_or_section, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_SEPARATE_MENU_SECTION, Clearly_labeled_vegetarian_dishes, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_CLEARLY_LABELED_ITEMS]}, time_line=4 weeks ago, review=It's difficult to find good North Indian delicacies in Mumbai. Waarsa definitely helps bridge the gap. The atmosphere and the food is equally soothing.

For starters we had,
Rajma Chukander ki Galouti: 4/5
Kairi Shakarandi ka Tikka: 4/5

In mocktails,
Divine Passion: 4/5
Zero Proof Americano: 6/5

For mains,
Kache Kale ke kofte: 5/5
The gravy is velvety!!
Taftan: 3/5

All and all, an experience worth reliving., name_person=Rohit Rawat}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,600–1,800, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=6 months ago, review=Waarsa at NCPA, Nariman Point, is a gem serving authentic Awadhi cuisine.

The food is flavorful yet light, with dishes like Raan-e-Mukhtar (slow-cooked goat leg) and Zafrani Lagaan Murgh stealing the show.

Vegetarian options like Bhindi Kali Mirch and Lauki aur Chana Dal Shikhampuri are equally delightful.

The Kesar Phirni was the highlight—creamy, aromatic, and perfectly sweet.

Their cocktails, like The Emperor’s Rose and Gin Gilori, are creative and pair well with the meal.

The ambiance is stunning, with salmon-hued walls, intricate ceilings, and elegant decor, creating a warm, royal vibe.

Service is top-notch, attentive, and friendly, making the experience special. Chefs Rahul Akerkar and Mukhtar Qureshi, culinary geniuses, craft a menu blending royal and home-style Awadhi flavors.

Owned by Aditya Birla New Age Hospitality, Waarsa is a must-visit for food lovers seeking an unforgettable dining experience in Mumbai.

Cocktails:

Emperor Rose: A refreshing, floral drink.  Gin Gilori: A gin-based cocktail with delicate flavors.  Court Jester: Gin with pickled Bhavnagri chili, jasmine, and mint.   Despite some inconsistency in early reviews, the drinks complement the cuisine beautifully.

Popular Dishes:Non-vegetarian: Raan-e-Mukhtar, Zafrani Lagaan Murgh, Murgh Gilafi Seekh Kebab, Rampuri Kacche Gosht ki Tikki.

Vegetarian: Bhindi Kali Mirchi, Lauki aur Chana Dal Shikhampuri, Awadhi Tawa Paneer Pasanda, Kasundi Baingan Tikka.

Desserts: Kesar Phirni, Angoori Rabdi.  Others: Chilgoza Shorba, Gucchi Biryani, Daal Q-Man.

Must try place., name_person=Prithvish Ashar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=Waarsa was an absolute delight!
While the ambience is fairly simple and understated, the food more than makes up for it. Every dish we tried was phenomenal...rich in flavour, beautifully balanced, and truly reminiscent of authentic Mughlai indulgence.

A special shout out to Rugved, whose service was impeccable. He guided us with great recommendations and ensured everything was just right throughout our meal.

We especially loved the nihari, the chef’s special mushrooms, and the butter chicken...each one, a standout in its own way., name_person=Misba Memon}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=4 months ago, review=Fine dine place at NCPAserving authentic awadhi cuisine. Most dishes hit the spot perfectly. Highlights would be the korma soup, kebabs, paneer gravies and the biryani, name_person=Sudarshan Pawar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,800–2,000}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=there was a photo shoot happening at the restaurant today from 4:30, so there was commotion from 3 (setting up lights, moving paintings) while we were eating - we were also asked to move from where we were sitting so they could set up for the photoshoot (this was at 3:30, the restaurant hours are till 4)
the owner came to our table at 4:15 while we were just finishing up and said that they were going to start a photoshoot so “can you guys be quiet or how is this going to work”
i dont understand how such a highly rated place can be so bad at service, it was truly a harrowing experience. we had booked a table in advance where they could have mentioned that they were going to need us to move at 4 - we would have dined elsewhere in that case because it is not like the food was cheap, name_person=Tanvi Agrawal}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=1}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=Let me begin with positives, the service was excellent. The food was quite well made but I am not sure it is worth their price. The breads can be better and the mushroom curry we got was not fit to be in their menu. The beetroot kebab and the chicken do pyaza were the highlights.

Now, the reason I am rating my experience as 2 stars is because I had the misfortune of going there when there was a photoshoot. They asked us to move from the table we were sitting. And  the owner spoke to us with a certain tone that is non welcoming to try and make us leave. It was a bizzare experience.  Why take people in when you know there is a shoot planned and then proceed to try and get them out early?, name_person=Gopichand Kotana}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=2}, time_line=a month ago, review=The meal was really delicious, however it was not particularly exceptional or authentic to the cuisine or dish specified. It also detracts from the overall experience when you have to walk through the construction site, surrounded by construction debris, to use the restroom and hand-wash., name_person=Padam Bhushan}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=We loved the food, the service and the ambience.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Lunch was delightful — a comforting home-cooked meal served with love.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Indian dishes top quality and full of spices.}"]

["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,400–1,600, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Dietary_restrictions, E:OTHER_DIETARY_RESTRICTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING, Wheelchair_accessibility, E:ACCESSIBILITY], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[5-8_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_FIVE_TO_EIGHT], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Not sure, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Clearly_labelled_vegetarian_dishes, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_CLEARLY_LABELED_ITEMS]}, time_line=a week ago, review=We went for a lunch with friends on a Saturday afternoon. In spite of a weekend, it wasn’t crowded though it got crowded later. Staff here is very helpful in suggesting what to have, they also have a regard for food allergies etc. Being orient cafe, decor has Burmese hats, bamboo containers. Menu covers Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese cuisine. Among non alcoholic drinks, Kumbocha is worth trying. Dim sums as well as Sushi are good. Butter garlic prawns also worth trying. Green Thai Curry and Khaw Sui are filling. There are very limited dessert options here., name_person=Supriya Devasthali}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=8 months ago, review=Visited Ping’s Café Orient in Lower Parel for a dinner catch-up with friends, and it turned out to be a mixed bag. The place has a cozy, quirky vibe, they’ve got Vietnamese hats hanging on the walls and framed photos that give off travel café aesthetics, which I really liked.

Coming to the food, we tried the drunken noodles, veg SoBo fried rice, veg cheesy dimsums, and veg crackling sushi. The dimsums were the star of the meal, super soft, cheesy, and just the right kind of indulgent. Honestly, I’d go back just for them.

The SoBo fried rice tasted good but was quite dry, and the portion size was underwhelming. The sushi didn’t work for me at all, lacked balance in flavors and texture. We were served rice crackers with five kinds of dips, which was a nice touch, though.

Some of my non-vegetarian friends tried the Thai-style chicken rice, and the feedback wasn’t great, dry and bland, unfortunately. For the six of us, the bill came up to ₹6,000, which felt steep considering the portion sizes.

The staff was polite and welcoming, though they seemed a bit short-handed. Service was decent but could’ve been quicker.

Overall, it’s a cute spot with potential, especially for the ambiance and those heavenly dimsums. But if you’re going for a full meal, don’t expect large portions or consistent quality across the menu.

My family was in Mumbai for several weeks dating at a few 5 star hotels, but our nine days stay at the St Regis was top notch above the rest. The rooms and food were good, the room turnover was seamless (they would slip in quickly whenever you left the room to tidy up without bothering you at all).  The hospital really set them apart. In particular our personal butler services provided by Sweta Biranje made our stay more than a 5 star experience.  Sweta would check in with us regularly to accommodate our needs, she was able to help with anything we needed from car rentals, shopping services, coffee and tea deliveries or anything at all.  She knew it was my father’s birthday and without asking she arranged for a birthday cake and flowers to beset up in his room.  She was outstanding for helping our stay feel special.

The staff overall was great as well. Always helping us wherever they could.

The hotel is also located next to/attached to a mall with good restaurants and shopping.

We will definitely recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a great place to stay.

Jeremiah, name_person=Jeremiah C}", "{guided_block={HOTELS_PILOT_TRAVEL_GROUP_TYPE=Family, HOTELS_PILOT_TRIP_TYPE=Vacation, HOTELS_ASPECT_SERVICES=5, HOTELS_VIBE=[Luxury, E:HOTEL_VIBES_LUXURY, Great_view, E:HOTEL_VIBES_GREAT_VIEW, Romantic, E:HOTEL_VIBES_ROMANTIC, Quiet, E:HOTEL_VIBES_QUIET], HOTELS_ASPECT_LOCATION=5, HOTELS_ASPECT_ROOMS=5}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=We had a great time at the St. Regis, Mumbai recently last week.We had booked two rooms at the hotel. If we return to Mumbai again, we will choose your hotel without hesitation😊❤️, name_person=Polina Dziuba}", "{guided_block={HOTELS_ASPECT_SERVICES=4, HOTELS_ASPECT_LOCATION=5, HOTELS_ASPECT_ROOMS=4}, time_line=a month ago, review=St. Regis Rooftop (Asilo): Unbeatable View, Room for Improvement on the Menu
The St. Regis rooftop offers an experience that is truly unparalleled in Mumbai. The view alone warrants a visit; situated high above the city, the panoramic, open-air setting is absolutely breathtaking, providing a stunning backdrop for any special occasion or evening out. The ambiance is chic, luxurious, and perfectly sets the stage for a world-class night.
However, where the atmosphere and setting are five-star, the food, while good, could certainly be better. For a venue of this caliber and with its premium pricing, the menu items do not consistently reach the level of culinary excellence expected. The dishes are satisfying, but they lack the innovative touch or flawless execution that would truly match the spectacular view.
This venue is absolutely the definitive choice for a night of spectacular views, high-end cocktails, and a beautiful atmosphere. If you are prioritizing ambiance and drinks, you will not be disappointed. But if your primary focus is a world-class meal, it's best to manage expectations regarding the kitchen., name_person=Savvy Sagar}", "{guided_block={HOTELS_PILOT_TRAVEL_GROUP_TYPE=Friends, HOTELS_PILOT_TRIP_TYPE=Business, HOTELS_TIPS_TOPICS=[Nearby_activities, E:HOTEL_TIPS_NEARBY_ACTIVITIES], HOTELS_ASPECT_SERVICES=5, HOTELS_VIBE=[Luxury, E:HOTEL_VIBES_LUXURY], HOTELS_ASPECT_LOCATION=5, HOTELS_ASPECT_ROOMS=5}, time_line=2 months ago, review=The St. Regis Mumbai is a great luxury hotel in a convenient spot. We tried
Blue Mint and Guava Martini- Both the beverages were very refreshing. Must Try.

Kadak Romali- Try this instead of Masala Papad for a change especially if you are in a group of 4-5 ppl. Romali was nice and crispy and freshly chopped onions and tomatoes and fresh sev made it taste delicious.

French Fries- We also tried some fresh fries and it was so fresh and good.

Non Veg Starters
Prawns Butter Garlic- one of the best starters ever. So creamy, buttery and garlicky. If you love garlic in your food, this one is a must try. Loved it.

Chicken tandoori lollipop, Kalimeri Kebab, Kulfi Kebab and Chicken Tikka were served over Barbecue grill and all of these starters were grilled to perfection and marinated well. All of these tasted super good.

Veg Starters
We tried Soya, Panner tikka, Mushroom tikka and baby corn. They were served over the barbecue grill. Mushroom and paneer tikka has to be my favourite among the veg starters.

Non Veg Main Course
We tried chicken angara with some garlic naan. Chicken Angara was served on a sizzler plate with some egg on top. It looked super tempting and tasted delicious. It’s combination with the garlic naan was amazing. Must must must try.

Veg Main Course
We tried the Chilli Garlic Pot Rice. It tasted good but was a bit too spicy for my taste buds. If you enjoy spicy food, you will enjoy this. Else you can try something else from their menu.

Overall everything that we tried tasted delicious and the staff over here is very kind and friendly. ["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=I stumbled upon Doolally Taproom in Khar, and it's a game-changer!

Their menu reads like a love letter to foodies and i happened to have their
- soft, pillowy Mushroom Baos stuffed with Mushroom Kalan, onions, and chutney mayo that'll hug your taste buds.

- Mangalorean Chicken Baos with chicken ghee roast that's buttery, spicy, and smug about it, and burgers that are anything but ordinary.

- Chicken Cheese Blast is a party in a bun, with a chicken patty, cheese, jalapeños, garlic mayo, and crispy onion rings.

- But the real stars of the show are the Achari Paneer Burger, where paneer meets its glow-up era with tangy achari sauce, crisp onions, and gooey cheese.

- Asian BBQ Chicken Burger, an explosion of flavours in one bite with fried chicken, BBQ sauce, cheese, gherkins, and onion rings.

- Pair any of these with Doolally's craft beer, cider, or mead, and you've got a match made in heaven.

Trust me, I died and went to foodie paradise. From the moment you step in, you’re welcomed by an impeccable ambience — a perfect blend of elegance, comfort, and sophistication. The floor-to-ceiling windows and serene sea views add a refreshing openness to the space, making it an ideal spot for both casual evenings and special occasions.

The food is equally impressive — beautifully presented and full of flavor. Whether you’re indulging in light bites or a full meal, the quality and attention to detail are consistent throughout. The drinks menu is well-curated, offering a range of classic cocktails, premium spirits, and innovative concoctions that are crafted to perfection by the skilled bartenders.

The service is exactly what you’d expect from the Taj — warm, attentive, and unobtrusive. Whether you’re meeting friends or winding down after a long day, the Atrium offers a luxurious yet relaxed experience that’s hard to match in the city.

Highly recommended for anyone looking to enjoy great food and drinks in a stunning, tranquil setting., name_person=Dr. Minal Kabra}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a week ago, review=The hospitality given by Ashwini was amazing she was a good host and a very kind soul enjoyed my high tea a lot  helped me taking pictures of the high tea experience .Thanks for the most welcoming and warm hospitality experience., name_person=Zoya Lakdawala}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,000–1,200, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch}, time_line=2 years ago, review=Omg

This cafe really needs to be shut down!, name_person=Kanak Misra}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Other, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a year ago, review=We stayed at the hotel and decided to use the Atrium lounge on a few nights as it was quiet and served drinks until 1am. The atmosphere was good; however, the service and entertainment need significant improvement. The singers were not very good, which sounds harsh, but it's the truth.

The service was the main letdown. Even on quiet nights, when we were literally the only table, the service was extremely slow. One night, it took over 20 minutes to get one whiskey, and a further 35 minutes to get a refill. On the next night, it took over 30 minutes to get two English breakfast teas. However, the bill was produced with record speed—68 seconds when requested one night. On some nights, we didn't even have to request the bill; it was eagerly presented to us with the card machine 20 minutes before closing time. Even though we waited patiently for our drinks, they couldn't extend the same courtesy and let us finish those drinks before requesting payment.

["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Other, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=a week ago, review=Amazing place to hangout with Loved ones and family. All Mocktails are great just ask them to make less sweet!, name_person=Harsh Thanvi}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=1}, time_line=Edited a month ago, review=This place we searched on the net. It's on Google, but getting there could be tricky and you can find yourself inside another resort. So ask, if you get lost . We entered another property from which it showed a road on maps. But that wasnt the restaurant we wanted to go. So someone at that property showed us the way to sea breeze which was via the beach itself, we were pretty amazed to drive on the firm sand. We reached sea breeze and wer were the only ones. The crew running the place were soft spoken nepali boys. They gave us the menu which was vast, but since it was just reopening they said they don't have a lot which is there. We decided to go with pizza and peri peri, which they suggested. Sadly, they don't have filtered / regular drinking water and we used our own regular home water. The food came in some time and we spend that time looking around the property which is bang on the beach. Played with the thin dogs there and a good chat. The pizza was decent and peri-peri very very spicy. Since we hate wasting food, we finished what we ordered.  The crew was well dressed and they spoke well, which was what we found good. The music was loud so we told them to reduce the volume. They informed us, that the water doesn't come till the entrance but sometimes it does. They thus inform the guests priorly, of the same and we checked the tide. We were in safe zone and sighed a breath, so if you are here, make sure you ask them of the tide. We bid farewell to the dogs who came till the entrance to see us off. The road to this place, has mostly no light and limited network, so make sure you download the map in advance when you arrive. There are not many sign boards, but you would find sign boards to the beach. The road is also narrow at several places, so drive slowly, safely, with your belts on and eyes to the road. I forgot, they didn't have any dessert ., name_person=WinNie}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=8 months ago, review=Liked this beachside restaurant only the serve time is too long.On one hand, the setting was absolutely stunning – the sound of the waves, the salty air, and the views of the ocean were all incredibly romantic. And the food, when it finally arrived, was delicious. But, oh man, the service was glacial.

We were eager to enjoy the sunset and a leisurely dinner.We waited for what felt like an eternity for our appetizers, and even longer for our main courses. By the time our food arrived, we were all starving and a bit cranky.
The food itself was great, with plenty of options,But the slow service really put a damper on our experience.

Welcome- Greeted well upon arrival. Give choice of tables to seat.

Ambiance - The restaurant is exquisitely adorned with a striking red and black color scheme, evoking an upscale Asian aesthetic. The expansive interior boasts high ceilings and thoughtfully arranged, well-spaced tables, ensuring a sense of privacy for our guests.

Food - The cuisine did not entirely meet my expectations, as I had anticipated a more refined presentation. However, for those who appreciate a richer preparation, it may be quite enjoyable, as it was for the rest of my family.
Recommend Dish - Turnip Cake

The interiors are lavishly done with gorgeous high ceilings and tasteful wall and ceiling decor.

We were there for lunch on a Saturday. The music was pleasant and not at all intrusive. Service was efficient enough. They didn’t have a detailed cocktail/drinks menu yet, but served as per our preference. Slightly better than average portion sizes for the appetisers.

1. Hunan lobster - Fresh and tasted brilliant - 5/5

2. Aromatic lamb - v soft and nicely cooked lamb with konjee sauce and sesame - 5/5

3. Coffee and chocolate cheesecake - I wasn’t too keen on the desserts they had, so the manager Talha went out of his way to get us this cheesecake from one of the other restaurants. Really wonderful and yum! - 5/5

We loved it!, name_person=Nadia Halim Dziobkowska}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservations not required, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=5 months ago, review=Tucked away in Bandra’s ever-evolving culinary landscape, Napoli by Shatranj presents itself as a polished neighbourhood Italian eatery. But despite the charming name and the promise of a thoughtfully curated Italian menu, the experience left more to be desired than remembered.

The meal started on a reasonably positive note. The Spaghetti Carbonara arrived with a creamy, well-emulsified sauce that clung nicely to the strands of pasta. The presence of pork gave the dish some much-needed body and savouriness, though it was hard to tell if guanciale was used. The overall flavour was pleasant, if unremarkable, and the dish did what it needed to without dazzling.

Unfortunately, the meal only declined from there.

The Steak, requested medium rare, did arrive at the correct doneness, which deserves acknowledgement. But that’s where the positives end. The cut of meat itself was a poor choice—tough, chewy, and devoid of the tenderness one expects from a properly sourced and rested steak. For a dish that typically commands a premium on any menu, this one felt more like an afterthought than a main event.

The Salmon Bruschetta fared no better. Topped with pallid, clearly farmed salmon that lacked freshness, the dish suffered from a lack of depth and definition. The cream which is meant to support or complement actually ended up dominating the plate. The result was a bland, vaguely fishy bite that could have come from any cold appetiser counter rather than a kitchen claiming Italian sophistication.

And therein lies the central issue with Napoli by Shatranj. While it gestures toward authenticity and finesse, the food rarely lands with the kind of precision or character that might distinguish it. The pricing, meanwhile, reflects a confidence that the food does not back up. At best, it feels like another stylish Bandra restaurant with a name borrowed from Naples but very little of its soul.

In the end, Napoli by Shatranj is not a terrible meal, but it’s a forgettable one—and that might be worse., name_person=Mithun Mohandas}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=The menu had a wide variety of options, and the food was simply delicious.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Being vegetarian, this place served me the best spaghetti pasta I could ask for.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Good food, great service, convenient location, great ambience}"]

However the food wasn’t upto the mark at all and didn’t feel worth the price.

The chocolate croissant we had was dry and stale. They were kind enough to replace it , however the replaced croissant wasn’t fresh either.

The lemon grass tea felt more like ginger tea in taste.

The pizza was decent but the crust felt like pita bread and was extremely crispy., name_person=Jiten Davda}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=Edited a month ago, review=Ananda Cafe is a wonderful slice of calm in the madness that in Mumbai. If you enjoy places that reverberates spiritually then this is the perfect place to spend time connecting with your dear ones, simply sipping a coffee contemplating or even meditating.

The hosts add to the joyous nature of the cafe, especially Mafalda who ensured that we meet our goal of having a great time. It wasn't easy, with us being 8 temperamental adults and all - but she approached us with a calming smile and guided us in placing the perfect order of food and beverage.

We especially enjoyed the Avocado Burrata Salad with Mango Sauce and the coffee! We are sure to visit Ananda Cafe - as a collective and individually - many many times in the future.

Thank you to the owners for creating this lovely sanctuary., name_person=Paramveer Bhatti}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Other, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹400–600, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Surya_Smoothie], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=8 months ago, review=This cafe is located near Juhu beach with decor that resonates with yoga and mindfulness themes, creating an ideal space for relaxation.​
