reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Somewhat recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,000–1,200, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING, Kid-friendliness, E:KID_FRIENDLINESS, Wheelchair_accessibility, E:ACCESSIBILITY], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Delivery, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Difficult to find parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=Up to 10 min}, time_line=a month ago, review=Sandeep Bar and Restaurant used to be one of the best places in Mulund — both for food and service. Sadly, it’s not the same anymore. The service has gone from excellent to absolutely terrible. The manager is extremely rude and doesn’t even bother to answer calls. When I tried calling to complain about an incorrect order, he hung up on me mid-conversation — very unprofessional.

The food quality has also gone down noticeably. The ingredients don’t taste as fresh as they once did, and the overall flavor has become quite average.

But the biggest disappointment is the attitude of the staff and management. They clearly don’t care about regular or family customers anymore — it feels like they only want to cater to drunkards.

It’s sad to see such a reputed restaurant lose its charm because of poor management and arrogance. I genuinely hope they improve, but for now, I wouldn’t recommend this place to anyone., name_person=Vinod}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 months ago, review=Sea Food is amazing. ["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹200–400, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[2_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=5 months ago, review=Fresh – Sector 17, Vashi, Navi Mumbai

If you're craving the best chaat in town, look no further than Fresh in Sector 17, Vashi. Tucked away near 3XCX+RGP, this place has become a local favorite for good reason!

The star of the show here is definitely the chaat — from crispy Shev Puri to tangy Dahi Puri and perfectly balanced Bhel Puri, every bite is bursting with authentic flavor. Freshness (as the name promises) and generous portions make it a total value-for-money experience.

But that’s not all — Fresh also has a great selection of Mango Mastani, thick milkshakes, and classic ice creams to cool you down, especially on a hot Navi Mumbai day. Whether you’re in the mood for a light snack or a sweet treat, they’ve got you covered.

The place is clean, service is quick, and the overall vibe is casual and comfortable. It’s ideal for a quick stop with friends or a family outing.

In short, Fresh is a must-visit if you're anywhere near Vashi — especially if you're a fan of traditional Indian street-style snacks with a hygienic twist!, name_person=atish aundhkar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1–200, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=5 months ago, review=Open sitting good. The rava dosa, with its spiced chili flakes, added an exciting twist to the traditional dish.\\n\\nDuring our visit, the atmosphere was alive with laughter and conversation, making it a joyous setting to enjoy a meal. Food & Drinks:
I started with their Paneer Manchurian Chili Dry – crispy, spicy, and full of flavor – and their Margherita Pizza, which had the perfect thin crust with fresh basil and gooey cheese.

For drinks, I tried their Red Wine and Pina Colada. The wine was smooth and served at the right temperature, and the Pina Colada was creamy, tropical, and refreshing – an absolute treat!

For the main course, I ordered the Paneer Afghani, Matka Biryani, Kadhai Paneer, and Butter Naan. Every dish was rich in flavor and perfectly cooked. name: Freny's - All day dining & bar
reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=2 months ago, review=We recently visited Freny’s All Day Dining Bar on Linking Road, Bandra West, and absolutely loved the experience! The space is warm, inviting, and thoughtfully designed — it truly feels like walking into someone’s charming East Indian home.
The interiors are a beautiful blend of retro, European, Portuguese, and East Indian décor — from pastel colors and vintage chandeliers to framed family photos and wallpapered ceilings. The ground floor gives off cosy café vibes, while the upper floor offers a more formal dining space with a well-stocked bar and nostalgic touches throughout. Every corner tells a story!
We tried a variety of items and everything was delicious:
Mocktails: Chocolate Skyline, Boozy Bougie Pop, Rose Ciel – all refreshing and unique!
Desserts: Tiramisu Dreamin, Caramel Apple, Cheese Basque Cake, Jardin Du Rose, and the star of the show — Matilda’s Chocolate Cake. Rich, moist, and absolutely unforgettable — hands down one of the best cakes we’ve had!
They also serve traditional East Indian dishes like fugiyas, alongside modern café-style fare including pizzas, burgers, and salads — offering something for everyone.
If you’re in Bandra, Freny’s is a must-visit spot for its heartwarming ambiance, nostalgic charm, and standout food & drinks. Can’t wait to go, name_person=amin shaikh}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=I had to experience this place cause it serves Traditional East Indian food!

We tried their Fugiya’s which are sweet and tasty. Then Fish Thali, Chicken Thali, Mutton Thaali, Prawns Thaali, Tiger Prawns with Curry and Peters Mitton Curry with Wedding Rice. Dessert must try is Fernandez Rocher.

The food and the East Indian vibe here is so comforting. You must go with your Friends and Family!, name_person=Renuka B (taste_toh_karo)}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Indoor_dining_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_INDOOR_DINING_AREA], GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,400–1,600, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Parking, E:PARKING, Kid-friendliness, E:KID_FRIENDLINESS, Wheelchair_accessibility, E:ACCESSIBILITY], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=A fine done restaurant apt for the locality. Great ambiance, good seating. Upper floor has some good views of the road.
Service is nice, staff is helpful.
Almost nothing to complain.
Menu is limited, which is a good thing. And every dish is will give you long lasting taste on your buds.
Portion size is sufficient for 2 people.
Wide variety of unique cocktails available.
Bar is on the upper floor with plenty for choice.
Prices are obviously on higher side considering the locality., name_person=Ha Ma Jo}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Fugiyas_with_Mustard_Garlic_Butter_Dip, Potato_Chop], GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=It was a pleasure dining at Freny's today with my boys. The ambience is full of warmth and coziness. The staff so courteous and polite. Special mention and thanks to Sankalp.
And what can I say about the food. Must visit to experience it. Thankyou @ Freny's.
Will visit soon..., name_person=Asha Pinto}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=8 months ago, review=We visited Freny's today and really appreciated the cozy ambiance and welcoming atmosphere. The kale, mango, and prawn salad was fresh and refreshing—perfect for the season. However, the fish and chips were not as enjoyable, as the fish didn’t seem fresh and was over-fried an dried. The pork belly taco was also disappointing, as it consisted mostly of fat with very little meat, which didn’t feel like good value for the price. Unfortunately, the food quality did not meet our expectations., name_person=Osmund Dcunha}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,000–1,200, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=a month ago, review=My first visit to the restaurant and i was happy with both ambiance and service, especially Govinda.Being pork lover, I tried Pork Indyal and chocolate eclair. They gave 2 pieces of fugiyas to taste complimentary,but charged Rs. 50 for 2 pavs which are available in market for Rs.3 each- at Rs 620/- plus gst for pork dish they could have atleast gave the 2 pavs free instead of promoting free fugiyas. The pork Indyal however was excellent in taste with really succulent pork pieces and flavoursome east indian style gravy. I dare say the best pork dish in mumbai. Eclair though was okay and would suggest to load caramal sauce topping in a warm drizzle to lift the dish. Deffinetly worth a visit if you have not tried before and well stocked bar too., name_person=Ghanashyam Shanbhag}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=1}, time_line=8 months ago, review=I just had “Easter Set Menu” at Freny’s in Bandra at ₹2200/- per person and it was extremely BAD.. if you’re planning to go there for a meal I highly DO NOT recommend this place at all. Worst looking and tasking sorpotel I have ever seen or had in my lifetime!  And not even one dish from the menu was worth ordering as second serving. We didn’t even feel like taking picture of all the food (maybe i should have atleast to post it here for everyone to see for themselves!!) Pls don’t go by thier “Insta” reels and pictures of the meal. Unfortunately we fell for it and wasted our money. Also while they had taken some Advance payment from me to “confirm” my seats.. since they had loads of booking for tonight apparently, however it was only myself and my Friend who had booked the Easter menu, the restaurant was empty! The owner and or the manager didn’t even bother to check if we like the food of not! The worst Pastel de Nata we’ve had. Absolutely nothing was close to even “good” forget being excellent in taste. Never ever going back here, I’ve even unfollowed their page on insta. Only fancy reels and interiors with no value for customer’s money and experience., name_person=Shipra Shetty}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,800–2,000, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=Edited 7 months ago, review=Was thinking of my East Indian ancestors recently and thought of having their kind of food, so I travelled to Bandruh... Not to offend my Goan ancestors, but I've always preferred pork vindaloo the East Indian way. And that's exactly what I ordered... Pork vindaloo or indyal with the very much missed and loved fuggias. I guess Freny's must have read my mind and even offered a complimentary fuggias just for me in addition to what I had already ordered. Not complaining at all!! 😁 Washed it all down with LIIT and later some water. It's nice having an East Indian place to go to in the city when you have a craving., name_person=Melinda Warty}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=It largely has the regular Italian dishes, pizza and pasta.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Loved the place -atmosphere, food , decor .}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=The ambience was loved by my family and the service was exceptional.}"]

Staff are polite and friendly., name_person=Lisette Fernandes}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,000–1,200, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=2}, time_line=6 months ago, review=We were a group of 13 people for sunday lunch. When we walked in at 1:30 pm, we were the only ones there. But soon it started filling up. We ordered 4 plates of hummus with 2 pita breads per plate. And then we ordered 2 of this 1 in all thaal or platter. Food was ok ok. Nothing turkish about it except for the hummus that we ordered separately.

The most disappointing part was their ambiance. It was hot and their air conditioners were non functional. Which they kept denying. Every time we told them to decrease the temperature, they would take the remote control in their hands and pretend to do their best. But that was not the case. After the crowd filling up, it really got warm and by then we had eaten our lunch, which added to the heat.

In all, not a good experience considering we went for Turkish cuisine but like I said, except for the hummus and pita bread, nothing was Turkish here., name_person=qahera sayed}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,000–1,200, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Free_parking_lot, E:PARKING_OPTION_FREE_PARKING_LOT], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Plenty of parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=4 weeks ago, review=We are so grateful that this restaurant is in bandra.

actually we used to go all the way from worli to kharghar to eat authentic Turkish naili barra and chaap, but we've got the same dish in bandra @ Turkey junction.

Their signature item mutton naili barra is a must try.

The ambiente is so nice, they even have dastarkhana for bigger family groups.

The staff are also very good here, they keep on suggesting things and ask about feedback on the food items.

Overall it was a very nice experience.

Looking forward to visit this place soon., name_person=VaruN AnanD}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Chicken_Meter_Kebab, Uzun_Mix_Platter], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Dietary_restrictions, E:OTHER_DIETARY_RESTRICTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a year ago, review=My first visit. My wife was here once before so she repeated the same order. A massive platter (see pic) that's enough to serve a full meal for 4/6/8 people. You can choose. It was great this format. Add a Butter roti to go with the gravy dish. You don't need to order anything more. I will be back for specific dishes later... And deserts, they were out of Shahi Tukda... Guys you can't run out of special deserts. The dress code of the speciality is noteworthy and gives you a feel of the country food you are eating.
You can choose to sit down and eat in a room in classic style as well., name_person=Rohit Srivastava}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3}, time_line=2 years ago, review=Food is good, pricing is just fine, and the decor is also decent, but the same decency vanished from the servers. name: Raghusiya - Udupi Bistro
reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹400–600, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING, Wheelchair_accessibility, E:ACCESSIBILITY], GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Plenty of parking, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=30-60 min, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Menu_is_all_vegetarian, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_COMPLETELY_VEGETARIAN]}, time_line=a month ago, review=A Tale of Two Visits: From Disappointment to Delight at Raghusiya!

I recently had the opportunity to visit Raghusiya twice, with a short span in between, and I must say, the transformation is nothing short of remarkable!

My first visit was on Gudi Padwa, just a few days after their opening. Unfortunately, the experience was a letdown. The service was painfully slow, the food was subpar, and the staff seemed lost. I was disappointed, to say the least.

Fast forward to my second visit today, and I'm thrilled to report that Raghusiya has turned the corner! The service was prompt, attentive, and the hospitality from the managers was truly heart-winning. The food, which was a major letdown earlier, was now delicious and thoroughly enjoyable. The Khousey soup was a standout, with the perfect balance of lemongrass and galangal that made it aromatic and flavorful.

The ambience is welcoming, pleasant, and well-lit, making it an excellent spot for a fine dining experience. While the prices may be on the higher side, the quality of food and service more than makes up for it.

Kudos to the team at Raghusiya for taking feedback seriously and working tirelessly to improve. I'm impressed, and I'm sure others will be too! If you're looking for a great dining experience, give Raghusiya a shot. You won't be disappointed!, name_person=Dr. Nayan Bheda}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 months ago, review=I recently visited here and I was honestly impressed! The place is so spacious — perfect for family gatherings, birthdays, and kitty parties. They serve pure veg and Jain food, which makes it a great choice for everyone.

We started with their mocktails — Blue Sea and Spicy Guava. Both were refreshing, but Spicy Guava was definitely our favourite!

For starters, we tried Benne Dosa, Idli Wada, Cigar Rolls and Paneer Tikka — all perfectly cooked and full of flavour.

In the main course, we had Paneer Lapeta Sabzi with naan — super delicious! And their Chef Special Sizzler was a must-try, served sizzling hot and absolutely yummy.

For dessert, we ended on a sweet note with Raja Rani — a rich combination of dry fruits, ice cream, and brownie. So indulgent!

Overall, a fantastic place for pure veg food lovers — definitely worth visiting✨, name_person=Ishita Jain}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Breakfast, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹200–400, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Free_of_charge_parking_lot, E:PARKING_OPTION_FREE_PARKING_LOT, Free_of_charge_street_parking, E:PARKING_OPTION_FREE_STREET_PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Plenty of parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=4 months ago, review=Raghusiya - Udupi Bistro is a great spot for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. The food is delicious and satisfying. Quantity is sufficient, no need to worry about portion sizes. Ambiance is neat and clean, perfect for family and friends. Service is good, staff is friendly and attentive. They also offer convenient street parking facility. Overall experience was fantastic, highly recommended. Breakfast options are varied and tasty. The property itself is grand and beautifully curated, giving a premium, rich vibe the moment you walk in. What stood out equally was the staff—everyone we interacted with was cordial, attentive, and genuinely willing to help.

A lovely surprise for us was that many staff members spoke Marathi, which is my mother tongue. It instantly made my family feel comfortable, especially since they aren’t very fluent in Hindi or English.

Coming to the food—absolutely sumptuous. There’s a great spread across Indian and Continental options. I especially loved the salad section—never thought I’d say this, but the salads were genuinely delicious and well-crafted. Desserts were awesome, and my daughter thoroughly enjoyed the entire dinner.

Overall, a wonderful place for a family celebration, and I’ll definitely recommend Earth Plate to others., name_person=Ninad Patil}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=4 months ago, review=Onam Sadhya at Sahara Star – A Feast of Tradition and Luxury

Celebrating the spirit of Onam in the grandeur of Sahara Star was truly a delightful experience. The plush property, located right next to Mumbai’s domestic airport, set the perfect stage for a festive indulgence. The lavish Sunday Brunch at The Earth Plate – Global Cuisine transformed into a traditional Kerala Sadhya spread, offering an authentic taste of heritage served with warmth and elegance.

The banana leaf thali came alive with a vibrant array of curries, pachadis, thorans, avial, olan, sambar, rasam, pulisery, and fluffy red rice – each dish bursting with homely flavors, perfectly balanced spices, and that comforting touch of Kerala’s culinary roots. Crisp papadams, tangy pickles, and steaming hot appams completed the meal, while payasam and other Indian sweets brought the feast to a heavenly close.

The buffet around the restaurant was equally indulgent, showcasing a harmony of regional Indian delicacies, global favorites, and stunning desserts – all beautifully curated in a festive floral setting that reflected the joy of Onam. The live counters, attentive chefs, and vibrant ambiance added to the overall charm, making it an immersive dining experience.

✨ From the soulful flavors on the leaf to the elegant hospitality and plush surroundings, the Onam Sadhya at Sahara Star was more than just a meal – it was a cultural celebration plated with luxury. A must-experience brunch that beautifully bridges tradition with fine dining in the heart of Mumbai., name_person=Harshad Dhamankar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservations recommended, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING, Kid-friendliness, E:KID_FRIENDLINESS], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Plenty of parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Vegetarian_menu_or_section, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_SEPARATE_MENU_SECTION]}, time_line=4 months ago, review=It's a beyond beautiful and by now nostalgia experience for us ❤️. Environment inside is mesmerizing... Kids enjoy the buffet. The Sahara Star is by now and emotional bond for us❣️ Staff is super caring and professional.

The staff at the restaurant also performed their duties with quality and care.

Kudos to everyone involved!

As for recommendations, the dishes I would suggest are:

- sichuan chili crab with fried bun / i request without wine  - deep fried chicken dumpling

. Super tasty..service impeccable..

Must try.

Review:

I rarely leave negative reviews, but unfortunately, my experience at [Hotel Name] fell far below expectations.

From the moment I arrived, things started off poorly. Check-in was disorganized and slow, with staff seeming overwhelmed and uninterested in helping guests. The location itself is unbeatable – right opposite Marine Drive, with a perfect view of the sea that makes dining even more special.

I tried their **half-and-half veg pizza**, and it turned out to be an excellent choice. The base was thin, crisp, and baked just right – not chewy or soggy. On one half, I went for the **classic veg toppings** (tomatoes, capsicum, onions, and olives), which had a fresh and vibrant flavor. The other half was **loaded with gourmet toppings**, with a rich cheesy layer, mushrooms, and bell peppers that gave a nice savory balance.

What stood out was the **quality of the cheese** – creamy, stretchy, and not too oily – and the **balance of spices and herbs**, which kept it flavorful without overpowering the freshness of the vegetables. Portion size is good enough to share if you’re not a heavy eater.

The **ambience** is calm and elegant with the sea breeze adding charm. Service was decent and staff courteous, though the place can get busy, especially in the evenings. Pricing is slightly on the higher side, but the taste, quality, and overall experience justify it.

✅ **Highlights**:

* Great sea-facing view
* Perfectly baked thin crust
* Fresh veggies & quality cheese
* Half-and-half option gives a variety in one pizza

⚠️ **Minor Cons**:

* Slightly pricey
* Gets crowded during peak hours, name_person=Mayur Aundhakar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,000–1,200, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=Up to 10 min}, time_line=3 weeks ago, review=Came for midnight dinner. Basilico in Colaba has built quite a reputation over the years, which is why I was genuinely looking forward to the experience. Unfortunately, it turned out to be one of those places where the hype no longer matches the reality.

We ordered the lemon coriander soup, which was a letdown right from the first sip – it lacked any real flavor of lemon or coriander. reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Somewhat recommend, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,800–2,000, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[2_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO, 3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=Visited Across, Kala Ghoda and had a really warm and comforting dining experience. We ordered quite a few dishes — Pomelo Bliss, Fresh Lime Water, Fry Bread, Mushroom Choila, Mustang Black Dal, Ghee Rice, and the Mountain Road Brownie. The food reflects the authentic flavours of the Himalayan region, and you can taste the use of mustard oil in certain dishes, which gives it a very homely, regional touch.

The staff surprised us with a complimentary Churpi Cheese Dip with crisps while the Mustang Black Dal was getting prepared. Churpi cheese is traditionally made in Himalayan regions — slightly smoky, chewy, and packed with natural flavour. The dip version they served was delicious and definitely worth trying! Honestly, the fact that they offered it complimentary because the dal was taking time (I’m guessing they make it fresh) felt very thoughtful and added to the experience.

We weren’t drinking alcohol, but based on how good the Pomelo Bliss mocktail was, I’m guessing their cocktails would be quite interesting too.

The place is slightly on the pricier side, but since we were celebrating our first date anniversary, it felt completely worth it. Overall, a cosy spot with great service and flavourful, comforting Himalayan cuisine — definitely a memorable meal!, name_person=Ketki Yash}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,200–1,400, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[2_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=Up to 10 min}, time_line=5 months ago, review=Across in Kala Ghoda, Mumbai, is brought to life by Viraf Patel and Prakriti Lama, who traveled the Eastern Himalayas to craft a menu celebrating its rugged flavors.

The restaurant specializes in Himalayan cuisine, blending traditional ingredients with modern techniques. Expect authentic dishes from Nepal, Bhutan, and Northeast India, featuring bold spices, local produce, and unique pairings

.Cocktails: The cocktails are a highlight, with the Mezcal Negroni stealing the show—smoky, balanced, and served with homemade Churpi cheese, elevating the experience

Fing Salad: A vibrant mix of greens and herbs, punched up with a zesty, umami-rich dressing, beautifully presented for a fresh, flavorful bite.

Veg Momos: Juicy, perfectly steamed dumplings bursting with flavor, paired with a tangy, spicy dip that adds a fiery kick.

Fry Bread: A unique treat with gooey Kalimpong cheese, drizzled with spicy honey dip for a delightful sweet-spicy balance.

Solu White Beans Hummus: A creamy, standout dish made from Himalayan white beans, topped with oyster mushrooms and fried onions, served with “insecurity bread” for scooping.

Bhatti Chicken: Slow-roasted chicken cubes marinated in roasted cumin and Nepali spices, served on puffed rice with fried onions—tender and packed with flavor.

Prawns in Mustang Jimbu: Perfectly cooked prawns with garlic, chili, and Himalayan wild chives, offering a fresh, aromatic twist.

Mustang Black Dal: The star of the menu, this Himalayan delicacy is a soulful, slow-cooked black dal served with ghee-infused rice and condiments—a hearty, comforting meal.

While there was a variety of drinks and milkshakes on the menu,the only downside I found was none of them were carbonated or aerated, which could be a drawback for those who prefer such options.

reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹600–800, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Free_parking_lot, E:PARKING_OPTION_FREE_PARKING_LOT, Free_street_parking, E:PARKING_OPTION_FREE_STREET_PARKING, Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET, Free_parking_garage, E:PARKING_OPTION_FREE_PARKING_GARAGE], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Vegetarian_menu_or_section, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_SEPARATE_MENU_SECTION, Clearly_labeled_vegetarian_dishes, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_CLEARLY_LABELED_ITEMS]}, time_line=Edited 2 weeks ago, review=Had an amazing dining experience at Chowman Andheri West!
From veg and non-veg starters to mains, gravies, desserts and drinks everything was absolutely top-notch. The flavors were rich, authentic and perfectly balanced, especially their Kolkata-style chilli chicken, drums of heaven, baos, momos, fried rice, noodles and khao suey.

The ambiance is beautiful with comfortable indoor and outdoor seating. Service was super fast, friendly and very professional. Great quality, generous portions and pocket-friendly prices make this place a must-visit for Asian food lovers.

Highly recommended for an unforgettable Chinese & Asian dining experience!, name_person=ABHITHEFOODIE}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=Chowman is located in Andheri West and it is near the Andheri Sports Complex and on the main road hence easy to find.

This brand hails from Kolkata and they have their presence in multiple cities. This particular outlet has indoor and outdoor seatings available and they have used the space nicely. The decor is decent and the overall vibe of the restaurant is nice.

The menu here is one of the best as they have covered a lot of items. The variety available is amazing and pricing is not high. The quantity and quality of whatever we tried was excellent. They also have a kids menu plus they run various offers too.

We went here for dinner and the kitchen service was on time. Special thanks to Staff Dhiraj & Santanu as they knew the menu well and they were attentive and proactive.

What We Had -
APPETISERS~
Doremon’s Beloved Red Chicken -
From the kids menu. This was honey sesame chicken. Taste wise good however too crispy hence hard and chewy. Need improvement.

Smokey Chicken -
Chicken tossed in garlic chilli based sauce tasted really good. Loved the juicy chicken and the smokey flavours of the chilli was good plus the garlic didn’t had strong taste.

Kolkata Style Chilli Shrimp -
One of the best shrimp dish. Tossed in soy sauce again not with overpowering flavours this dish was tasted really good. The fresh prawns, the crunchy outer layer and the sauce was this dish excellent.

MAINS~
Pan Fried Noodles -
Again one of the best pan fired noodles experience. Lightly fried noodled with soy based gravy, veggies, chicken and prawns. Trust me this is a must try as it tasted outstanding.

Chowman’s Special Rice with Hong Kong Chicken Gravy -
Rice with egg, chicken and prawns paired with hot Hong Kong gravy was soul satisfying. Loved the combination and taste wise both the dishes were excellent.

DESSERT~
Chocolate Mousse -
The mousse was chocolatey and creamy plus it was fresh and wasn’t too sweet. Hence tasted delicious.

BEVERAGES~
Thai Lemonade.
Sparkling Blueberry.
Both the drinks tasted nice and paired nicely with the food.

So our meal at Chowman Andheri West was one of the best Chinese food experiences I’ve had. They also run dine in offers so do check that before going. Highly recommended and a must try., name_person=Shaikh Khalid Sarfaraz}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹400–600, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=Kolkata based chinese brand now in Mumbai. Welcome to Chowman. The place has some delicious chinese food ( both veg and nonveg). The place is Walking distance from Azad Nagar metro station. The ambiance of this place is great, having both indoors as well as outdoor seating arrangements. Let's talk about food, in food we tried Drums of Heaven, Chicken Dimsum, Veg fried Rice, Crispy corn, Prawns Garlic, Bassa fish which are all delicious. We started with the Crab Meat Soup, and it was rich, comforting, and full of flavor. The Schezwan Crab Whole was a complete showstopper—spicy, tangy, and perfectly cooked. The Chicken Lollipop was crispy on the outside, juicy inside, and paired so well with the dips.
Seafood lovers will really enjoy the Fried Squid in Sweet Chilli Sauce—it had the perfect balance of heat and sweetness. The Beckti Fish in Green Curry was another highlight, fragrant and creamy, with delicate fish that just melted in the mouth. They serve veg and non-veg both

Please visit and enjoy, name_person=Amandeep Singh}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Smokey Chicken - Chicken tossed in garlic chilli based sauce tasted really good.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Chinese cuisine and some thai food available here... food is really tasty 😋}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Non-Veg Combo – Generous portion, hygienically packed, enough for 3-4 people.}"]

Tucked away in the heart of Bandra, this space feels less like a cafe and more like a minimalist sanctuary—the perfect backdrop for a date that requires no rush, just good conversation and even better plates.
The afternoon light here hits differently, and the menu is curated to match that relaxed, "slow living" energy.

• Guacamole - Feta Hash Brown: We started here, and it was a revelation in texture. The hash brown offered a deafening, golden crunch that played perfectly against the cool, creamy richness of the guacamole. Conveniently located at just a short walk from Link Road or Metro stations, the place is easy to spot, with warm lighting and lush greenery that instantly draw you in.

The establishment is modern and chic, with open seating curated with a green, refreshing ambiance. It also offers an air-conditioned section featuring ambient lighting and a minimalistic design. The stacked bar looks great tucked into a corner, overlooking a comfortable sofa setup ideal for larger groups. The overall feels are chill, gram-worthy, and genuinely perfect for a date or family meet-ups.

We visited for a midweek dinner and to our surprise, the place already had a decent crowd, so a reservation is recommended. The staff was courteous and professional, and they offered us a nice table.

The pop playlist was soft, and we quickly got chatting while browsing the beautifully designed cocktail menu. The food menu lists down the ingredients and features a mix of Indian, Asian, and continental dishes, while the servers were always at hand to describe each item, making it much easier to order. We sampled :

-Virgin Mojito : Standard but well made. Arrived promptly. Apt choice to pair with starters.

-Ghost Chilli Chicken : Delicious and succulent, the chicken was char grilled to perfection. Served with a mango based chutney. Not as spicy as the name suggests.

-Spinach, Chilli & Ricotta Stuffed Mushrooms : Button mushrooms stuffed with fresh ricotta and spinach served on a bed of chilli tomato puree. Filling and crafty, the green apple and cinnamon chutney brings out the flavours.

-Spicy Prawns Tempura : Classic tempura, good size and crunch. Dynamite sauce does the trick.

-Mercado Verduras : Thin base with exotic toppings like sundried tomatoes, brocolli and olives. Rocket leaves sprinkled on top adding freshness and texture but may not be everyone's cup of tea.

-Black Pepper Rice Bowl : Sticky rice served with black pepper prawns gravy with a kick. Savoury aftertaste lingers for a while. Portion good enough for two.

-Mutton Kheema Pav : Perfectly cooked mutton with sunny side up egg on top for adding a runny buttery balance. Recommended and loved it !

-Biscoff Cheesecake : Light, creamy and delectable. Not overly sweet like traditional Biscoff desserts which makes it more bingeworthy !

-Gooey Brownie with Ice Cream : on house melt in the mouth brownie. One of the best we've tried in Mumbai for sure ! You cannot miss this !

The owner of the place is passionate about food and hospitality and it shows. Guest feedback is well appreciated and this gracious approach instantly makes the place worth visiting again.

To conclude, whether you're stepping in for a casual catch-up or a special night out, Feast & Fable's inviting upbeat vibe, lipsmacking food and great service make it an exciting choice for anyone exploring the neighborhood. Highly recommended by popular foodie Kunal Vijaykar, you cant go wrong with Gurukrupa, name_person=swayambharat}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Indoor_dining_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_INDOOR_DINING_AREA], GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 months ago, review=We recently visited Gurukrupa Restaurant in Powai, and it turned out to be such a delightful experience! The place has a warm and welcoming vibe, and the staff truly know how to make you feel comfortable from the moment you step in. Their hospitality was genuinely impressive — polite, attentive, and quick with service.

We ordered "Kori Roti" and "Fried Rice", and both dishes exceeded our expectations. The Kori Roti was absolutely authentic — rich, flavorful, and perfectly spiced with that signature Mangalorean touch. You could taste the freshness and effort put into every bite. The Fried Rice was equally delicious — perfectly cooked, aromatic, and packed with flavor. Together, the combination was simply mouthwatering.

The restaurant maintains great hygiene and offers a cozy, family-friendly environment that makes dining here enjoyable and relaxed. Prices are reasonable for the quality and taste they deliver.

Overall, Gurukrupa Restaurant is a gem in Powai — ideal for anyone who loves authentic South Indian and coastal food. Will definitely be visiting again soon!, name_person=Likhith Salian}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=Just had an absolutely incredible dining experience at Gurukripa, and I'm still thinking about that food! Bombil Fry - Crispy, perfectly seasoned Bombay duck that was simply divine. Fresh fish, well-marinated, and fried to perfection.

Mysore Donne Chicken Biryani- This deserves a paragraph of its own! Served in the traditional donne (cup), the biryani was aromatic, flavorful, and the chicken was tender. Authentic Mysore style all the way.

Mangalorean Mutton Rayalseema - Tender mutton with robust spices. The meat was cooked beautifully and just fell off the bone.

Neer Dosa (2 orders!) - Soft, lacy, and perfect to scoop up all those amazing gravies
Prawns Pulimunchi - Tangy and spicy, exactly how it should be
Gad bad (Full) - A delightful end to the meal!

The Kingfisher Draught (2 glasses) paired perfectly with the spicy food. Even the basics like Steam Rice and Kokum Cooler were spot-on.

Service: Quick and efficient - they managed to get all 16 items to our table hot and fresh.

Value: With the variety and quality we got, absolutely worth every rupee!

However, while the ambience is impressive, the food was just okay. The dishes were decent but didn't quite live up to my expectations in terms of flavor. That said, the variety on the menu is good, so there’s plenty to choose from.

Pom Passion- A pomegranate, passion fruit and oirange mixer refreshing drink.

Coco Berry-A fusion of coconut, cranberry and vodka.

Note - please carry odomos if you are planning to visit this place., name_person=Jackie Fernandes}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in}, time_line=2 years ago, review=We recently had the pleasure of dining at the newly opened BYOB Please in Thane, and the experience left us highly impressed. This unique concept of bringing your own bottle and pairing it with their delightful cuisine is a winning formula.

The open-air dining setup added to the charm, making it a perfect spot for gatherings with friends and family. We were especially thrilled to find that they were screening live matches during this ongoing World Cup season. Enjoying your meal while watching your favorite sports just takes the experience to another level.

What made our visit even more enjoyable was their live music program, which is a regular feature here. Every week, they host live music sessions, and it added a delightful touch to our evening.

Let's talk about the food. The menu boasts a diverse range of cuisines, including Chinese, seafood, and North Indian dishes. We sampled a bit of everything, and each dish was a culinary delight. The flavors were on point, and the pricing was surprisingly reasonable for the quality and quantity of food we received.

The highlight of our experience was the pet-friendly ambiance. It's not often that you find places that welcome your four-legged friends, and this added a wonderful touch to our evening.

In conclusion, BYOB Please in Thane is a place that we wholeheartedly recommend. It's not just a restaurant; it's an experience. Whether you're looking to enjoy great food, watch sports, or listen to live music, this place has it all. It's become one of our favorite spots in Thane. reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,800–2,000, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3}, time_line=2 years ago, review=We tried Tom Yum soup which was well made but had a extra dash of lemon.
Then we had golden monk chicken which came with salad. Salad should have been cold. This dish was very nutritious and good for health conscious people.
We had tempura prawns sushi. It was average. I liked their wasabi which had slight sweet tinge to it.
Noodles with exotic vegetables which had ample of  vegetables with some fried noodles. Crunchiness of noodles and vegetables was giving it a very good consistency.
For dessert we had crispy honey noodles with ice cream. It was well made but the there was small dollop of ice cream and plate full of noodles. We expected dessert to be in little smaller quantity and there was disproportionate amount of ice cream and noodles.

Overall it's a pocket friendly place for asian cuisine. Service was good. They can improve their ambience.
It's a small place so could be difficult to find for first comers., name_person=vishal sawant}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹400–600, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3}, time_line=a year ago, review=Golden Monk is located in the SAB TV office lane which is off Link Road and it is one of the oldest restaurant of that area hence easy to find.

The restaurant is decent in size and ambiance wise it has gone kind of dull with old school vibe still its cosy and decent.

They specialise in Asian cuisine hence the options available are great. Prices are not too high and the quantity served is good.

I went here for lunch and both kitchen plus table service was nice.

What We Had -
APPETISERS~
Cantonese Assorted Vegetable Dumpling.
Cantonese Chicken Dumpling.
Both the dumplings were generously filled and flavours wise nice use of fresh crunchy veggies and chicken with garlic ginger tasted excellent.

MAINS~
Veg Edamame Blue Fried Rice.
Shredded Chicken In Hunan Sauce.
Both the mains were excellent. Loved the rice as it had light spices used and hence the Hunan gravy went perfectly with the rice.

So our meal was great at Golden Monk and Asian food lovers should definitely try this., name_person=Shaikh Khalid Sarfaraz}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=5 years ago, review=Golden monk serves such good Chinese food.
Recently ordered from this place and the food was simply superb!
I ordered the following items:

Crispy chicken: My favourite Chinese appetizer and golden monk made sure that it was perfect. The chicken was crisp and the tangy flavour was superb and I loved every bite!

Chicken Malaysian flat noodles: These are flat noodles that has exotic veggies and chicken and egg. These noodles literally had the perfect flavour and the quantity was superb. Really amazing stuff!

Chicken clay pot rice: This rice item had an amazing quantity and had different veggies, mushrooms and chicken in its contents. This was more of a gravy cum rice item. The taste was fabulous and all the ingredients were very well cooked!

The packaging was also very good!
The food was delicious and the quantity was great!

Golden monk is a place that'll definitely make you it's fan with its value for money food with superb quantity and amazing taste!, name_person=Wesley Pereira}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Delivery, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹600–800}, time_line=a year ago, review=Craving warm comfort food, I decided to order my first ramen ever. Though I don't have a reference for comparison, I must say that the coconut prawn ramen was delicious! It was creamy, sweet and comforting just as I was looking for. 👌 🍜

I also ordered Burnt Garlic Noodles, which was really good too but nothing like the ramen.

1️⃣ SUGGESTION
Portions of both the dishes were quite large, easily serving two people or 3 if they eat like me! I would suggest giving the option of ordering half. I would definitely like to get this ramen again but since the size is so big I will think twice if it's just me having it., name_person=ANDREA.}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=5 years ago, review=Golden Monk is situated in the sab tv lane in Amdheri Lokhandwala and is a great option for chinese cuisine. They have a themed chinese decor and serves tasty & yummy chinese dishes.

Leave it to me ❤️: This mocktail is made up of soda , ginger , mint and sugar syrup which is just so soothing and refreshing to have.

Virgin Pina Colada : Classic drink made to perfection.

Manchow Soup ❤️: Ordered Jain option for Manchow soup which was just yummy and tasty with great taste to offer.

Paneer Chilly ❤️: Classic Paneer Chilly was spicy and good to have.

Aubergine with Basil & Chilly ❤️: Crispy Aubergine with Basil & Chilly was a great option to taste rather than the usual ones.

Malaysian Flat Noodles ❤️: Malaysian Flat Noodles had an authentic Chinese taste and had a decent quantity to fulfill your tummy.

Crispy Honey Noodles with IceCream : Crispy Honey Noodles topped with Vanilla IceCream is a great option for dessert to end your dine on a high., name_person=Karan Shah}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹400–600, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3}, time_line=a year ago, review=Good place to have Chinese food.

Hopefully they will be more responsible to the society and other customers going forward., name_person=Sonali Shivlani}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=I was looking for a venue for a lazy brunch, and Zomato suggested Bora Bora. I had been there before, quite a while ago, and with a review pending I thought why not, so here goes. I reached to find out that the AC section was closed for renovation, and was given a table outside. The overhead fans were quite efficient, and it wasn't too warm so the lack of AC wasn't an issue for me. I chose the alcoholic menu for their Sunday brunch, and started off with Long Island Iced Tea, Tempura Prawns and Mini Angry Bird. The drink was the first to be served, it was properly chilled, though a little on the sweeter side. Soon the prawns arrived, served fried with mayo and chutney. They weren't too oily, and the chutney went really well with the prawns. Up next was Mini Angry Bird, a veg pizza. Thin crust with tons of cheese, reasonable lot of toppings, a few olives, peppers and capsicum, I enjoyed every bite of it, most recommended, especially for vegetarians. Browsing through the menu the starters seemed really interesting so I decided to stick those and skip the main course. My next order was Chicken Chilly Tacos and Top Secret Malai Kebab, and my next drink was Blenders Pride. The tacos were particularly impressive, spicy meat on toasted bread with cheese, they were an absolute winner. The kebabs weren't too bad either, the meat was tender and though the name said Malai, there was some spice to it, which I didn't mind at all. This was followed by Wild Fish Fingers, strips of basa with a crunchy crust, I found it to be average, have had better elsewhere. With my tummy filling up, I drained my final round of whiskey, and ordered desserts. First up was a platter of pastries, in 3 flavours. The orange pastries were nothing to write about, the red velvet was a little above average, while the kiwi was the by far the best. Next I had some icecream, Vanilla and Strawberry scoops put together and it was delicious, I was tempted to go for another round, but then I was suggested Gulab Jamun by the staff so I opted for that, and what a suggestion it was. The gulab jamuns were soft, sweet and simply superb, a must-have here. Speaking of the staff, I must mention the attendant to my table, Angam. He was most polite, helpful, always with a smile, a big shoutout to his stellar service. With the desserts done, I asked for the cheque to conclude what had been a truly fulfilling meal. To sum up then, Bora Bora offers an excellent brunch, ticks most of the boxes, be it food or drinks or hospitality, there's little to complain. reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹600–800, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 weeks ago, review=Having lived and worked in Japan, albeit many moons ago, I was not expecting to be reminded of the tastes and feel of a typical izakaya in the land of the rising sun, in, of all places, Bandra, Mumbai.
We were ushered to our seating by a raucous welcome from the Kuuraku staff, which was more reminiscent of the Wankhede Stadium than a Japanese restaurant. But there was a effervescence about the staff at Kuuraku, reflecting the confidence that they have in their excellent food.
We ordered the Special Kushi Course, comprising 5 sticks of yakitori. The standout of this was the chicken tail. It was so good that we ordered two extra sticks of this, named bonjiri shio. We also ordered a portion of pork belly yakitori although this was very slightly disappointing as it was a little on the tough side. Another slight disappointment was the chargrilled asparagus wrapped in pork belly. Again, the pork belly wasn't as tender as I expected and the asparagus was a little small and fibrous. However, the edamame challenge was a lot of fun. The idea is to grab as much edamame as possible with one hand - and what you grab is what you get to eat. I used my goalkeeper hands to grab, what the server told me was an over par amount. The edamame was quite good too. The crunchy ebi roll was very generous too coming as a generous portion. The temperature of the rice was spot on as was the consistency. Could the quality of the rice be higher as in Japan? Well yes if you can get that rice but otherwise it really was excellent. The same goes for the pork rice. Here the consistency or the stickiness of the rice was more important than in the ebi roll and if they could get better rice it was be amazing. The slight disappointment was the inclusion of bell peppers. Heresy! Finally, the tea was served in a beautiful black pot, again, very true to Japan.
All in all this was an excellent place with a really true feel of Japan, helped also by the constant stream of Japanese music and the service was particularly excellent. Bravo Kuuraku, name_person=Indrajit Advani}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Somewhat recommend, GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Indoor_dining_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_INDOOR_DINING_AREA, Booth_seating, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_BOOTH_SEATING, Counter_seating, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_COUNTER_SEATING], GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,200–1,400, GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Varies by time / day, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[1_person, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_ONE, 2_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO, 3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR, 5-8_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_FIVE_TO_EIGHT, Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Clearly_labeled_vegetarian_dishes, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_CLEARLY_LABELED_ITEMS]}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=Visited Kuuraku Bandra for the first time and absolutely loved the experience! I’ve never been to Japan, but from everything I’ve seen online, this place feels incredibly authentic. The cozy ambience, smart use of space, and the open kitchen view really add to the charm and give it that genuine Japanese feel.

We opted for their vegetarian dishes and everything was excellent —
• Teppan Gyoza Veg
• Veg Creamy Ramen
• Crunchy Veg Roll
• Spicy Edamame
• Blueberry Kombucha
• Yukimi Daifuku

The portion sizes are huge, so we couldn’t try many desserts, but the ramen and the crunchy veg sushi roll were definitely the highlights — rich, comforting, and full of flavour.

Overall, great food, warm ambience, and a place I’d definitely recommend if you’re looking for a Japanese dining experience in Bandra!, name_person=Ketki Yash}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Somewhat recommend, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservation required, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Moderate noise, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING, Kid-friendliness, E:KID_FRIENDLINESS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Somewhat difficult to find parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION]}, time_line=3 weeks ago, review=Kuuraku turned out to be one of the most unique dining experiences I’ve had in a while. The moment you enter, they greet you loudly in the traditional Japanese style, and you’re asked to remove your shoes before stepping in. It immediately gives you that feeling of entering a clean, calm, and different kind of space.

Our server, Madan, was honestly the nicest guy very friendly, always smiling, and super helpful throughout the meal. He made the experience even better.

We tried a bunch of things:
Bull Yakult Sour, Kara Men, Virgin Matcha Ale, Spicy Salmon Roll, crispy chicken, and quite a few other dishes. Everything tasted great. The sushi was fresh, the drinks were good, and the food overall had a really comforting Japanese flavour to it.

They also give you warm towels when you sit, which is a small thing but adds to the whole experience. The seating is comfortable too, and the place just feels peaceful.

The only thing I’d say is that it is on the expensive side. But considering the food, the service, and the whole vibe, it still feels worth it.

Overall: Had an excellent time here. Great food, great service, and a very different, authentic atmosphere. Would definitely recommend., name_person=KartiK Mittal}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservations recommended, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Somewhat difficult to find parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Somewhat recommend, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Loud, but you can still talk, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Paid_street_parking, E:PARKING_OPTION_PAID_STREET_PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[2_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO], GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Clearly_labeled_vegetarian_dishes, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_CLEARLY_LABELED_ITEMS]}, time_line=3 weeks ago, review=I had a lot of expectations from Kuuraku a friend recommended the place.

Would highly recommend making a reservation before going here else you might not get a table. This rating is subject to change if I go there again.

For starters we had 2 portions of the Tori Kushi Course. The first time around the staff got it so late that it was cold till it reached us. We asked twice and then they realised they forgot it. But the food was yummy when it was cold and when it was hot. Hence would recommend it.

It’s a small, warm space in Khar with a simple, earthy charm — the kind of place where you can actually hear conversations, enjoy the aroma from the open kitchen, and feel connected to the food being prepared.

The menu is a beautiful mix of coastal, Kerala, and Maharashtrian flavours, but presented in a very thoughtful and modern way. Every dish has a story, and you can sense the amount of care the chefs put into balancing comfort with creativity. The curries are rich without being heavy, the spices are well-rounded, and the seafood is exceptionally fresh. Even the vegetarian dishes stand out with bold, homely flavours.

Their weekend brunch is especially worth trying — soft appams, dosas, light stews, filter coffee — everything tastes like a regional home kitchen brought into a modern dining space. Portions are satisfying and plating is elegant without being overdone.

Service is polite, patient, and genuinely interested in helping you choose. Because the space is compact, the whole experience feels personal and relaxed rather than rushed or commercial.

Prices are on the higher side, but completely justified considering the quality, originality, and the chef-driven approach. It’s not a “quick meal” type of place — it’s somewhere you go to slow down and enjoy food with intention.

Overall: Kari Apla is a wonderful blend of nostalgia, regional flavours, and modern presentation. If you enjoy coastal Indian cuisine or simply love trying thoughtfully crafted food, this is a spot you shouldn’t miss., name_person=rajesh jaiswar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Tender_Coconut_Pudding, Passion_Fruit_Soda, Avocado_Thecha_&_Batata_Papad, Banana_Leaf_Roasted_Fish_with_Scallion_Chilli_Parotta], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=Hands down one of the best meals in Mumbai! Since there's no valet, you can find parking in one of the bylanes near the restaurant.

Ambience - very calm, small, cosy place with limited seating. Not too loud. They have a bar type arrangement with an open kitchen where you can watch the chefs at work.

Food - amazing South Indian food! Tried the Inji Pulled Pork, the Souriani prawns, fish cooked in Banana leaf with scallion parothas.
Everything was delicious.
Special mention for the tiny, delicious ladi pav. It's super flavorful.
They ran out of the tender coconut pudding (guess we'll have to go there to try that again)
But the banana bread + coffee ice cream combo is superb and also a must try.

Portion size is small, yet sufficient.
Slightly priced on the higher side.

Service - very prompt and attentive hosts.
Would definitely recommend going here for some out of the box cuisine.
Best to make reservations before your visit., name_person=Rudri Randeria}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 months ago, review=Kari Appla, Bandra – A Hidden Gem of Flavours

What an absolute delight this place turned out to be! Kari Appla is a small, intimate restaurant that beautifully blends the cuisines of Maharashtra and Kerala. The concept is special—the husband hails from Kerala, and the wife from Maharashtra—and you can feel that personal touch in every dish.

I was attended to by Parth and later by Suresh, both of whom were warm, attentive, and made the experience even better. Even though the owners weren’t around that evening, their passion clearly shines through the food and the space.

The highlight of my visit was the Angamalai Pork Roast with Ghee Rice. Simply phenomenal! Perfectly spiced, rich, tender pork with that punch of Kerala-style masala, balanced by the subtle fragrance of ghee rice. It’s an absolute must-try if you’re here.

The restaurant itself is small but thoughtfully designed. There’s a see-through kitchen, which is neat, spotless, and such a joy to watch while the chefs work their magic. They also have a live counter setup where you can sit at the bar-style stools and enjoy your meal right in front of the action—it’s rare to find such transparency and energy in a kitchen.

The walls are lined with photos that give you a sense of warmth and homeliness, almost like walking into a family album. Combined with the intimate seating and the friendly staff, the whole vibe feels cozy yet modern.

Overall, Kari Appla is a hidden treasure in Bandra—it’s not just about food but about heart, culture, and soul on a plate. Stumbled upon this gem on the District app while wandering through Bandra. The Yoga House is one of those classic Bandra homes turned into a calm, airy cafe. You won’t spot a flashy sign from the road, so trust Google Maps and keep your eyes peeled for a quiet villa entrance. A staff member guided us upstairs. The first floor looks set up for yoga, and the cafe opens out on the second.

Seating is split into three moods. Indoors for soft light and calm conversations. A leafy outdoor section for sunshine and breezes. And one level up, a shamiana style nook where you sit cross-legged and forget time. It feels like a friend’s mindful terrace more than a commercial cafe.

We picked an outside table. Peaceful. Not crowded. Bandra energy without the traffic noise. Service was warm and unhurried. We tried their Summer Salad. Fruity, crunchy, and bright with mixed produce. Roughly ₹545 all in. Portion was decent and left us satisfied. Prices lean premium, but you are paying for the setting and the slow, healthy focus.

What I loved

1. Tucked away location that keeps it serene

2. Variety of seating that lets you choose your vibe

3. Staff that actually looks after you without hovering

Good to know:
•	Harder to spot from the street, so navigate straight to “The Yoga House” near Nargis Villa or Water Bungalow

•	Menu skews healthy and light. Great if that is your mood, not ideal if you want heavy mains

Verdict:
Come here when you need a gentle pause in the middle of Bandra. Perfect for solo journaling, slow brunch with a book, or a catch-up where you can actually hear each other. ["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,200–1,400, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=a month ago, review=The Borivali Beacon: Where the Heart of a Bawa Beats

In the often-cacophonous theatre of Borivali West, where every corner screams for attention, there exists a quiet, graceful pause—a Parsi sanctuary. To call this establishment merely a café is to mistake a perfectly cut diamond for a simple stone. This is a treat, yaar, a small revelation wrapped in an ambience of serene, unpretentious class.

It is a place where the air itself seems infused with generational grace, the kind that whispers of old Bombay, good recipes, and true hospitality. Everything about the setting—the light, the clean lines, the subtle decorative flourishes—suggests that one should simply sit, sigh, and prepare for a genuine moment of peace.

A Culinary Revelation: The Mexican Manna
While the atmosphere is a gentle balm for the soul, let us not mince words, dikra: the food is the star, the crescendo of the entire visit. You can, and should, close your eyes and point randomly to the menu; you will not find fault. But if one must declare a favorite, it is with dramatic emphasis that I must praise their pizzas.

And among them? The Mexican Pizza is not just food; it is a philosophy. It’s an unlikely, perfect marriage of Parsi punctuality and Aztec spice, a fiery yet balanced canvas of flavor that dances on the palate and leaves you wondering why you haven't dedicated your life to consuming it daily. A testament to a kitchen that respects tradition but isn't afraid to give it a joyful, spicy kick.

The Triumph of the Sweet Smile

Yet, even after the last crumb of that incredible Mexican feast has vanished, the lasting impression, the true elixir of this Borivali gem, is the management.

You know the types, don’t you? The proprietors in other establishments who stride through the dining room with the air of an emperor addressing his least favorite vassals, whose very presence makes you feel guilty for existing, as if your patronage is a tiresome formality.

Here, we find the sublime opposite. The humble manager is a lesson in human decency. His kindness is not a trained customer service routine; it is an aura. He moves with an earnest sweetness, his smile a genuine beacon that will cling to you long after you’ve left the place. It's the unmistakable, unwavering elegance of Parsi hospitality—a profound, quiet pride in making you feel welcome, safe, and utterly valued.

This gentleman’s demeanor is not just good for business; it is good for the soul. He is a testament to the belief that true class resides not in the décor, but in the effortless, respectful treatment of one’s guests. No! No! I visited Mimi Café & Bistro based on reviews and performance marketing done by some content creators on Instagram, but the overall experience was very disappointing.

The food was the biggest letdown. Everything tasted bland and tired, as if it had been sitting out for too long. The dishes looked far better on the menu than what actually arrived at the table, and even the basics lacked seasoning and freshness. We ordered the Fajita Spice Pizza (one of the worst pizzas I’ve ever had in my life), Italian Sizzlers (not up to the mark at this price point), Peri Peri Fries, Caribbean Blonde, and Bisleri—total bill: ₹1581.

The atmosphere didn’t help either. Instead of feeling cozy or inviting, the dining area felt worn out and a bit chaotic. Customers have to wait for about half an hour to get a seat, and because the waiting area is inside the café, right next to the seating area, the people already dining end up getting disturbed by the commotion.

Overall, the combination of mediocre food and an unappealing atmosphere made the experience a complete miss for me. I hope things improve, but as of now, I don’t see myself returning anytime soon.

I definitely would not recommend anyone visit here to dine in. We thought of trying a new restaurant nearby.

We chose The Fillo, a recently opened restaurant in Bhayandar West. Excited about visiting the place, and considering it was a weekend, we decided to reach early to avoid waiting. However, our excitement quickly turned into disappointment, resulting in one of the worst dining experiences we’ve ever had.

When we arrived, they informed us that all the tables were occupied and asked us to wait for 30 minutes. We had reached at 7:45 PM, but even after waiting, we didn’t get a table. The host insisted we sit in the garden area, which was vacant. However, we had clearly mentioned that we preferred an AC table and were willing to wait. This made me feel quite awkward—if we had already requested an AC table, why were they trying to force us into the garden area?

To make matters worse, we noticed a group of four people arrive without a reservation, yet they were promptly offered an AC table. When we questioned the host and the manager, they claimed the table was for four people and not for two. My husband and I were furious with this illogical reasoning. After arguing with them, they apologized and eventually arranged a table of six for us.

Once seated, barely 5–7 minutes passed before a staff member approached us and asked us to move to a smaller table for two so they could accommodate another family of 4–5 people. While we agreed to cooperate, we couldn’t help but feel undervalued as customers. Regardless of whether there are two or four diners, everyone is paying for their meal, and this kind of treatment felt discriminatory.

While seated at the table for two, we observed the staff moving another family from a table for six to a table for four, just to accommodate others. The constant shuffling of guests between tables was chaotic and showed a complete lack of management.

The food, unfortunately, didn’t make up for the poor service. The menu was limited, and the dishes we tried were disappointing:

Cheese Fries: Served in a strainer, causing all the liquid cheese to drain off. The fries were dry and lacked flavor. When we complained, they apologized and served cheese separately, but by then, the taste was already ruined.

Chur Chur Naan: This was essentially a crumbled potato paratha with no distinctive flavor or masala.

Pesto Bao: While new and somewhat acceptable, it wasn’t impressive.

Frustrated, we gave up and didn’t order anything else. The overall experience felt like a complete waste of time and money. In hindsight, we should’ve gone to one of our usual dining spots where we’re always satisfied with the meal and service.

I will never recommend The Fillo, even if someone offers to take you there for free or as part of a party., name_person=Deepa Thathagar}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Most unique place for the Mira Bhayandar people of Veg and Jain food lovers.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Poor table management, extremely delayed service, and unorganized staff.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=The menu offers a wide variety of dishes to choose from.}"]

The place is conveniently located and has a lively vibe.

What we ordered:
Medium Ice Cream Cups × 4 (each with two scoops of our choice — loved that they allow two flavours in one cup).
We tried multiple flavours including Blueberry Cheesecake, Tiramisu, and many more.

Bill: ₹1025 for 4 people (around ₹250 per person) — reasonable considering the quality, taste, and variety.

Highlights: The ice cream was absolutely delicious. One of my friends was genuinely surprised to see such a place with so many unique varieties in Kharghar — something he had only experienced in Bandra or South Mumbai. He even mentioned that he’ll bring his partner here next time. The option to taste before choosing was a big plus, and every flavour we tried stood out.

Service: Friendly and helpful staff, quick in serving, and they happily offered us tastings to help us decide.

Ambience: Clean, modern, and cheerful — perfect for hanging out with friends or enjoying a relaxed ice cream and snack session.

Overall: A delightful spot in Kharghar for ice creams and more. Great flavours, good service, and a pleasant experience overall. •	Chicken Peri Peri Calzone – ₹389

•	Babaji Sandwich – ₹319

reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a week ago, review=🌶️🔥 Chulha Village, Ghodbundar – A True Desi Food Experience! 🍲🌾

Visited Chulha Village in Ghodbundar, Thane West, and it truly lives up to its name — mitti se juda, swaad se bhara. The ambience gives proper village-style vibes, warm and earthy, making the whole dining experience feel comforting and authentic.

We started with refreshing mocktails — the Virgin Mojito and Passion Punch were well-balanced and perfect to kick things off. For food, the Chicken Lollypop was crispy and flavorful, while the Murg Aalishan Kebab stood out with its rich marination and smoky taste.

The main course was the real highlight. The Chicken Handi and Kala Masala (Broiler) were packed with bold, traditional spices and tasted absolutely delicious when paired with Jowari Roti and Cheese Garlic Naan. You can genuinely taste the desi masalas and slow-cooked flavors in every bite.

["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Peri_Peri_Chicken_Pizza, French_Fries], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a year ago, review=I recently had the pleasure of visiting Tales of Tavern, and it was an enjoyable experience from start to finish. The pub offers a buffet that is impressive in its variety and quality. Both vegetarians and non-vegetarians will find plenty of options to satisfy their cravings. The assorted choices ensure there's something for everyone, making it a great spot for group outings.

The welcome drink set the tone for the meal with its refreshing and well-balanced flavors. It was a nice touch that made me feel valued as a guest. One of the highlights of the buffet was the inclusion of pizza. It's not often you find such a staple comfort food included in a buffet spread, and it did not disappoint. The pizzas were well-cooked with a perfect blend of toppings, appealing to both adults and kids alike.

The ambiance of Tales of Tavern is another strong point. The decor is thoughtfully designed, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere that is perfect for both casual lunches and lively dinner parties. Although I visited for lunch, I could easily see how this place would transform into a fantastic dinner and party venue. The lighting, music, and overall vibe make it an ideal spot for evening gatherings.

In conclusion, Tales of Tavern is a well-rounded pub that excels in offering a diverse and delicious buffet. The ambiance of the restaurant is inviting and spacious, with comfortable seating arrangements suitable for both small and large groups. The decor is modern yet cozy, creating a pleasant dining atmosphere.
The service provided by the staff is commendable. They are attentive, friendly, and prompt in attending to the needs of the customers.
The buffet started with a refreshing mocktail but was much needed to beat the summer heat.
Coming to the food...
We started with an aromatic chicken clear soup which had it's flavours infused in every bit of a drop.
The starters offered in the lunch buffet are diverse and flavorful. The Paneer Hariyali Kebab is a standout, with tender paneer marinated in aromatic green herbs. The Potato Yellow Chilly and Black Pepper Chilly provide a spicy kick, while the Chicken Alishan Kebab and Chicken Harissa Wings are perfect for meat lovers with their juicy and succulent flavors. 🍗
The main course selection offers a variety of options catering to different tastes. The Herb Rice is fragrant and perfectly cooked, complementing the Spicy Black Bean Sauce which adds a rich and bold flavor. The Veg Kolhapuri bursts with traditional Indian spices, while the Chicken Kadai and Grilled Chicken with Rojan Sauce are both tender and flavorful. The Dal Tadka is a comforting addition, providing a perfect balance of lentils and spices.
It also had a seperate Pizza and Salad Bar 🍕

The Salad Bar offers a refreshing assortment of options, including Nachos with Salsa, Russian Salad, Chicken Sauces Salad, Beetroot Hummus & Pita, and a vibrant Mix Fruit Platter, providing a healthy and light complement to the meal.
The dessert selection is the perfect conclusion to the meal. The Biscoff Cheesecake is a heavenly delight, with its creamy texture and indulgent flavor. The assorted pastries are beautifully presented and offer a variety of sweet treats to satisfy any sweet tooth. 🍰
In conclusion, the lunch buffet at Tales of Tavern in CBD Belapur, Navi Mumbai, is a delightful culinary experience that caters to a variety of tastes.
