PROS -
- Amazing location, the area was more than big enough for us. The have one small space and one large space divided, as per your need & party size you can choose one or both.
- Decor was on point. They have their own vendor for the same who has monopoly, but Shweta knows her stuff, and will help you achieve the best possible decor in your budget. Totally Trustworthy, just be clear and detailed in your brief and references
- Food - Bang on. Worth every penny, all of our guests mentioned great stuff & compliments about the food, starters and welcome drinks. On request, the starters where circulated for much longer than the usual time as well. The staff service was very well executed too. Kudos to Subhash sir.

CONS -
- The DJ and lights vendor (Sanjay), who they have appointed, and who has monopoly there, was the only thing that didn't work out for us. As our timing were a little extended due to back to back functions the same day, we were asked to pay for 2 shifts for the DJ. Which we agreed on, also extra amounts where paid for stage lightings as well for Dance performances, as they weren't a part of the DJ or Decor Setup.
- Inspite of paying everything in advance to the said vendor, things werent planned properly. We made a pro active effort of providing all music files for the DJ night and performances well in advance, the DJ was totally unprepared and didn't have any files with him, inspite of everything being shared with him a week prior. By God' s Grace, we had a backup plan with backup pendrives, and yet still the DJ managed to screw things up and didnt play the tracks as per the given order or on time.
- There were 6-7 Pendrives given to the DJ by different parties for the sangeet choreographed performances. We got none of them back
- The DJ was not informed that its a double shift, hence he didn't start the soft music sessions on time. We know this because he actually said to us "Your sangeet and function starts at 6, why do you need music from 4 PM"?. The double shift was booked from 4 PM - 10 PM.
- The vendor (Sanjay)  was very pro active with us, till the payment went to him. Post that, everything was a blunder.
- Of course in our post event feedback we mentioned all of this to the owner. A few days later the said vendor called us on our honeymoon, and had the audacity to say "Aap mera naam kharab kar rahe ho, maine aapko apna best DJ diya tha" :/

So overall, i would say this place is lovely, in terms of the food, venue and decor. The moment you step inside, the Korean-inspired ambiance instantly wins your heart — pastel décor, cozy corners, and such cheerful energy that lifts your mood right away. ✨

The staff was extremely polite and welcoming, and the service was smooth throughout our visit. Now coming to the best part — the food! Every dish we tried was beautifully plated, bursting with flavor, and carried its own unique twist.

We ordered the Chicken Yom Tom, Street Style Chicken Chilli, Chow Mein Bowl, and Pink Rice Bowl, along with Spring Rolls, a Belgian Chocolate Boba Shake, and a Strawberry Milkshake — and honestly, every single item was a hit! The Chicken Yom Tom had a comforting, mildly spicy taste that instantly stood out, while the Street Style Chicken Chilli was bold, tangy, and perfectly balanced. The bowls were hearty, wholesome, and packed with flavor — ideal for a fulfilling meal. 🍜

For desserts, we indulged in their Milk Cake, Assorted Mochi, and Churros, and it was the perfect sweet ending! The mochi was soft, chewy, and absolutely delightful — with just the right touch of sweetness. 🍡💖

Overall, everything about Aegyo Café felt so thoughtfully curated — from the presentation to the flavors, from the interiors to the service. It’s one of those cafés where you don’t just eat — you experience the vibe. Every corner is picture-perfect, every dish is delicious, and every moment feels joyful.

If you’re someone who loves exploring cute, aesthetic cafés with great food and good vibes, Aegyo Café deserves a top spot on your list! 🌸✨, name_person=sayama khan}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=We visited Aegyo Bakehouse and absolutely loved the experience! It’s a pretty place with aesthetic decor — perfect for photos and an even better spot for all Korean food lovers. They offer both indoor and outdoor seating, making the ambience super cozy.

We tried their new Pan Asian menu and everything was impressive.
•	Chicken Shanghai came topped with peanuts and red chillies — the perfect asian starter
•	Chicken Chilli Rice Bowl had a rich, flavourful gravy that paired amazingly well with the rice.

reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=8 months ago, review=Vice Global Tapas & Bar in Juhu is a vibe—dark, aesthetic, and effortlessly classy. Perfect for a laid-back yet upscale dining experience.

We kicked things off with the Turnip Cake, which was soft, flavorful, and paired beautifully with its sauce. The Paneer Chilly Bao had a perfect balance of spice and fluffiness, while the Exotic Veggie Dim Sum was a delightful bite. The Greek Flatbread was a fusion twist done right!

For drinks, we sipped on two tropical cocktails that were refreshing and well-crafted. And to end on a sweet note, the Tiramisu was the perfect indulgence—rich, creamy, and just the right amount of coffee kick.

Overall, a must-visit spot for anyone who loves good food, great drinks, and a chic, intimate atmosphere.🩷🌈, name_person=Aastha Parab}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,800–2,000, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=5 months ago, review=Absolutely loved Vice – 5/5 stars!

Vice totally delivered on all fronts — food, vibes, and music. The atmosphere was electric, and the DJ Gaurang was phenomenal — 10/10 for the playlist and smooth transitions.

The food? Exceptional. The chimichurri paneer was out of this world — perfectly cooked, packed with flavor, and such a fresh twist on a classic. Even the meat dishes were super innovative — not your usual fare, but elevated and bold in the best way.

Everything felt well thought-out and delicious. It’s rare to find a place that nails food and vibes equally, but Vice has cracked the code. Can’t wait to go back!, name_person=Vrusti Patel}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=9 months ago, review=So, I finally checked out Vice Global Tapas Bar in Juhu, and honestly, it’s got everything you’d want for a fun night out—great food, crazy good cocktails, and a vibe that just makes you want to stay longer. The interiors are fancy yet cozy, with dim lights and a lively atmosphere. Perfect for catching up with friends or just chilling with a good drink.

Now, let’s get to the food:
•	Turnip Cake – Didn’t expect much, but it was surprisingly good! Crispy on the outside, soft inside, and full of flavor.
•	Yasai Tempura Sushi – If you love sushi, this one’s a winner. Crunchy, fresh, and packed with flavor.
•	Korean Pot Rice – Comfort food at its best. The flavors were bang on, and it’s super satisfying.
•	Spaghetti – Classic and well-made. No complaints!
•	Smoked Ale – If you’re into something strong with a smoky twist, this is a must-try.
•	Am I Clear? – The name itself is fun, and so is the drink. Strong, smooth, and refreshing.
•	NY Baked Cheesecake with Nutella Pour – Just order it. No questions. It’s rich, creamy, and that Nutella pour is just heaven.

The bar menu is a highlight, with some really unique cocktails. The bartenders know their stuff, and the drinks are just as much an experience as the food.

Overall, Vice is the place to be if you’re looking for good food, good drinks, and a good time. Whether you’re going all out on a night with friends or just want to enjoy some solid food and chill, this spot delivers. We felt that we were left hungry at the end in spite of having spent quite a bit!!, name_person=Swati Chitalia Leading to Light}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,800–2,000, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 years ago, review=For a long time, I wanted to visit the Conservatory for its bright sun-filled glass roof terrace setting. We called them at the very last minute on Saturday morning for dinner reservations, and they said we can accommodate you for an early dinner slot between 6:30 to 8:30 pm. We were initially booked for a table in a lower area, but on our request based on availability, they happily moved us to the terrace. In early evening sunlight, the terrace set up was stunning, with light classy furniture and tastefully placed plants everywhere! And then the sun went down and the place glowed warm dim lighting. For starters the Beetroot Thecha Toast with the subtle fiery taste of thecha and loads of avocado and cream was great! The very popular heartily portioned Bombil Fish and Chips was amazing! Only a Bengali chef can do justice to the tricky fish of Bombil, without making it too heavy or oily. For mains, we had the Parsi Mutton Kheema pizza with six slices and lavish kheema topping, which was a great blend of Italian and Parsi cuisines. We ended our fantastic dinner with heart-warming French Toast for desserts, loaded with butter, the right amount of sweetness, and fresh berries. We paid 4k between the two of us for four dishes, which makes it a tad bit expensive. For the posh Juhu ambience, the quality ingredients, and the chef’s innovation and craft, maybe the price is justified! The other reviews for this place are like playing a game of one truth and two lies. Most reviews suggest the staff is unfriendly, the food doesn’t taste good with small portions, and the place is expensive. reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹400–600, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=a month ago, review=It appeared to be a newly opened spa from the board's description. However, Chinese Whisper is actually an Asian Resto by Binny.

It's located on the first floor. The entry way is pretty at night. The interior of the place is similar to an asian night bar resto except they don't have alcohol on their menu.

I along with my veg fren tried their Wok Toss momo which was a little off in taste because of excessive soy sauce. The filling was a mashed mixture of veggies. Later, we tried their Hot Top Ramen which was sooooo good. The soup was flavorful, perfect for the cold winter. I will reccomend them frying the paneer. Soft paneer wasn't complimenting the dish.

All in all as a newly opened Asian resto it's pretty good to chill at night. Can't comment on the authenticity of the Asian cuisine. However, the experience was a 7/10. I will try non-veg soon.

A note from my veg fren: please provide uniform or hire a qualified server. The cute boy doesn't give a good impression of the place., name_person=draksha ikram khan}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=1}, time_line=3 weeks ago, review=The best example of a restaurant being run without any passion or commitment towards service or quality.

I visited this place last night for dinner with the expectation of at least decent service and good food, especially since it’s a new restaurant in town. I also noticed a review mentioning “authentic Chinese dishes,” which encouraged me to try it. Unfortunately, the experience was extremely disappointing.

The service staff appeared to be two under-18 kids who had no idea about the menu, the dishes, or basic service etiquette. The food itself was an overload of ginger, garlic, and sauces—nothing close to authentic Chinese cuisine as mentioned in earlier reviews.

Despite the restaurant being almost empty, we had to wait 45 minutes for our food. I also observed at least three other tables giving negative feedback to the same staff due to poor food quality.

My sincere suggestion to the management: build your passion and sincerity first. Focus on serving your guests with care and quality—the money will follow automatically., name_person=SANDEEP S NAIR}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=a month ago, review=Awesome experience at this small but authentic restaurant.
The food was simply too good..getting such diff cuisine in vasai is great.

DO TRY IT ONCE.  And ask them to recommend if you dont understand the cuisine.

reviews: ["{\"name_person\":\"Aabhaas Walia\",\"time_line\":\"3 years ago\",\"review\":\"Located at lobby level of The Leela Hotel. It is a beautiful bar with splendid alcoholic drinks. The decor is excellent and so is the ambience.\\nPerfect for a cozy evening.\",\"guided_block\":{}}", "{\"name_person\":\"The Glocal Journal\",\"time_line\":\"7 years ago\",\"review\":\"Spanish Affair @TheLeela, Mumbai\\n\\nLeela at Bombay is near the airport road and known to host businessmen. The property's grandeur and usage of plantations to make it a destination for peace in this bustling city.\\n\\nWhen I first read, Spanish food caught my eyes and I thought I had to try it.\\n\\nWe had an evening of wine from Torres and Spanish food by the poolside at Six Degrees.\\n\\nHow was the ambience?\\nIt was a pretty evening with wines flowing, prawns cooking while the sound of fountains soothed & the sight of the poolside pleased\\n\\nWhat did you do?\\n\\nFor vegetarians, we had spinach croquet which was smooth and potato paella . Also, we had mushroom paella. Not to forget the Spanish tradition of having many olives in your meal.\\n\\nWould add, it was heavenly for non vegetarians with Serrano Ham and pequilo peppers and many others flowing. I didn't try it but my friends who had this said this.\\n\\nWe had a cold soup viz Ajio blanc shooters which was weirdly nice. It was really different but tasted good.\\n\\nComing to the wine,\\nTasted the Rose : De Caste which was good in its own way.\\n\\nThen next up, I have hogged onto the desserts.\\n\\nAroz con leche : This was served in a pretty looking jar but didn't taste great.\\nCreme catalana : This was delectable.\\n\\nPolvorones almond cookies : These cookies were soft and crunchy and just nice.\\nWe also tried the Churros. They were made at the time of serving. Chose chocolate and strawberries to go with as the strawberries balanced out the sweetness.\\nThere were pretzels and macaroons too. And not to forget the orange sponge cake which is again a Spanish authenticity.\\n\\nEnded it with,  the chocolate flan.\\n\\nMy Spanish affair ended on a sweet note.\\nIf you are fond of it, go and try it out!\",\"guided_block\":{}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Everything On A Plate EOAP\",\"time_line\":\"7 years ago\",\"review\":\"The Leela Mumbai is taking its patrons on a culinary journey to Spain and is leaving no stone unturned. Celebrating the flavours of Spain, The Leela has collaborated with Chef Sergio Millet, Executive Chef of Mas Rabell restaurant at the famous Torres vineyards in Spain.\\n\\nTo add to the treat, The House of Torres is pairing with the menu some of its legendary wines ( Mas La Plana, Ibericos Rioja, Gran Coronas, Grans Muralles). What stuck with us the most about the wines, apart from the gorgeous flavours, was that each of them has a wonderful story to tell each explained to us passionately by Tushar.\\n\\nWe had the pleasure to attend one of their Tapas evenings and here\\nare some things that stood out :\\n\\nAjo Blanco\\nWe were quite happy to see this popular cold soup as a starter, especially served as shots! Ajo Blanco is typically made from a mix of bread, almonds, vinegar, olive oil, salt, water and garlic. The drink is very smooth & is quite refreshing, especially in the summer.\\n\\nGambas Pil Pil\\nThe Gambas ( Shrimp ) Pil Pil ( Sauce ) were flying off the stove like hot cakes! Almost everyone took seconds & thirds. Gambas Pil Pil Prawn tossed in a sizzling hot sauce of garlic, chilli & olive oil. Not only was it a delight to watch the chef toss them on the live counter but it was also plated adorably in these tiny little red pots.\\n\\nPan con Tomate with Spicy Tomato Sauce\\nMany say this dish is as humble as tapas can get. The tiny, bite-sized pieces of Spanish toast are a delicious, quick snack made with just five ingredients, namely, bread, tomato, olive oil, garlic, and salt.\\n\\nChicken and Mushroom Paella\\nWe kind of missed this but the others were raving about this dish!\\n\\nThese were just the tip of the iceberg, you must visit to learn more\\nabout the other delicacies on the menu.\\n\\nDesserts\\nFor the most part of the evening, we were hovering around the dessert counter drooling over the desserts on display.\\n\\nChurros\\nWe loved watching the churros being made and gulping them down nice and warm. To add to the delicious brown pastry, we had chocolate sauce, strawberry sauce & Ice cream made in the Leela Kitchen.\\n\\nCr\u00e8me Catalana\\nThe dessert draws parallels with the cr\u00e8me br\u00fbl\u00e9e, the difference being the latter doesn\u2019t contain fine cornflour. The custard was well set and was garnished with fresh fruit, we quite enjoyed it.\\n\\nArroz con Leche\\nPresentation-wise, this stood out the most as it was served in these tiny dessert jars with a dropper full of syrup. The Arroz ( Rice ) con Leche ( Milk ) is basically a Mexican rice pudding and can be a bit bland. Chef Rachna gave it a little extra flavour by adding in some fresh fruits.\\n\\nThere were also Alfajores, Polvorones Almond Cookies, Pretzel Pops, Macaroons, Orange Sponge Cake and more!\\n\\nOur brief visit to the Leela Mumbai Tapas Evening was definitely not enough for us. We will be visiting again soon.\",\"guided_block\":{}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Joanita Francis\",\"time_line\":\"9 months ago\",\"review\":\"I had the pleasure of dining at Six Degrees at The Leela Palace, Mumbai, and it was an exceptional experience from start to finish. The food, drinks, and service were truly outstanding!\\n\\nThe Grilled Bratwurst Sausages with caramelized onions were absolutely to die for\u2014perfectly cooked and bursting with flavor. It was meant to be an ordinary evening—our anniversary, swept under the rug of endless deadlines and bustling schedules, like any other working couple caught in the grind. With our go-to club unexpectedly shut, we wandered into Novotel—not expecting much, just hoping for a decent drink and a meal to end the day.

But what unfolded was nothing short of an experience.

The ambience hummed with understated elegance, and the stewards—especially Tauffik and Yash—welcomed us with warmth that felt personal, not rehearsed. No pretence, just genuine hospitality with a hint of finesse you’d expect from a luxury brand, but often miss.

Then came the cocktails—
The first sip transported me. A brilliant concoction of scotch, pineapple, and a whisper of cinnamon—balanced with surgical precision. Nothing overbearing. Just a beautiful orchestration of flavors, where each note knew its place.

As if that wasn’t enough, I ordered another. This time, it was bold, tangy, and not even remotely sweet—exactly how a well-thought drink should punch you: with character, not confusion.

The food followed, and it didn’t disappoint.
The Chicken Spaghetti was a protein-lover’s dream—light on oil, laced gently with garlic, and sprinkled with greens that weren’t an afterthought but a part of the experience.

And then, a pleasant surprise: Chicken Kori with Appam—comfort food executed with restraint and finesse. No excess oil, no spice overpowering the senses—just subtlety, balance, and technique.

If you haven’t been here yet, trust me—it would be regretful not to.
I forgot the heart robe “tiramisu” which they prepped fresh for us from scratch.

It’s one of those places where you walk in for a drink and walk out with a story., name_person=Sunnyy Narwani}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=3 months ago, review=The bar at Novotel Mumbai is quite impressive, and the food was exceptionally tasty. On our most recent visit — a Sunday — we were somewhat surprised to find ourselves waiting for nearly 15 minutes before being seated, despite having a paid and guaranteed reservation. While the restaurant’s popularity, especially over the weekend, is understandable, such a delay does take away slightly from the otherwise premium dining experience one expects with a confirmed booking. In contrast, our weekday visit was handled seamlessly, with immediate seating and a noticeably calmer ambience.

The service on both occasions, however, was exceptional. Every member of the staff was attentive, courteous, and eager to make the experience memorable. A special mention must go to David, who stood out for his warmth and proactive attitude. He went above and beyond to accommodate our preferences, even helping customize certain dishes — a gesture that reflected genuine hospitality and care.

Coming to the food, O Pedro continues to impress with its bold, vibrant flavors. The menu has a unique character — there’s a slight get-used-to element initially, as the dishes often play with contrasting and layered flavor profiles. Overall, the palate leans towards the spicier side, but once accustomed, it becomes quite addictive. Highly recommend trying the Jackfruit Pilaf, the Chorizo Fried Rice (adding an extra egg takes it up a notch), and the Butter Garlic Prawns, all of which stood out for their balance of flavor and quality of preparation.

The ambience, much like the experience, varies by day. On weekends, the place is packed with energy — the crowd is vibrant, the music is loud, and the overall buzz is palpable. While that lends a lively atmosphere, it can get slightly overwhelming when you’re looking for a quieter dining experience. On weekdays, however, O Pedro strikes the perfect note — with softer music, balanced lighting, and an ambience that lets you truly unwind and savor your meal., name_person=Akshay Grewal}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Loud, but you can still talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=10-30 min}, time_line=a month ago, review=O Pedro is one of my most favourite restaurant in Bombay. Their other outlet is in Andheri East.

The restaurant is spacious with nice sound system, a projector screen, a finely lit bar and multiple seatings for all type of groups. They have not invested much in the ambiance however the feel is nice.

They specialise in a multi cuisine menu and the options are great. Dishes are nicely balanced for both vegetarians and non vegetarians. Prices are at par with similar type of brands amd the best part is the offers on drinks. On a daily basis they have kept different offers so do check those before visiting.

I went here for dinner and the kitchen service was quick and the table service by staff Jeevan was good.

What We Had -
APPETIZERS~
Kashmiri Paneer Tikka -
Fresh paneer with coriander and green base tasted decent. The spice rub lacked the zing and I felt less time was given to tandoor. Hence minor improvements needed.

Devil's Chicken Chilli -
Looked fiery but tasted great. Juicy chiken chunks with bell peppers and onions with garlic and red chilli base tasted delicious. Loved the bold flavours which were not too strong.

Butter Garlic Prawns -
One word perfect. Fresh prawns with bell peppers and onions and base as butter garlic tasted outstanding. Loved the juicy prawns and the butter didn't left any sweet after taste plus flavours from the garlic was spot on.

MAINS~
Desi Style Triple Rice (Chicken)-
A perfect craving buster for a Chinese lover like me. Loved the rice, gravy and the egg on the top. Deliciously tasty as everything about this dish was amazing.

DESSERTS~
English Vinglish -
A fusion of chocolate brownie with gajar ka halwa. Looked stunning tasted great. Loved eating every bit of this.

MOCKTAILS~
Fruit Punch.
Citrus Cooler.
Both the mocktails were refreshing with perfect flavours.

So our dinner at Craftbar BKC was a great meal as everything from food, service to music was amazing. Donna Deli – Bandra West | Saturday Dinner Review

📍 Location & First Impressions
Donna Deli sits right on SV Road, Bandra, a short stroll from Khar Road Station so if you’re planning to drive, God be with you. If you're walking in, the white-washed European façade welcomes you like you’ve entered a Pinterest board.
Pro Tip: If it’s a weekend, reservation is non-negotiable. This place fills up quicker than your WhatsApp family group on Diwali morning.

🍽️ What We Tried

1. Truffle Pizza

Creamy, crispy, indulgent basically everything you want from a pizza that wears truffle like a crown. If royalty had a flavor, this would be it.

2. Truffle Fries

Yes, more truffle. Don’t judge.
We inhaled these while waiting for our drinks. Perfectly crisp, generously tossed, and honestly… finished too soon.

3. Donna’s Signature Drinks

We tried a bunch of their mocktails (let’s just say the menu has more Donnas than a Bollywood family tree). Refreshing, quirky, and worth experimenting with.

4. Hungover Noodles (⭐ The Star of the Night)

Do not go by the looks.
These noodles pack flavour, comfort, and a bit of drama. Easily the winner and something you’ll crave again.

🛎️ Service

Shockingly fast.
I mean the food arrived before our mocktails.
They take the “fast” in fast-casual seriously.

🌿 Ambience & Vibe

Donna Deli scores big here white décor, leafy corners, soft lighting, aesthetic touches everywhere. Instagram would approve. So would your date.

🚗 Parking & Access

Located right on SV Road

Walking distance from Khar station (recommended)

If coming by car, patience is a mandatory side dish

The ambience, the vibe and the entire setting made our big day truly magical.\\n\\nA special shoutout to Ajinkya, Chetan & Utkarsha ma\u2019am for ensuring that every little detail was taken care of with so much dedication and warmth. The food was absolutely top-notch, and every guest couldn\u2019t stop praising it!\\n\\nA big thanks to Chetan for making sure the decor matched my exact aesthetic & everything looked even better than I imagined.\\n\\nThe name Exotica truly speaks for itself \u2014 and this place will always hold a very special place in our hearts. \u2665\ufe0f\\n\\nHighly recommended for anyone looking for a serene, beautiful and perfectly managed wedding venue!\",\"guided_block\":{\"GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT\":5}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Nitin Pawar\",\"time_line\":\"a month ago\",\"review\":\"Had a fantastic experience! We visited around 7 PM, and since there were only a few people, we enjoyed our meal in peace and had great conversations till 11 PM.\\n\\nThe prices are reasonable, and it doesn\u2019t even feel like you\u2019re in Thane. Perfect for families or special occasions. Couples will also love it \u2013 ideal for anniversaries, birthdays, or any celebration. reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservations not required, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION]}, time_line=a month ago, review=Fabulous. Food and ambience far outperforms most jazz bars I've seen in Singapore. Very nicely curated menu, great blues music on weekends. Will definitely go back for RD Burman night on Thursday. The kathal parotha was 10/10. Highly recommend. I'm surprised this place is in Grant Road and even more surprised it wasn't packed on a weekend., name_person=Zubin Madon}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=4 months ago, review=A refreshing take on the Japanese listening bar concept.. This space exudes a suave, retro charm that instantly whisks you away to the golden age of vinyl from the '80s and '90s.
We indulged in:

Soul Revival 🍸
Flower Child 🍹
Butter Garlic Lobster 🦞
Korean Fried Chicken Tteokbokki 🍗
Prawns Sambal Coconut Rice 🍚
Chilli Crisp Fettuccine 🌶️
Pistachio Tiramisu 🍰
Each dish was a thoughtful composition of flavours, beautifully presented and well-balanced.
The cocktails? Artfully crafted and truly intriguing.
Add to that the impeccable service and ambient tunes that cradle every conversation amd you've got a spot that doesn't just serve food, it curates an experience.

Absolutely worth the visit., name_person=Tanvi Yamsanwar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Indoor_dining_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_INDOOR_DINING_AREA, Bar_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_BAR_AREA], GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservations not required, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=4 months ago, review=Great cocktails, well priced menu.
Food was a hit and miss. Few items to try - Buttermilk Fried Chicken, Kerala mutton and parotha, miso glazed chicken and blueberry empanadas.

Cocktails must try - Rock and Roll and Espresso Martini, name_person=K N}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=4 months ago, review=Such a cool and refreshing concept — Baroke is a vinyl-only listening bar inspired by Japanese culture, and it’s genuinely unlike anything else in the city. The vibe is mellow, the interiors are aesthetic, and the music? Pure magic. There’s something about hearing records play in the background while you sip a cocktail that just hits different.

Tried a bunch of things from the menu and loved almost everything:
🥑 Avocado, charred corn, pepitas, masa chips – Surprisingly tasty but not the best dish
🍟 Truffle fries with parmesan, chives & aioli – addictive. You have to order these!
🍝 Fettuccini aglio e olio – kind of a miss
🍛 Penang tofu with bok choy and jasmine rice – a warm, wholesome dish with great balance
🍹 Soul Revival cocktail – refreshing and perfectly balanced.
🌸 Flower Child cocktail – like a breakfast cocktail! Slightly citrusy, a little sweet, and soooo good.

Perfect for good conversations, good food, and even better music, name_person=Siya Gandhi}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,200–1,400, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=4 months ago, review=Amazing cocktail bar in Mumbai just loved the cocktail here and food was good too must try truffle fries and all the non-veg items here!

reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=11 months ago, review=I recently dined at Dreamland Cuisine Hotel and had a mixed experience. The food was undoubtedly tasty and flavorful, with a good variety of dishes on the menu. However, there were a couple of things that brought the experience down. The waiting time was longer than expected, and when the food finally arrived, it wasn’t served hot. While the flavors were great, eating lukewarm food took away some of the enjoyment for me.

That being said, considering the price, I’d say the value for money is excellent. The portions were decent, and the taste of the food certainly made it worth what I paid. It’s clear that the hotel focuses on providing flavorful dishes without making them overly expensive, which is a big plus. However, the service and the timing need improvement to match the quality of the food.

In India, levying a "restaurant packaging charge" or similar charges for food containers is considered an unfair trade practice and is deemed illegal.

Unfair Trade Practice:
The Consumer Court has ruled that charging for packaging on online food orders is an unfair trade practice, as it is considered false and misleading.
Price Inclusion:
The price of a product/service should include all operating expenses and profit margins, including packaging, according to the Consumer Affairs Department.

From the moment you step in, the aroma of traditional spices and freshly cooked dishes sets the tone for a wholesome dining experience. The menu is extensive and features a wide variety of options, including some excellent fasting food items that are hard to find in most other places.

The flavors are spot on—each dish feels homely yet thoughtfully prepared, offering a genuine slice of Maharashtrian culture on the plate. The puran poli, misal, and thalis are standout choices, while the sabudana khichdi and fasting specials add a nice touch for those observing fasts.

That said, the pricing leans toward the higher side. While the quality justifies the cost to some extent, if you’re visiting with a large group, be prepared for the bill to add up quickly. The portion sizes are fair, generally serving two people comfortably, but for bigger gatherings you will need to order more dishes to keep everyone satisfied.

The ambiance is simple yet welcoming, making it suitable for both family outings and casual get-togethers. From the moment we walked in, the warm and welcoming atmosphere set the tone for a great evening. The service was friendly, attentive, and made us feel right at home.

We ordered the Prawns Thali, Surmai Thali, and Crabs Lollipop — and every single dish was a hit! The flavors were rich, authentic, and beautifully balanced. But I have to say, the Prawns Thali truly stole the show — perfectly cooked, bursting with coastal flavor, and generously portioned. It’s easily one of the best seafood thalis I’ve ever had!

Highly recommend this place to anyone who loves delicious seafood, great service, and a cozy, vibrant vibe. Can’t wait to come back!, name_person=Adarsh Nandiwadekar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,000–1,200, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=4 months ago, review=It’s disappointing to see all the fried fish being prepared in the same burnt oil. This not only affects the taste but also ruins the texture and overall experience.

Recommendation: Please consider adding more manpower in the kitchen area to ensure better quality control during peak hours. While the Stuffed Pomfret and Stuffed Bombil were delicious in terms of flavor, the burnt rawa from oil completely overshadowed their potential.

For the Thali options — especially Surmai and Pomfret — it would be great to offer guests a choice between Masala Tawa Fry and Regular Oil Fry, so they can pick based on their preferences.

Please keep in mind that guests often spend thousands of rupees expecting a high-quality experience. One poorly executed dish can ruin their entire impression — especially for women, who tend to be more sensitive to taste, name_person=Saisha Patil}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=11 months ago, review=Hotel Nav Gomantak in Dombivili is a fantastic spot for seafood lovers, offering the best food, ambience, and hospitality. We tried their Prawns Masala Thali, Prawns Green Masala Thali, Pomfret Rava Fry Thali, Stuffed Pomfret, Surmai Fry, Tisrya Masala, and Green Mutton Thali, and every dish was outstanding in taste, quality, and portion size—truly worth every penny. The staff is cooperative and humble, adding to the delightful dining experience. The sol kadhi was refreshing, and they also serve wine, beer, and hard drinks, with a rooftop seating area enhancing the ambience. Conveniently located opposite Roshan Automobiles, this place is a must-visit and is sure to become a favorite spot in Dombivili., name_person=Bhakti Sabnis}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=11 months ago, review=If you're a seafood lover, Nav Gomantak in Dombivli is the place to be! Known for its authentic coastal flavors, this restaurant truly delivers an unforgettable culinary experience with its traditional Gomantak cuisine.

I started with the **Surmai tawa Fry Thali**, and it was a delight. The surmai was perfectly fried—crispy on the outside and tender on the inside, served with flavorful sol kadi, chapati, rice, and a tangy fish curry that hit all the right notes. The highlight of the meal was the **Bharlela Pomfret**, a whole pomfret stuffed with a deliciously spiced masala that was bursting with flavor.

For vegetarians, the **Veg Birda Bhaji Thali** is a must-try. The bhaji, made with sprouted beans, was rich, wholesome, and paired beautifully with soft chapatis and flavorful accompaniments.

The **Chicken Koliwada** was another standout—crispy, spicy, and perfectly cooked, making it a perfect snack or starter. To end the meal, I indulged in their desserts, which were simple yet satisfying, giving a perfect sweet touch to the spicy coastal flavors.

The ambiance is simple and homely, while the staff is friendly and attentive. If you’re in Dombivli and craving authentic coastal cuisine, Nav Gomantak is a must-visit. It’s a heaven for seafood enthusiasts and a treat for anyone looking to savor the essence of Gomantak flavors., name_person=Prachi vaidya}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=The ambiance is simple and homely, while the staff is friendly and attentive.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Prices are reasonable, considering the quality and quantity offered.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=The Bharlela Pomfret portion was extremely small considering the price.}"]

All the starters we ordered came with the same chutney until we specifically asked for something different. The butter garlic prawns were a disaster — frozen, served in a white pasta-style sauce with random vegetables, and completely inedible.

The washrooms were leaking during rains, which made them unhygienic and unpleasant to use. Even the ice we were served had a plastic thread inside and was dirty.

Alcohol options listed on the menu were out of stock, and cocktails weren’t available before 4 pm as no bartenders were present.

The ambiance was no better, with the DJ playing old, depressing songs on loop, completely killing the mood. Food overall was below average, with the only dish worth mentioning being the manchurian — probably the safest option.

We tried quite a few starters and drinks and the bill was around 8k for 3 people which is quite expensive.

They do have AC. The staircase is pretty steep to reach up. 4 tables at top floor. Overall not so ambient place.\\nThe timings of restaurant are not updated, we went at 2:30 noon and they were closed. Opened again at 7:30 pm evening. And this was on Sunday.\\n\\nFOOD:\\nOrdered hoksa(pork) curry with bamboo shoots and sticky rice, and Iromba, all recommended by waiter, while pork sausage and pork momos as our choice. Iromba is white chutney which he said is less spicy but also turned out to be very spicy. Pork curry has less gravy and filled most with a lot of oil, we mixed oil and some bamboo shoots with rice to eat as there was negligible gravy. But the Pork was well cooked and tasty\\uD83D\\uDC4D.\\nBamboo shoot has a very strong unique smell, many people might not like it, so order accordingly.\\nPork sausage taste was very unique, don't know to describe it as good or bad, that was spicy too, had many green chilli pieces inside it.\\nIromba was a like a spicy gravy chutney, can't mix with rice, didn't know what to do with it.\\nPork momos were the tastiest, one of\\nthe best we've eaten\\uD83D\\uDE0A, especially with that unique chutney, seemed like blend of pan fried onions and some other things, had dark brown colour. Complimented the pork meat so well.\\n\\nOverall, all dishes are on the spicier side and very unique of making it.\\n\\nSERVICE: Language barrier is evident. They don't seem to understand much English, but they're very friendly. Mr Yogesh, the manager, offered me personalised services; the other servers were equally helpful and absolutely friendly. The main Course was average - I tasted some French Beans and Chicken. In the deserts, the Wasabi Cheese Case was fantastic.

Visit 3 [ Extract ]

Some of the dishes I had:

Duck [ in the main course, whose precise name I don't remember ] - Unusually strong on species, very much unauthentic, some pieces covered almost entirely in bones, and tough to chew upon. Call it a botched preparation and mood spoiler! It's not very often that I leave behind any dish. The grievance was resolved amicably.

Pork baos - You don't get these in many same-level restaurants, so a must-try. On a sweeter side and minced well and soft to consume. Arrived in the estimated time.

The quantity for all the dishes was above average and probably the largest I have seen at same-level restaurants.

Visit 4

A supreme and unforgettable experience

Some of the dishes I tried:

Traditional Pecking Duck - A conventional Chinese dish which is usually served with pancakes, troika of sauces, some veggies, and ofcourse, the duck cuts. Kudos to the chef, on my request, for serving me ready-made and saving me all the effort. The dish was slightly on the sweeter side, and the rolls had a good proportion of duck. Much laborious to scoff if all constituents are served separately.

Steamed Chilean Sea Bass - Prepared in soya ginger sauce, lightly spicy, mildly  pungent, and medium in size. Delicious, healthy and a must try. Maybe a few veggies at the side should be considered.

Light Breeze mocktail - Indeed light, mild soda, simple as it gets. Kinda like virgin mojito less Sprite/7UP and less coriander.

Grapefruit-based mocktail - the best of the three, authentic grapefruit flavour with medium bitterness, preserving the original taste, no soda.

Watermelon-based mocktail - another light one with no soda, pure watermelon [ and no syrup ] and a dash of cucumber.

I would like to thank Mr Jojo for preparing tailor-made off-the-menu [ above-mentioned ] mocktails, all of which were served inside 10 mins. And not to forget, offering me cashews which were off-the-menu. At the end, he also made an exception and served me the desserts from another restaurant because I didn't want any from the menu courtesy to various reasons.

This is amongst the handful of restaurants in this range where almost all the dishes are available in small and large sizes, and this allows one to make better selections on quantity. To add to that, even small sizes are equivalent to medium in many dishes. If I were to offer a suggestion, it would be to rejig the currently-mediocre dessert menu and add dishes like creme brulee, coconut pudding and cheese cake. On the embellishments front, I would say the restaurant is slightly behind despite the fact that they have a Chinese dragon hanging from the top & and a plush red carpet albeit the latter doesn't cover the flooring of the whole restaurant . The pots don't look very attractive and there is room for vibrance - a few paintings & art pieces could help. The restaurant size is quite big with 10+ tables.

It was also nice to meet & have an interlocution with Mr Srinivas, and I would like to thank him for personally overseeing the dinner and ensuring that it was a memorable experience. It is recherche of someone of his level to come down and discuss the ways certain past flaws were handled and briefing on the feedback taken to minimise the bitter moments; I really appreciate this commitment.

I am looking forward to visiting here again soon., name_person=Pratik Gadgil}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=Edited 7 years ago, review=Ambience and Food merit a Four

You will be happily surprised., name_person=Ninad Jadhav}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=2 years ago, review=Nestled conveniently near Gold Gym in Mulund, Fit Taste is a newly opened haven for health-conscious foodies seeking a scrumptious and nourishing meal. From the moment I stepped into the cafe, I was impressed by the clean and inviting ambiance, setting the tone for a promising dining experience.

One of the first things that caught my eye was their impressive array of fresh juices. I opted for the "Coconutty Muskmelon" juice, and it was a delightful thirst-quencher. The combination of muskmelon with the subtle hint of coconut was a refreshing treat, making it an ideal choice for a hot summer day.

As a fan of protein-packed meals, I decided to try their "Superman" sandwich, and it did not disappoint. This filling sandwich featured a generous serving of a 2-egg omelet, along with tender chicken and a medley of fresh veggies. The combination of flavors and textures worked harmoniously, creating a wholesome and satisfying sandwich that kept me energized throughout the day.

Next up, I couldn't resist trying their "Tandoori Tikka" wrap, which came wrapped in a vibrant beetroot multigrain roti. The succulent chicken, crisp iceberg lettuce, nutrient-rich spinach, and the tangy onion, all wrapped up in the colorful roti, made for a delightful and flavorful wrap. It was a great choice for those looking for a healthy yet flavorful option.

One of the highlights of my meal was the "Thai Green Curry Pot Rice." The aromatic coconut curry infused with exotic veggies provided a burst of flavors that transported me to the streets of Thailand. The perfectly cooked rice and the medley of vegetables added a delightful touch to this wholesome dish. It was evident that Fit Taste takes care in crafting dishes that are both delicious and nutritious.

To satisfy my sweet tooth guilt-free, I opted for their "Healthy Smoothie Bowl." It was a feast for the eyes and the taste buds, as it was adorned with a colorful assortment of seasonal fruits like dragon fruit, papaya, and banana, all topped with creamy yogurt. Each spoonful was a burst of fruity goodness, and the combination of textures made it an enjoyable and wholesome dessert.

Overall, Fit Taste exceeded my expectations as a healthy cafe in Mulund. With a wide variety of delicious and nutritious options, the cafe is a great choice for health-conscious individuals and food enthusiasts alike. The fresh juices, protein-packed sandwiches, flavorful wraps, aromatic pot rice, and satisfying smoothie bowl all showcase the cafe's dedication to offering wholesome and tasty meals. The staff was friendly and attentive, adding to the overall positive experience. Whether you're a fitness enthusiast or simply looking for a guilt-free yet delectable meal, Fit Taste is undoubtedly a must-visit destination. I'm already looking forward to my next visit to explore more of their tantalizing offerings.

reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Delivery}, time_line=5 months ago, review=I used to order food from them quite regularly, especially when they first started. As an NRI, I travel frequently, and during my monthly subscription, I had clearly informed them that I might occasionally skip meals due to my travel schedule.
Since April, I haven’t been well and have had to skip meals more often. Instead of checking in or showing any understanding, I was repeatedly threatened—not just once, but multiple times. This became overwhelming, so I finally told them to cancel my subscription and stop delivering meals. I even mentioned they could treat the remaining balance as a charitable contribution from my side, and I would simply leave my feedback honestly.
Their response?
"It was only one meal left; we can't build an empire with such a huge amount."
This is exactly the problem. When they were just starting out, they were respectful and customer-focused. I initially ordered through Aniket, and the experience was great. But now that the business has grown, it seems one customer or one meal no longer matters.

Conclusion: A definite must-avoid., name_person=Amit}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹200–400, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=10-30 min}, time_line=a month ago, review=This review is based on a deeply concerning first visit to this restaurant. When the Maharaja tray arrived, it was full of normal snacks you can find easily on the streets like jalebi and samosas. I’ve been visiting Café Bae in Lower Parel for the past three years, and over time, I’ve tried pretty much everything on their menu. It’s been a go-to spot for casual meals, and while the food has always been decent, there have been a few changes worth noting.

Earlier, Café Bae felt like a solid pocket-friendly option – good food at fair prices. But lately, the prices have gone up, and with that, the overall value feels a bit off. The space is quite compact and tends to get crowded, which can make the experience feel a bit cramped, especially during peak hours.

That said, some of their food items still stand out. The pizzas are consistently good, and the nachos are definitely worth ordering. The fries are alright – nothing extraordinary, but they do the job. As for the drinks, they’re okay – decent enough, but not a highlight.

Overall, Café Bae still holds some charm, especially if you're familiar with it like I am. reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Brunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Strawberry_Freakshake], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=A nice little café located near TalaoPali in Thane, definitely a convenient hanging-out place. The cafe offers a good variety of fast food including nachos, pizza, burgers, pasta, different pastries, mocktails and milkshakes.

We tried the pasta and strawberry shake, and both were quite good. However, the nachos with cheese were disappointing and didn’t taste as expected.

The seating space is limited—only three regular tables and three high tables (which accommodate only two people per high table), so it may not be the best choice for larger groups.

The ambience wasn’t great either since it was not smelling very pleasant inside, which affected the overall experience. There is no dedicated parking (only on-road), and there are no washrooms available, which can be inconvenient.

Overall, a decent café for a quick visit, but there are a few things that could definitely be improved., name_person=Rahul Bhoir}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Other, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹200–400, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[2_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO, Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=10-30 min}, time_line=3 months ago, review=​I recently visited Kill No Kalorie Cafe in Thane and had an amazing experience. The Starberry menu was a particular highlight—the flavors were both creative and delicious.​The cafe's decor is clean, minimal, and charming, creating a cozy and relaxing atmosphere. The prices were quite reasonable, which is a definite bonus.​While the cafe offers a good selection of desserts and a few small bites, the main attraction is their strawberry-based items like the Strawberry cream and Strawberry Nutella cheesecake.​The cafe does have some downsides, though.
